findings.title: Accepting a passing final result can erase an already reported failure
findings.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. The coordinator never compares an event with the corresponding final result, so a worker can report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing. The final passing result is returned to the pipeline even though the coordinator has already received evidence of failure.
findings.suggestion: Track check results by lease attempt and reject a final result that contradicts the events for that attempt, preserving failures as infrastructure failures or explicitly represented retries.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid event for the requested test with ok=false, then posts a valid GateRun for the same SHA and command with ok=true and exitCode=0. The job completes successfully.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:125 validates events with `validCheck(request, event.data.result, event.data.phase)`; lines 130–136 independently validate the final run and call `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)`. src/db/workers.ts:290–291 writes `state='done',result=?` without comparing stored events. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns that final result.
verification.trigger: A leased worker submits a valid failing check event, then a matching, schema-valid passing final result. The job completes as passing despite its recorded failure.

findings.title: Restart discards in-flight LAN retry jobs
findings.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves its durable LAN job running, but resume treats its handle as stale, cancels it, and enqueues another execution. This repeats work that had already been leased or completed and defeats durable reattachment for these gate executions.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach the matching durable handle on resume, including timeout and targeted retry purposes.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down after a worker completes a regression-retry job but before the pipeline checkpoints its result. On restart, the completed handle is discarded and the retry is run again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29–39 only reuses a handle when stage/round/purpose match and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; otherwise it calls `cancelGateExecution(pending.handle, ...)` and clears the checkpoint. Restart enters the gates stage through `runGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", ...)` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1215), so a persisted regression-retry handle is discarded. The restart test explicitly asserts `expect(fresh.attaches).not.toContainEqual(handle)` and `expect(fresh.starts).toHaveLength(2)` for regression retries (test/gate-executor.test.ts:899–900).
verification.trigger: Coordinator restarts with a completed LAN regression-retry job whose result has not been checkpointed by the pipeline. Resume discards its persisted handle and starts initial gates again; if the regression recurs, it also repeats the retry instead of consuming the completed result.

findings.title: Local fallback can populate a LAN baseline cache entry
findings.detail: After infrastructure failures, the LAN executor returns a locally executed GateRun as an ordinary LAN result. The baseline cache key was selected as LAN before execution, so a passing fallback baseline is cached under that key. A later run can reuse it while its actual gates execute on a worker with a different environment, even though the cache distinguishes executors to avoid comparing results from different environments.
findings.suggestion: Do not cache a baseline produced by local fallback under the LAN executor key; propagate the actual execution environment or mark fallback results non-cacheable.
findings.failure_scenario: No worker is available for a baseline, so local fallback passes and is cached as LAN. A worker later becomes available and runs the change, while the pipeline reuses the local baseline as its worker baseline.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:77-89 runs `local.start(request, controller.signal)`, then `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true)` and `return workers.sanitize(run)`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:550-551 selects the cache key from configuration: `executor: cfg.gateExecutor === "lan" && cfg.workers.repos.includes(ctx.repo.slug) ? "lan" : "local"`. At src/pipeline/engine.ts:574-577, `const fresh = await runBaseline()` is cached with `if (cacheableBaseline(fresh, gates)) store.putBaselineCache(key, fresh, ctx.run.id)`. src/gates/cache.ts:157-172 checks passing results and check identities, without checking execution provenance.
verification.trigger: With LAN configured for an opted-in repository, unavailable workers cause the baseline to fall back locally. A passing local result is stored under the LAN cache key. When a worker becomes available, change gates can run remotely while using that local baseline, including on subsequent cache hits, potentially misclassifying environment-dependent failures as regressions.

findings.title: Bound retries for job requests and propagate permanent failures
findings.detail: The shared request loop discards every transport error and retries indefinitely, including certificate fingerprint mismatches and other permanent errors. It also retries every server error without a deadline. Heartbeats can continue renewing a job while a bundle, event, result, or failure request is stuck in this loop, so the coordinator never expires the lease or falls back locally. Permanent connection errors also leave the worker silently retrying instead of reporting the cause.
findings.suggestion: Classify retryable transport and server errors, propagate permanent errors, and bound job-request retries so a failed job stops renewing its lease or reports its infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator accepts heartbeats but repeatedly returns HTTP 500 for a job's result endpoint. The worker retries that result forever while heartbeats renew the lease, leaving the gate run pending indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:139 uses `for (;;)`, and lines 150–158 return on 200, throw on statuses below 500, otherwise sleep and retry with only the delay capped: `delay = Math.min(delay * 2, 10_000)`. Line 233 awaits this loop for `/result`; `job.reported = false` occurs only afterward in `finally` (line 239). Heartbeats independently send `jobs: heldJobs()` (line 173). src/db/workers.ts:187–189 renews each held lease with `this.now() + this.times.lease`, so it never expires while these heartbeats succeed.
verification.trigger: Repeated HTTP 500 responses from the result endpoint while heartbeats continue succeeding cause unlimited result retries and lease renewals, keeping the gate pending without retrying another worker or falling back locally. This is an unusual trigger: ordinary listener exceptions are converted to HTTP 400 (src/server/workers.ts:138–139).

findings.title: Reject a final result that contradicts streamed check failures
findings.detail: Check events are validated and stored independently of the final GateRun. The final result is checked only against the requested names and commands, so a worker can first report a failing check and then submit a passing result for the same check. The coordinator accepts the pass even though it has already recorded evidence of a failure.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the final result with the events from the current lease and reject contradictory outcomes as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid check event with `ok: false`, then posts a GateRun containing the same check with `ok: true` and exit code 0. Both requests are accepted and the gate completes as passing.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:135–136: `if (action === "events" && event.success) workers.event(id, event.data); else if (result.success) workers.complete(id, result.data.run);`. src/workers/validation.ts:25–49 validates only the request and final run, with no comparison against streamed failures.
verification.trigger: A valid `ok:false` event followed by a valid final check with `ok:true` and `exitCode:0` is accepted; the final passing result determines the gate outcome.

findings.detail: The end-to-end test registers the credential in the same process that runs both the worker and coordinator, then checks only the stored coordinator result and events. Coordinator-side redaction can therefore make the test pass even if the worker sends the credential unredacted. That leaves the requested boundary check untested.
findings.suggestion: Capture the worker's outgoing event and result payloads before they reach the coordinator, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator, and assert that the credential is absent.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction regresses and a gate prints a worker-only credential. The credential crosses the network, but the current test still passes because the coordinator shares the credential registry and redacts it before storage.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers the secret with `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`; its `loop` helper directly calls `runWorker(...)` in the same process (test/workers.test.ts:459). Assertions inspect only coordinator results: `expect(jobs[0]?.result).not.toContain(secret)` and `expect(jobs[0]?.events).not.toContain(secret)` (test/workers.test.ts:681–682). findings.title: Publish worker check events before validating the final result
findings.detail: Individual check events are stored and forwarded to the run as gate results after only their name, command, and shape are checked. The worker has not yet supplied a checked SHA or a complete GateRun. If its eventual result has the wrong SHA, omits a check, or never arrives, those earlier events remain visible as pass or fail evidence even though the attempt is classified as an infrastructure failure.
findings.suggestion: Keep worker check events provisional until the final SHA and GateRun have been validated, or clearly mark and exclude them from authoritative gate evidence until validation succeeds.
findings.failure_scenario: A leased worker posts a passing event for a requested check, then posts a result with a different SHA. The result is rejected and retried, but the earlier passing event has already been persisted in the run's gate events.

"pass" : ...}`` and `data: r`. A later SHA mismatch only calls `workers.fail` (src/server/workers.ts:128–133).

findings.title: A failed streamed check can be replaced by a passing final result
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure failures must “never turn a failing check into a pass” and that the result is untrusted. Streamed check events are stored independently, but the final GateRun is validated only against the requested names and commands; it is never compared with the events already accepted for that lease. A worker can therefore report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing, and the coordinator accepts the passing GateRun as the authoritative outcome.

candidates.title: Accepting a passing final result can erase an already reported failure
candidates.detail: Check events and the final GateRun are validated independently. The coordinator never compares an event with the corresponding final result, so a worker can report a failed check and then submit the same check as passing. The final passing result is returned to the pipeline even though the coordinator has already received evidence of failure.
candidates.suggestion: Track check results by lease attempt and reject a final result that contradicts the events for that attempt, preserving failures as infrastructure failures or explicitly represented retries.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid event for the requested test with ok=false, then posts a valid GateRun for the same SHA and command with ok=true and exitCode=0. The job completes successfully.

candidates.title: Restart discards in-flight LAN retry jobs
candidates.detail: Only baseline, initial, and rebase handles are eligible for reattachment. A shutdown during a timeout rerun or a baseline or regression retry leaves its durable LAN job running, but resume treats its handle as stale, cancels it, and enqueues another execution. This repeats work that had already been leased or completed and defeats durable reattachment for these gate executions.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to reattach the matching durable handle on resume, including timeout and targeted retry purposes.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator shuts down after a worker completes a regression-retry job but before the pipeline checkpoints its result. On restart, the completed handle is discarded and the retry is run again.

candidates.title: Local fallback can populate a LAN baseline cache entry
candidates.detail: After infrastructure failures, the LAN executor returns a locally executed GateRun as an ordinary LAN result. The baseline cache key was selected as LAN before execution, so a passing fallback baseline is cached under that key. A later run can reuse it while its actual gates execute on a worker with a different environment, even though the cache distinguishes executors to avoid comparing results from different environments.
candidates.suggestion: Do not cache a baseline produced by local fallback under the LAN executor key; propagate the actual execution environment or mark fallback results non-cacheable.
candidates.failure_scenario: No worker is available for a baseline, so local fallback passes and is cached as LAN. A worker later becomes available and runs the change, while the pipeline reuses the local baseline as its worker baseline.

candidates.title: Bound retries for job requests and propagate permanent failures
candidates.detail: The shared request loop discards every transport error and retries indefinitely, including certificate fingerprint mismatches and other permanent errors. It also retries every server error without a deadline. Heartbeats can continue renewing a job while a bundle, event, result, or failure request is stuck in this loop, so the coordinator never expires the lease or falls back locally. Permanent connection errors also leave the worker silently retrying instead of reporting the cause.
candidates.suggestion: Classify retryable transport and server errors, propagate permanent errors, and bound job-request retries so a failed job stops renewing its lease or reports its infrastructure failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator accepts heartbeats but repeatedly returns HTTP 500 for a job's result endpoint. The worker retries that result forever while heartbeats renew the lease, leaving the gate run pending indefinitely.

candidates.title: Reject a final result that contradicts streamed check failures
candidates.detail: Check events are validated and stored independently of the final GateRun. The final result is checked only against the requested names and commands, so a worker can first report a failing check and then submit a passing result for the same check. The coordinator accepts the pass even though it has already recorded evidence of a failure.
candidates.suggestion: Reconcile the final result with the events from the current lease and reject contradictory outcomes as an infrastructure failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid check event with `ok: false`, then posts a GateRun containing the same check with `ok: true` and exit code 0. Both requests are accepted and the gate completes as passing.

candidates.title: Worker-side credential redaction is not independently tested
candidates.detail: The end-to-end test registers the credential in the same process that runs both the worker and coordinator, then checks only the stored coordinator result and events. Coordinator-side redaction can therefore make the test pass even if the worker sends the credential unredacted. That leaves the requested boundary check untested.
candidates.suggestion: Capture the worker's outgoing event and result payloads before they reach the coordinator, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator, and assert that the credential is absent.
candidates.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction regresses and a gate prints a worker-only credential. The credential crosses the network, but the current test still passes because the coordinator shares the credential registry and redacts it before storage.

candidates.title: Publish worker check events before validating the final result
candidates.detail: Individual check events are stored and forwarded to the run as gate results after only their name, command, and shape are checked. The worker has not yet supplied a checked SHA or a complete GateRun. If its eventual result has the wrong SHA, omits a check, or never arrives, those earlier events remain visible as pass or fail evidence even though the attempt is classified as an infrastructure failure.
candidates.suggestion: Keep worker check events provisional until the final SHA and GateRun have been validated, or clearly mark and exclude them from authoritative gate evidence until validation succeeds.
candidates.failure_scenario: A leased worker posts a passing event for a requested check, then posts a result with a different SHA. The result is rejected and retried, but the earlier passing event has already been persisted in the run's gate events.

findings.title: Home-relative paths and file URLs bypass sanitization
findings.detail:
The sanitizer compares link destinations only against literal filesystem roots. A home-relative link such as the one in the request is left broken, and a file URL containing the absolute worktree path is published unchanged, including the owner's username. The direct check below returned both inputs unchanged.

Command: bun -e 'let s=await Bun.file("src/gates/publication.ts").text(); let f=new Function(s.slice(s.indexOf("export function sanitizePublication"),s.indexOf("/** Check both")).replace("export function","function").replace(/: string( \| undefined)?/g,"")+";return sanitizePublication")(); for(let x of ["[file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)"]) console.log(f(x,"/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run","/Users/alice/.limitless"))'

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before each merge command
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can repeat that sequence on retry. A reclaim during the lookup is invisible until the heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and check it immediately before each merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest, its PR view request is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the old heartbeat fires. The old worker then runs gh pr merge.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:701 calls `await mergePullRequest(...)`; ownership is checked afterward at :715 with `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`. Inside src/git/repos.ts:1447, the helper awaits `sh(view, { cwd, signal })`, then at :1462 executes `sh(cmd, { cwd, signal, stdin: body })` without checking claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the helper's PR view is pending, then return a valid OPEN response before the heartbeat aborts. The displaced worker issues gh pr merge.

findings.title: Guard the actual push after its preparation awaits
findings.detail: The transaction verifies the claim before calling pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, transport setup, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before issuing git push. A reclaim during any of those awaits leaves the old worker able to push before its heartbeat notices.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership inside the push helper immediately before issuing the push, using a guard supplied by the land worker.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker passes the ownership transaction, pauses in the helper's ls-remote call, and another owner reclaims the entry. When ls-remote returns, the stale worker pushes its merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517 checks ownership in `this.owned(...)`, then :522 calls `await pushExistingBranch(...)`. Inside src/git/repos.ts:1313, that helper awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", ...])`, awaits an ancestry check at :1315, and pushes at :1321 with `await remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])`; neither continuation checks claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim after the outer ownership check while the helper's ls-remote is pending. If the remote head and ancestry checks pass before the next heartbeat, the displaced worker pushes.

findings.title: Do not discard a checkout reused by the new claimant
findings.detail: All attempts for an entry use the same land-<id> worktree path. After a reclaim, the old worker reaches this unconditional cleanup even when a new worker has already recreated and started using that path. It can remove the new worker's worktree and cause its checks or merge to fail.
findings.suggestion: Isolate checkout paths by claim or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a newer claimant's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI response is deferred, the entry is reclaimed and the new worker creates its checkout, then the old response returns. The old worker detects the lost claim but its finally block removes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:549 calls `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` after the CI observation, but :396-397 unconditionally runs `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. The shared path is `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)` at :812. `discard` removes the worktree at :839 and calls `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` at :842.
verification.trigger: A new claimant using the same work directory recreates the entry's checkout while the old CI response is pending. Returning that response throws on lost ownership, and the old worker's finally removes the new claimant's checkout.

findings.title: CI inspection can still write after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: Passing the ownership check as `current` does not guard every write inside `ciDecision`. Its inspection awaits the default branch and check-run responses, then emits feed events and updates the `ci.main` setting before checking `current()`. A claim reclaimed during either read can therefore leave the old worker writing outcomes after ownership was lost.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership after the awaited reads and in the same transaction as each resulting durable write, including CI inspection writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker starts CI inspection, another owner reclaims the entry while the default-branch check response is pending, and the old response contains a failing check. The old worker emits a `ci.main_red` event and updates the CI setting after reclaim.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:625 passes the ownership-aware `current` callback to `ciDecision`. However, src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:239 awaits `checks(mainSha)`, :258-264 emits `"ci.main_red"`, and :267 executes `store.setSetting(`ci.main:${pr.repo}`, Object.fromEntries(state))` before :268 checks `if (!current()) return true`. The emit helper writes through `store.saveGithubPr(...)` at :201.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while default-branch checks are pending, then return a failing check whose name matches the PR's failing check. The displaced worker persists a ci.main_red event and updates the CI setting before noticing lost ownership.

findings.title: A displaced worker can delete the new owner's worktree
findings.detail: The unconditional cleanup runs after `LandClaimLost` as well as normal completion. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` worktree path, so once a new owner has checked it out, the old worker's `discard` removes that checkout and its Git worktree registration. The new owner can then fail or operate on a deleted checkout.
findings.suggestion: Give each attempt an isolated worktree path or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a successor's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is waiting for CI, its claim is reclaimed, and the new worker creates the same checkout. When the old CI response arrives, its ownership check throws and its `finally` deletes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:812 derives the checkout solely from the entry ID: `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`. After the ownership check at :549 throws, :396-397 still executes `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`; :842 unconditionally runs `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: The new owner recreates the same checkout before the displaced worker's deferred CI response returns. The displaced worker detects claim loss but deletes the new owner's worktree during cleanup. This duplicates C3.

findings.title: A worker that lost its claim can remove the new worker's checkout
findings.detail: The unconditional cleanup runs when an ownership check throws after a reclaim. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` worktree path, so the old worker can remove the checkout after the new owner has created it. This violates the requirement that a worker that lost its claim write nothing and can cause the new attempt's Git commands or gates to fail.
findings.suggestion: Make checkout ownership and cleanup safe across overlapping attempts, and prevent an old attempt from removing a newer attempt's worktree.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker waits for CI, another queue reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, then the CI response returns. The old worker detects the lost claim but its finally block removes the shared checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:811-812: `return join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`);` shares the path across owners. src/land/queue.ts:396-397 unconditionally executes `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. src/land/queue.ts:838-842 calls `removeWorktree(...)` and `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` without checking ownership.
verification.trigger: Another worker reclaims the entry and recreates its checkout while the old worker awaits CI. The old worker detects claim loss, unwinds through finally, and deletes the new worker's checkout.

findings.title: Reclaim tests do not exercise a running replacement worker
findings.detail: The new tests replace the claim owner in the store but never start a replacement worker or inspect its checkout. Their snapshots therefore pass even though the old worker's unconditional cleanup can delete a replacement worker's files.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that pauses the old worker, reclaims the entry with a second queue, waits until the second attempt has created its checkout, then releases the old worker and verifies that the checkout and second attempt remain intact.
findings.failure_scenario: A reclaim occurs while the old worker awaits CI or a merge result, and the new worker begins using the same worktree before the old worker exits.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:1642 reclaims with `store.claimLandEntry(SLUG, 30_000, "new-owner", clock.now() + 31_000)`, then lines 1651–1654 only `release.resolve()`, wait, stop the original queue, and compare snapshots. The CI test follows the same pattern at lines 1702–1713. Neither starts a replacement worker or checks its worktree. findings.title: Merge helper can issue a merge after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: The ownership check happens before calling mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing `gh pr merge`, and can await further reconciliation and retry operations. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the old signal active until its next heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue the merge. The check after the helper returns is too late.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the merge helper and check it immediately before every merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest, its `gh pr view` response is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the response is released before the old heartbeat. The old worker then runs `gh pr merge`.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:701-715 awaits `mergePullRequest(...)` before `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`. Inside that helper, src/git/repos.ts:1447 awaits `sh(view, { cwd, signal })`, then src/git/repos.ts:1461-1462 constructs `gh pr merge` and executes `sh(cmd, { cwd, signal, stdin: body })` without a claim check.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the helper's PR view is pending, then return a valid OPEN response before the heartbeat aborts the old signal. The old worker issues the merge command despite losing ownership.

findings.title: Push helper can push after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: The transactional ownership check precedes pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before starting the push. A reclaim during any of those operations is not detected before the push is issued.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership immediately before the actual push inside the helper, including after its asynchronous preparation.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker passes the ownership check and blocks in pushExistingBranch's remote lookup. Another owner reclaims the entry and the lookup returns before the next heartbeat; the old worker pushes its merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517-522 checks ownership in `this.owned(...)` before calling `pushExistingBranch(...)`. Inside the helper, src/git/repos.ts:1313 awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", url, ref], ...)`, src/git/repos.ts:1315 awaits the ancestry check, and src/git/repos.ts:1321 executes `remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])` without checking claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry during the helper's remote lookup. If the remote still matches the approved SHA and the old signal remains un-aborted, the old worker proceeds to push its merge commit.

findings.title: A worker that loses its claim still removes the shared checkout
findings.detail: The `finally` block always discards the worktree, including when an ownership check throws LandClaimLost. Both attempts use the same `land-<entry id>` path, so the old worker can remove the checkout a new owner has already created, disrupting its checks or merge.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts distinct worktree paths or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a checkout owned by a newer claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A new owner reclaims an entry and recreates its worktree while the old worker awaits CI. The CI response returns, the old worker detects the lost claim, and its finally block removes the new owner's worktree.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:811-812 derives the checkout path solely from `land-${entry.id}`. src/land/queue.ts:396-397 always runs `await this.discard(repo, cwd)` in finally; src/land/queue.ts:842 then executes `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` without an ownership guard.
verification.trigger: A new owner reclaims the entry and recreates the shared worktree during the old worker's CI wait. When the old worker detects claim loss, its cleanup removes the new owner's worktree.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before issuing the command
findings.detail: The request says a worker that lost its claim “issues no merge or push.” The ownership check before calling `mergePullRequest` does not cover its internal awaits: the helper awaits a fresh `gh pr view` and can also await reconciliation and retry operations before issuing `gh pr merge`. A reclaim during one of those awaits leaves the signal live until the next heartbeat, so the stale worker can still merge.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and check it immediately before each merge attempt, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause the helper's PR view response, reclaim the entry with a new owner, then release the response before the old heartbeat fires; the old worker issues `gh pr merge`.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:1447 reads the PR through `await sh(view, { cwd, signal })`; src/git/repos.ts:1461-1462 subsequently issues `gh pr merge` through `sh(cmd, ...)` without revalidating ownership. The queue's next ownership check is after the entire helper returns, at src/land/queue.ts:715: `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`.
verification.trigger: Pause the helper's PR view, reclaim the entry, and release a valid OPEN response before the old heartbeat fires. The helper issues the merge command using the still-active signal.

findings.title: Recheck ownership immediately before the actual push
findings.detail: The request says a worker that lost its claim “issues no merge or push.” `pushExistingBranch` performs several asynchronous operations after the guarded checkpoint, including resolving the commit, reading the remote and checking ancestry, before starting the push. A reclaim during those operations is not detected until the heartbeat.
findings.suggestion: Provide an ownership guard to the push helper and invoke it immediately before starting the push.
findings.failure_scenario: Pause the helper's remote lookup after `pushedSha` is recorded, reclaim the entry, and release the lookup before the next heartbeat; the old worker pushes the merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517-522 checks ownership with `this.owned(...)`, records `pushedSha`, then calls `await pushExistingBranch(...)`. Inside that helper, src/git/repos.ts:1313 awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", ...])`, then :1315 awaits `worktreeGit(...)`, and :1321 issues `await remoteSh([...BRANCH_PUSH, ...])` without another ownership check.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the push helper's remote lookup is deferred, then release it before the old worker's heartbeat. With the approved remote head unchanged, the old worker still pushes the merge commit.

findings.title: Guard CI inspection writes after its internal awaits
findings.detail: The request says “a worker that lost the claim writes nothing.” Although `current` now checks ownership, `ciDecision` delegates to `inspectCi`, which writes default-branch CI feed and settings after awaited reads and only checks `current()` afterward. Its rerun response handler also writes the failure outcome after an awaited request without rechecking ownership.
findings.suggestion: Recheck ownership at each CI inspection write boundary, in the same transaction as the write.
findings.failure_scenario: Reclaim the entry while default-branch check data or a rerun response is deferred; releasing the response lets the old worker update CI settings, feed, or failure records.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:584-587 passes an ownership-aware `current` callback into `ciDecision`. However, src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:239 awaits `checks(mainSha)`, :258-264 can `emit("ci.main_red", ...)`, and :267 calls `store.setSetting(...)` before :268 checks `current()`. Similarly, :223 awaits the rerun response and :233 calls `store.finishCiFailure(f, "rerunning")` without checking ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim during deferred default-branch check data or a rerun response. Releasing the response before the heartbeat lets the old worker write CI settings/feed records or update the failure outcome despite losing its claim.

findings.title: Do not discard a reclaimed worker's shared worktree
findings.detail: Every attempt for an entry uses the same `land-<id>` path. The unconditional cleanup runs even when an ownership check detects a reclaim, so the old worker can remove the newer worker's checkout while it is running. This also conflicts with the request's requirement that a worker that lost its claim writes nothing.
findings.suggestion: Give attempts separate worktree paths or otherwise ensure stale cleanup cannot remove a newer attempt's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker is awaiting CI, another process reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, and the old CI response arrives; its `finally` removes the new worker's worktree.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:393 awaits `this.awaitCi(...)`, but :396-397 unconditionally executes `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. Both owners use the same path: :811-812 returns `join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`. Cleanup at :839 removes the worktree and :842 executes `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })` without validating ownership.
verification.trigger: Another process reclaims the entry and recreates its checkout while the old worker awaits CI. When the old response arrives, ownership validation throws, but its finally block removes the new worker's shared checkout, disrupting its work.

findings.title: A rejected rerun can remain pending forever after claim loss
findings.detail: The rerun claim is persisted before the POST. If ownership changes while the POST is in flight, the new guard discards its response, including an explicit rejection. The replacement worker sees the existing rerun_requested record, but only resolves it when GitHub reports a later workflow attempt. A rejected request creates no later attempt, so CI remains pending and the land cannot complete or report the failure.
findings.suggestion: Provide a recovery path for an unconfirmed rerun request that lets the current owner resolve a rejected or absent rerun without allowing the old owner to write after losing its claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker claims a CI rerun, GitHub returns HTTP 422 after another worker reclaims the land entry, and the old worker discards the response. The replacement repeatedly observes the original workflow attempt and retains rerun_requested indefinitely.

A runless entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release resumes active entries by looking up that ID and blocks the entry when no run exists. If a deployment rolls back while such a land is queued or in progress, the old daemon changes it to blocked instead of preserving it for the newer release to resume.
candidates.suggestion: Make runless entries invisible to the previous release's active queue, or otherwise provide a rollback-compatible persistence and resume mechanism.
candidates.failure_scenario: A runless land is waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release; on startup the old queue claims it and blocks it with "run  is gone".

candidates.detail: The empty-string sentinel satisfies the old schema, but the previous release treats it as a real run ID. After a rollback, its queue resumes the active entry, cannot find run "", and marks the land blocked. Upgrading again cannot resume it automatically, including when the new release had already pushed its checked base merge.
candidates.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or otherwise ensure the previous release does not claim and permanently block them.
candidates.failure_scenario: Queue an unowned PR, restart into the previous release while it is checking or waiting for CI, and the old worker blocks it with a missing-run error.

candidates.title: Unowned lands have no UI representation
candidates.detail: The new entry is persisted and exposed by the land API, but the UI has no queue view or other rendering path for entries without a run. Its existing land presentation is attached to run details, so a user cannot see the unowned entry in the UI as requested.
candidates.suggestion: Expose unowned land entries in a UI queue or equivalent view, including their state and PR link.
candidates.failure_scenario: Queue a manual PR and open the UI: there is no run detail page for it and no UI list showing its land state.

candidates.title: Blocked unowned lands disappear from the digest
candidates.detail: The new feed item has a null run ID, but the digest discards every item without a run ID before computing actionable blocked lands. Consequently a blocked manual land is omitted from the owner’s actionable feed digest.
candidates.suggestion: Resolve unowned land feed items by their PR URL or land entry ID and evaluate their current state without requiring a run.
candidates.failure_scenario: A manual PR fails its confined checks and produces a `land.blocked` feed item; the digest removes that item because `runId` is null.

candidates.title: Active unowned lands cannot survive a rollback
candidates.detail: The empty-string sentinel satisfies the old schema, but the previous release treats it as a run ID. After a rollback, its land worker calls getRun("") and blocks the entry with “run  is gone”, including an entry that had already pushed its checked merge commit and was waiting for CI.
candidates.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation or a release transition that prevents the older worker from claiming unowned entries, while preserving their progress for the newer release.
candidates.failure_scenario: Queue an unowned PR, restart into the previous release while it is checking or waiting for CI, and the old worker marks it blocked instead of resuming it.

candidates.title: Unowned PR numbers are rejected
candidates.detail: The new path only accepts a full GitHub URL, although the requested command accepts a PR target and the existing CLI supports bare PR numbers. If a factory run exists for the same number on another repository, the initial run lookup can instead select that unrelated PR.
candidates.suggestion: Resolve numeric PR targets against an unambiguous configured repository, or require an explicit repository-qualified target when resolution is ambiguous.
candidates.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 77 --sha <head>` for a hand-opened PR returns “run not found” when no factory run has that number.

candidates.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
candidates.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This new early return prevents those PRs from entering the queue, even when the factory has permission to update their head branch.
candidates.suggestion: Support the fork head repository and its push permissions while retaining the approved-head lease and exact-head merge checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with “cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed”.

candidates.title: Unowned land entries are not shown in the UI
candidates.detail: The change creates API and feed records but adds no UI consumer for land entries. The existing UI is run-oriented, so a land with no run has no page or list through which its status and failure reason can be seen.

candidates.failure_scenario: Queue a hand-opened PR and open the UI: its queued, blocked, or landed entry is not visible there.

candidates.title: Unowned PR numbers are rejected

candidates.title: Fork PRs targeting a configured repository are refused

candidates.title: Runless land test does not exercise actual confinement

findings.title: Scratch warnings do not reach an implementer when the round otherwise passes
findings.detail: The warning is appended only when a later implementation stage already runs. An advisory audit finding does not itself produce feedback or schedule another round, so an approved round can proceed to publication with the scratch file still in its commit history. This leaves the reported failure mode unresolved when no gate, review or verification failure happens to trigger another round.
findings.suggestion: Arrange for an implementer to receive actionable scratch feedback before publication while keeping the finding advisory, and cover the otherwise-passing round.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer adds .tmp-gate/report.xml containing output that exceeds the publication decoding limit; gates and review pass. No second implementation runs, and publication is refused.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/prompts.ts:216–217: `const block = findings.filter((f) => f.severity === "block"); if (!block.length) return "";`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1127–1133 appends warnings only when constructing an implementation prompt. src/pipeline/engine.ts:962–965: `const passed = await oneRound(ctx, round, holdout); if (passed) { await ctx.setPhase("deliver"); return; }`. test/pipeline-audit.test.ts:96 explicitly expects `prompts.length` to be `1` for the approving case.
verification.trigger: The first implementation adds .tmp-gate/report.xml exceeding the publication decoding limit, while gates, review and verification pass. The warning never reaches another implementation prompt; the run advances to delivery and publication is refused.

findings.title: Large text logs with terminal control characters are excluded from the size warning
findings.detail: Sizes are recorded only for blobs that pass reviewableText, which rejects control bytes such as ESC. Git can treat a UTF-8 log containing ANSI color sequences as text, but the size rule sees no size for it and emits no warning. Generated command and gate output commonly contains such sequences.
findings.suggestion: Measure new files classified as text independently of the stricter reviewable-content predicate.
findings.failure_scenario: A round adds a 200 KiB UTF-8 build log containing ANSI color escape sequences outside a root hidden directory. It receives no large-text-addition warning.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:560 rejects control bytes: `if (byte === 0x7f || (byte < 0x20 && ![9, 10, 12, 13].includes(byte))) return false;`. src/git/repos.ts:1150 excludes those files from sizes: `.filter((path) => contents.get(afterText.blobs.get(path) ?? "")?.reviewable)`. src/gates/audit.ts:297 uses `(diff.headTextSizes?.[f.path] ?? 0) > 102_400`. ANSI ESC (0x1b) therefore prevents the warning.
verification.trigger: Add a 200 KiB UTF-8 log containing ANSI color escapes outside a root hidden directory. Its size is omitted, so no large-text-addition warning appears.

findings.title: Advisory can reach publication without an implementer seeing it
findings.detail: The warning is added only when an implementation round is already starting. If gates and review pass, the pipeline does not start another round, so the implementer never receives the feedback and the scratch file can remain in the published history. The new approve-path test explicitly expects only one implementation round.
findings.suggestion: Arrange for the implementer to receive and act on the advisory before publication while retaining the requested non-blocking treatment for intentional additions.
findings.failure_scenario: The first round adds .tmp-gate/report.xml and all gates and review pass. The run proceeds without a second implementer prompt containing the warning.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1127–1133 reads `ctx.state.lastAudit` into implementation feedback, but src/pipeline/engine.ts:962–965 immediately sets phase to `"deliver"` when the round passes. The delivery guard at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1974–1975 rejects only missing audit evidence or `lastAudit.some((f) => f.severity === "block")`. test/pipeline-audit.test.ts:95–96 expects success with only one implementation prompt in the approving case.
verification.trigger: A first round adds .tmp-gate/report.xml and all checks approve. The advisory remains nonblocking, and the run reaches publication without any implementer prompt containing it, missing the requested opportunity to remove scratch output.

findings.title: Large text logs with terminal escapes are excluded from the warning
findings.detail: The size map excludes anything that fails reviewableText, which rejects escape bytes even in otherwise valid UTF-8 text. Terminal-colored gate output commonly contains ANSI escapes, so a large new log outside a hidden root directory receives no large-text warning.
findings.suggestion: Use a text classification appropriate for the size advisory that includes UTF-8 logs with terminal control sequences.
findings.failure_scenario: A new 150 KiB gate-output.txt contains normal UTF-8 output and ANSI color escapes. It is omitted from headTextSizes and the large-text-addition rule does not fire.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:560 returns false for ANSI ESC bytes through `byte < 0x20 && ![9, 10, 12, 13].includes(byte)`. src/git/repos.ts:1150 filters headTextSizes to `.reviewable` files. src/gates/audit.ts:297 treats an omitted size as zero: `(diff.headTextSizes?.[f.path] ?? 0) > 102_400`.
verification.trigger: Add a 150 KiB gate-output.txt containing ANSI color escapes. It is omitted from headTextSizes and receives no large-text-addition warning.

findings.title: Cover large-text warnings in the next-round prompt
findings.detail: The pipeline test exercises next-round feedback only for the root-hidden-addition rule. The large-text-addition rule is tested in audit isolation and with real Git, but no test verifies that its warning reaches a subsequent implementer prompt.
findings.suggestion: Add a pipeline case that commits a new text file over the threshold, triggers a second round, and asserts that the next implementer prompt names the file and large-text advisory.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression removes large-text-addition from the pipeline feedback filter while leaving audit detection intact; the existing tests still pass, but the implementer does not see that advisory in the next round.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-audit.test.ts:89 creates only a small report: `".tmp-gate/report.xml": "<report/>\n"`; line 106 asserts only `expect(prompts[1]).toContain("Advisory [root-hidden-addition] .tmp-gate/report.xml")`. test/gates.test.ts:1079–1083 checks `large-text-addition` through `auditDiff` alone. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1131 independently filters feedback using `["root-hidden-addition", "large-text-addition"].includes(f.rule)`. No test asserts large-text-addition reaches the next-round prompt.
verification.trigger: Removing large-text-addition from the pipeline feedback filter leaves existing assertions satisfied while newly added large text files lose their next-round advisory.

findings.title: Encoded credentials in filenames escape diagnostic redaction
findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic passes a Git-controlled path to `redactCredentials` without decoding it first. That function replaces only literal credential variants, so a percent-encoded credential remains recoverable in the error message. The new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts` has the same issue: `redactGateOutput` also performs literal credential redaction. These diagnostics can be stored as events or sent back to an implementer.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress the filename when its decoded forms contain a credential. Apply the same handling to both audit findings and publication diagnostics.
findings.failure_scenario: A new file is named with a percent-encoded registered credential and contains text that triggers the publication decoding refusal. The resulting error includes the encoded credential in the path; an audit warning for a file under a root hidden directory can expose it in the same way.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:758 constructs diagnostic paths with `privacy.redactPrivate(redactCredentials(path), entries)`. src/util/proc.ts:839 registers only literal and JSON-escaped credential variants; src/util/proc.ts:847 replaces literal matches using `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`. src/gates/audit.ts:425 similarly uses `redactGateOutput(f.file)`. A probe with a synthetic percent-encoded registered credential confirmed that both diagnostic redaction and the audit finding preserve the encoded credential.
verification.trigger: Use a percent-encoded registered credential in a filename, with no corresponding private-strings entry. A decoding refusal naming that path, or a root-hidden-addition warning, exposes the recoverable credential.

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, ...)`; src/pipeline/review.ts:541 sums `costUsd` across results. src/db/stats.ts:265-275 uses one fallback record with `provider: details.provider`, `modelId: String(t.model_id)` and the entire trial cost. src/db/stats.ts:180 sets `invocations: rows.length`.
verification.trigger: A review eval invokes primary provider A and verifier B. Their combined spend becomes one record attributed to A, undercounting calls and omitting B's workload.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 accumulates `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens`; src/evals/runner.ts:1173-1175 stores round evidence for implementation cases. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 sets both cache metrics to `null` whenever `rounds?.length` is truthy.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read and 20 cache-write tokens and one round record. Its model and provider statistics report null for both cache metrics.

findings.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
findings.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1115 invokes the selected verifier through `sendTo`; src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns the combined panel result. src/db/stats.ts:269-275 attributes the trial fallback's combined tokens and costs to `details.provider` and `t.model_id`. Round records are only appended under `if ("hidden" in item)` at src/evals/runner.ts:1173-1175.
verification.trigger: A review panel uses reviewer A and verifier B. Although this panel is represented by the trial fallback rather than a stored implementation round, the claimed outcome occurs: combined cost and tokens are attributed to A and B receives no workload. This overlaps C1.

findings.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 preserves trial-wide cache totals. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 nevertheless assigns `null` to both splits for round-backed trials; src/db/stats.ts:291 consequently sets `inputTokens` to null. src/db/stats.ts:174-176 propagates any null metric into the aggregate sum.
verification.trigger: A completed multi-round implementation eval has stored cache-read and cache-write totals. Its eval aggregate reports both cache metrics and uncached input tokens as null despite those available totals.

findings.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
findings.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
findings.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:931 persists `store.recordEvalTrial({ ...trial, status: "running" });` before invoking the harness. src/db/stats.ts:258 excludes only `(t.status === "skipped" || details.preparationFailed)`; the fallback at :271 uses `status: details.invocationStatus ?? String(t.status)`. At :179–180, `invocations: rows.length` counts this record while only `status === "ok"` counts as successful.
verification.trigger: A first trial is persisted as running before its first harness call, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. A statistics read counts one unsuccessful eval invocation. The running checkpoint actually follows workspace preparation.

findings.title: Eval successful share can reflect grading failures instead of provider results
findings.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and aggregate the provider invocation status separately from the grading outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully, but its grading process times out. The eval provider statistics count the invocation as unsuccessful.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1209–1212 sets `roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason` when the provider returned `"ok"` but grading errored or timed out. src/db/stats.ts:265–266 selects stored `rounds`, :287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 counts only `r.status === "ok"` as successful.
verification.trigger: An implementation invocation succeeds but grading times out. Its stored round status becomes timeout, lowering the provider's successful share despite a successful provider result.

findings.title: Eval aggregation tests do not exercise runner-produced round evidence
findings.detail: The eval test constructs round records directly and assumes their status and duration describe provider calls. The runner can modify round status after grading and records duration through grading, so this fixture does not catch the resulting misclassification of provider success.
findings.suggestion: Add a test using runner-produced eval evidence where the provider succeeds but grading fails or times out, and assert the provider success share.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression or existing defect that treats a grading timeout as a failed provider invocation passes the manually seeded round test.

verification.evidence: test/provider-workload.test.ts:469 manually sets `status: "ok"`; :482 seeds another round with `status: "timeout"`; :523 expects `successfulShare: 0`. Runner-produced evidence differs: src/evals/runner.ts:1209–1212 overwrites a successful invocation's round status when grading fails: `result.status === "ok" && (grade?.implement?.reason === "error" || grade?.implement?.reason === "timeout")` then `roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason`. src/db/stats.ts:287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 counts success only with `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: A provider invocation succeeds, but hidden-test or gate grading times out. The runner stores round status `timeout`, so aggregation counts the provider invocation as unsuccessful. The manually seeded aggregation test passes without exercising this distinction.

findings.title: Multi-call eval trials are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: The request asks for workload “per provider and model” with “eval invocations shown separately.” A review eval can invoke multiple panel members or samples, including providers other than the trial target. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial, but this code attributes the entire combined record to the trial target and counts it once. candidates.title: Multi-provider eval costs are attributed to the trial's provider
candidates.detail: Review panels can invoke finders and verifiers on different providers and models. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial totals, but this code assigns all of those totals to details.provider and the trial model. The resulting provider and model workload numbers can therefore charge one provider for work performed by another.
candidates.suggestion: Attribute calls from the stored per-call evidence where available; represent an unresolvable split as unknown rather than assigning the combined amount to one provider.
candidates.failure_scenario: A review trial targets provider A but also invokes a verifier on provider B. The full combined token count and cost appear under A, while B receives none.

candidates.title: Implementation evals discard stored cache token totals
candidates.detail: Every eval with round evidence forces both cache measurements to null, even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Consequently, a normal implementation eval makes the corresponding provider totals unknown, including when the trial has only one round and its cache split is unambiguous.
candidates.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals where they can be attributed, and preserve them at an appropriate aggregate level when individual rounds cannot be split.
candidates.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial records 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its eval statistics report both as null, as do the containing provider totals.

candidates.title: Recorded rounds are reported as individual invocations
candidates.detail: A round can contain multiple provider calls: the runner retries a failed resumed session within the same round and sums both calls into one round record. Counting each round as one invocation understates workload and its success share reflects only the final result, despite the API naming the field invocations.
candidates.suggestion: Count individual calls when evidence supports it, or expose round counts separately without presenting them as invocation counts or invocation success rates.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementation round makes a failed resumed call followed by a successful fresh call. Statistics report one successful invocation instead of two calls with one failure.

candidates.title: Combined eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
candidates.detail: For evals without recorded implementation rounds, the fallback treats the entire trial as one provider invocation. Review panels and sampled reviews can make multiple calls, including calls to other providers, while the runner combines their usage into the trial totals. This assigns all of that usage to the trial target and omits the other providers' calls, so provider and model workload numbers are wrong.
candidates.suggestion: Aggregate per-call evidence where it is persisted, and make unavailable attribution explicit rather than assigning combined usage to a single provider.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls a finder on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The report counts one invocation and assigns both calls' tokens and cost to A; B receives no workload.

candidates.title: Missing durations are reported as zero total wall time
candidates.detail: The duration aggregation silently drops unknown durations and returns the sum of the remaining values. If every duration is unknown, it reports zero milliseconds; if only some are unknown, it presents a partial sum as the total. This differs from the explicit unknown handling used for the other metrics.
candidates.suggestion: Represent total wall time as unknown when any included duration is unavailable, or expose the measured count and clearly identify the sum as partial.
candidates.failure_scenario: A provider has one unfinished invocation with no finished timestamp. Its historical totals report one invocation and zero milliseconds of total wall time even though its duration is unknown.

candidates.title: Eval rounds discard available cache-token totals
candidates.detail: Every eval trial with recorded rounds reports unknown input and cache-token totals, even when the trial stores those measurements and has only one round. The test explicitly expects null for round cache splits, so it would not catch this loss of available workload data.
candidates.suggestion: Attribute the stored cache totals when they can be assigned unambiguously, and test a single-round trial with nonzero stored cache-read and cache-write tokens.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval trial has one recorded round and details.cacheReadTokens = 20 and details.cacheWriteTokens = 5; its provider and model report null for both cached-token metrics and uncached input.

candidates.title: Round aggregation test asserts missing cache measurements
candidates.detail: The seeded round test expects null cache metrics but does not seed the trial-level cache measurements recorded by the eval runner. Consequently it passes while the aggregation discards cache data for an unambiguous single-round trial.
candidates.suggestion: Add a single-round eval with nonzero trial-level cache totals and assert the provider/model input, cache-read and cache-write aggregates.
candidates.failure_scenario: A single-round eval stores cache usage in its trial details, but the statistics endpoint returns null for those metrics and the existing test still passes.

candidates.title: Cross-origin requests can trigger unbounded historical aggregation
candidates.detail: The existing GET endpoint now synchronously loads and aggregates every stored invocation and eval trial when no cutoff is supplied. GET requests are exempt from the origin check, so a web page can repeatedly trigger this work against a local daemon even though it cannot read the response. As history grows, each request consumes increasing CPU and memory and blocks the daemon's event loop.
candidates.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user with a large invocation history visits a page that repeatedly loads the local /api/stats/providers URL; each request runs the full historical aggregation and can make the daemon unresponsive.

candidates.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls provider A once and provider B twice. The result reports one invocation and all combined spend under A, with no workload for B.

findings.title: An unrelated later test failure can replace the first error as the signature
findings.detail: When the first failure-shaped line starts with `error:`, the search advances to any later `(fail)` line unless another failure-shaped or passing line intervenes. It does not establish that the lines belong to the same Bun assertion block. For a build error followed by a test failure, the signature identifies the later test and the excerpt combines evidence from two failures, potentially discarding the later test's diagnostic. A targeted check, `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; console.log(ciSignature("test", "error: first failure\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) second failure", "fallback"));'`, returned `line: "(fail) second failure"` with an excerpt starting `error: first failure`.
findings.suggestion: Associate an assertion with a following Bun test name only when the intervening output establishes that they belong to the same failure; otherwise retain the first error line.
findings.failure_scenario: A job logs `error: first failure`, then ordinary output, then `(fail) second failure`; the record and fix-round signature identify the second failure while the excerpt begins with the first.

findings.title: A dirty worktree can bypass detection of a cancelled worker's push
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs the local session even if the cancelled worker already pushed an unreported commit. The request requires that case to end NeedsHuman.

The job is omitted from heartbeat renewals, expires, and its eventual result is rejected.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:565-567: the fence executes `for (const job of agentJobs.values()) job.controller.abort();`. src/workers/client.ts:501-504: `heldJobs()` filters with `job.reported && !job.controller.signal.aborted`; heartbeats send `jobs: heldJobs()` (line 546). findings.title: Cancel the open job when reconciliation fails
findings.detail: If `publication.resume()` throws, the error is propagated while the queued or leased job remains open. The engine can then finish the run as NeedsHuman, but the worker continues executing and can push after the coordinator has stopped waiting for its report. Orphan cleanup only runs at factory start or stop, so it does not close this window.
findings.suggestion: After re-reading the job and handling a concurrently completed result, conditionally cancel an open job before propagating the reconciliation error.
findings.failure_scenario: A resumed leased job is still running when the coordinator's git status command or private-strings read fails. Reconciliation throws, the run ends NeedsHuman, and the worker later pushes a commit.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:75-79 awaits `publication.resume(request)`, then on exception only checks abortion and a completed job before `throw error`; it never cancels the open job. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1143-1144 converts reconciliation errors into `NeedsHumanError`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:448-450 records the terminal status without cancelling worker jobs.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back after reconciliation
findings.detail: A failed resume check cancels the old job and goes straight to `prepare()`. If the worktree is dirty, or the remote lookup fails, `prepare()` returns null and the executor runs locally without checking whether the cancelled worker already pushed. The existing failed-job path checks the remote before local fallback; this new path bypasses that protection and can continue a run with an unaccepted worker commit on its branch.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an unreconciled job, verify the branch against the stored request before permitting a local fallback; treat an unavailable remote check as an unresolved failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes but its report has not been accepted. After restart, the coordinator worktree is dirty, so resume fails, the job is cancelled, prepare returns null, and a local session runs instead of stopping for the unreported push.
