findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: A land trigger is immediately evaluated against any saved poller snapshot, even if that snapshot predates the approved head. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when the saved head differs, and a later poll cannot reconsider it. The queue has already blocked the entry, so the requested conflict round never starts.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation before rejecting a land trigger for a stale head, or retain the trigger pending until a current observation can decide it.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A; a review round pushes head B and B is approved before the next poll. Landing B conflicts with the base, but the saved snapshot still says A, so the B trigger is permanently skipped as `PR head moved`.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());` uses the saved observation without refreshing it. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127: `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head ? "PR head moved"`; src/db/store.ts:1139: `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. Only pending triggers are processed (src/db/store.ts:1071).
verification.trigger: Saved head A differs from the land trigger's approved head B: the land trigger is permanently skipped. A subsequent poller event can independently recover the conflict, but the land trigger itself is lost.

findings.title: A conflict observed during another round is lost permanently
findings.detail: An active review or conflict round causes the trigger to be marked skipped. The poller emits `pr.conflicting` only on entry into the conflicting state, so if the active round fails or ends without changing the head, subsequent polls do not create another trigger. The unresolved conflict therefore never gets its own round.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while another round is active and reconsider it when that round terminates, subject to a fresh PR observation and the daily cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A review round is in flight when the poller first observes the PR as CONFLICTING. The trigger is skipped; the review round later fails without pushing, and every subsequent poll still sees CONFLICTING, so no conflict round starts.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:1130–1131 rejects any active round: `rounds.some((r) => !TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(r.status)) ? "round in flight"`; lines 1137–1140 permanently consume that trigger with `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`. Only pending triggers are retried (src/db/store.ts:1071: `WHERE state = 'pending'`). Subsequent unchanged observations emit no replacement: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 requires `next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING"` to emit `pr.conflicting`.
verification.trigger: An eligible factory PR first becomes CONFLICTING while a review round is active. Its conflict trigger is marked skipped. The review round then fails without pushing; continued CONFLICTING observations never generate another trigger, leaving the conflict unresolved unless a separate new trigger occurs.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land trigger
findings.detail: The land path uses any stored GitHub snapshot without refreshing it. `startConflictTrigger` marks the trigger skipped when that snapshot's head differs from the land entry's approved head, even if the snapshot is simply older than the approval. The trigger is then no longer pending, so this landing-queue trigger cannot recover on restart.
findings.suggestion: Refresh or otherwise establish the snapshot's freshness before permanently skipping a land trigger; retain it pending when the observation cannot establish the current head.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saved head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, and the land queue detects a conflict at B. Processing compares B with the saved A and skips the trigger instead of starting a round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 compares `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head` and selects `"PR head moved"`; src/db/store.ts:1139 persists `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: The PR advances from saved head A to approved head B before polling; landing detects a conflict at B, but processing rejects B against stale A and permanently consumes the land trigger.

findings.title: Retrying comment creation can post duplicate resolution comments
findings.detail: The `gh` wrapper retries transient failures around the entire comment command. If GitHub creates the comment but its response is lost, the retry creates another comment without checking the marker again. The preflight marker lookup only protects a later delivery attempt, not retries within this call.
findings.suggestion: Recheck for the marker after an uncertain comment outcome before issuing another creation request.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts `pr comment`, but the client receives a timeout or connection reset; the retry posts a second comment with the same conflict-round marker.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1921-1922 wraps each gh call in `withGitHubRetry(async () => (await runner(args, signal, stdin)) ?? "", { budget, signal })`; :1899 calls `await gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ctx.signal, text)`. src/git/repos.ts:91-97 retries `call` after transient failures. The marker lookup at engine.ts:1892-1894 occurs outside that retry.
verification.trigger: GitHub creates the comment but its acknowledgement times out; with retry budget remaining, the same comment command runs again without checking for the marker, creating a duplicate.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the PR delivery grant
findings.detail: The new auto-merge mutation occurs before `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush` verify that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected branch and repository, and matches the round's current grant. A stale or invalid round can therefore modify the PR even though delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head branch changes while a conflict round runs and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the changed branch.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 executes `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.autoMerge) await gh(["pr", "merge", prUrl, "--disable-auto"], ctx.signal)`. Only afterwards, :1869-1870 calls `stored()` and `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. src/core/delivery.ts:99 rejects `pr.headBranch !== branch`.
verification.trigger: The PR head branch changes while the round runs and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge before rejecting the changed branch, leaving an unrelated current head's landing configuration altered.

findings.title: Restart tests do not cover a stale saved observation
findings.detail: The restart tests use either no saved observation or one matching the trigger. They therefore pass while a saved observation for an older head causes a durable land trigger to be skipped permanently, and while an outdated open, non-draft observation can start an ineligible round.
findings.suggestion: Add restart and land-trigger cases with an older saved head and with a PR that became draft or closed after the saved observation. Assert that a current observation governs whether the trigger starts.
findings.failure_scenario: A pending trigger for head B is recovered while the database still contains an open CONFLICTING snapshot for head A; the existing tests never exercise this state.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:330-340 reopens the database and processes a trigger without saving an observation; the other startup test saves the same head for both trigger and snapshot (lines 517, 525: `headRefOid: await remoteHead()`). Neither covers mismatched heads. src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 uses any saved snapshot: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1126-1140 compares `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head`, assigns `"PR head moved"`, and permanently updates the trigger to `state = 'skipped'`.
verification.trigger: Recover a pending trigger for head B while the saved open CONFLICTING observation still names head A. Recovery skips the trigger instead of refreshing the observation; the restart tests do not exercise this state.

findings.title: The non-factory polling case bypasses the poller
findings.detail: The non-factory branch inserts a trigger and calls the store consumer directly, so it does not test whether polling a non-factory PR creates a round. A regression in tracking, event generation, or poller consumption for that case would still pass the test.
findings.suggestion: Exercise a tracked non-factory PR through the same fake GitHub poller path as the other eligibility cases and assert that no conflict round starts.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller erroneously starts a conflict round for a non-factory PR, but the test bypasses the poller and continues to pass.

verification.evidence: test/conflict-rounds.test.ts:365-372 explicitly branches on `eligibility === "non-factory"`, then calls `factory.store.recordConflictTrigger(...)` and `factory.store.startConflictTrigger(...)` directly. The actual `startGitHubPoller(factory.store, ...)` call appears only in the `else` branch at lines 372-373.
verification.trigger: A regression in the poller's handling of non-factory PRs would remain untested by this case because it directly exercises the store consumer and never starts the poller.

findings.title: Persisted conflict filenames bypass credential redaction
findings.detail: Conflict paths come from the repository under review and are copied into run state without credential redaction. The state is subsequently persisted by updateRun, so a registered credential embedded in a filename reaches storage even though the later PR comment redacts it.
findings.suggestion: Redact credential-bearing paths before storing them or sending them to any external sink, while retaining whatever representation is needed for local conflict resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed repository contains a conflicting filename that includes a registered token; the token is stored in conflictFiles in the run state.

verification.evidence: src/git/merge.ts:79-83 obtains conflicting filenames from `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U -z` and returns `paths`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:2245 assigns `ctx.state.conflictFiles = conflicts`; :2252 persists it through `ctx.store.updateRun(..., ctx.state)`. src/db/store.ts:1484-1486 serializes state using `values.push(json(state))` without credential redaction.
verification.trigger: A conflicting filename contains a registered credential. Its raw value enters conflictFiles and is persisted in state_json; redacting the later PR comment does not redact the stored state.

findings.title: Disable auto-merge only after validating the delivery grant and PR head
findings.detail: The new GitHub mutation runs before stored() and assertFactoryBranchPush validate that the grant still holds and that the PR is still open on the expected branch and head. A stale conflict round can therefore change auto-merge settings even when its delivery is subsequently refused.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and recheck state after the mutation before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: The PR head or round grant changes while a conflict round is running and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then rejects the stale round.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1866 disables auto-merge before :1869 invokes `stored()` and :1870 invokes `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. The stored-record guard at :1851-1857 throws when the round's record changes; the PR-head validation therefore also follows the mutation.
verification.trigger: The PR head or stored round grant changes during execution. An enabled auto-merge setting is disabled before delivery discovers the stale authority or head and refuses to push.

findings.title: An untrusted PR comment can suppress the resolution comment
findings.detail: The idempotency check accepts the marker in any PR comment without verifying its author. A PR participant can post the predictable marker before delivery, causing the factory to treat the required resolution summary as already published.
findings.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1891 defines `const marker = `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:${ctx.run.id} -->``; :1892-1894 reads comments as `{ body?: string }[]` and checks `!comments?.some((comment) => comment.body?.includes(marker))`. Posting the summary at :1899 depends solely on that body check, with no author validation.
verification.trigger: A PR participant posts a comment containing the round's marker before delivery. The merge is pushed, but the participant's comment satisfies the deduplication check and suppresses the factory's resolution summary.

findings.title: A stale saved snapshot can start a round for a draft PR
findings.detail: When a saved poller snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. A PR can become draft or close without changing its head, so the saved observation still passes the start checks. Delivery eventually checks draft status, but the forbidden round and its model work have already started.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR state before starting a pending conflict trigger, and leave the trigger pending if its current state cannot be verified.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller saves an open non-draft PR, the owner converts it to draft, and a land conflict trigger is processed before the next poll. A conflict round starts from the stale snapshot.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 uses the saved snapshot directly. src/db/store.ts:1099: `const seen = parse<typeof observation>(this.githubPrData(trigger.prUrl), observation);`; src/db/store.ts:1124 checks only `seen.isDraft`; src/db/store.ts:1144 then calls `this.insertRun(...)`. A later delivery guard exists at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1864: `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.isDraft) throw new Error("the PR is draft");`.
verification.trigger: A saved open, non-draft snapshot remains after the owner converts the PR to draft. A land trigger matching that saved head starts a conflict round before the next poll, wasting round work despite the draft exclusion. The later delivery guard prevents pushing while draft.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot permanently discards a land conflict trigger
findings.detail: The request says a landing queue conflict must start a conflict round and that the trigger must survive restart. Whenever any saved PR snapshot exists, this path uses it without refreshing it. If its head predates the approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". The later poll updates the snapshot, but the skipped trigger is never reconsidered, so the blocked entry has no round.
findings.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger, or leave a trigger pending when its saved observation is older than the trigger head and retry after a fresh observation.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, then the land queue detects a conflict at B. The saved A snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped permanently.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`; src/db/store.ts:1126–1127: `seen.headRefOid !== trigger.head ? "PR head moved"`; src/db/store.ts:1139: `UPDATE conflict_triggers SET state = 'skipped', reason = ? WHERE id = ?`.
verification.trigger: Landing approved head B conflicts while the saved snapshot still names A. Processing permanently skips the land trigger rather than refreshing the observation or retaining it pending. A separate later poller trigger may recover the conflict.

findings.title: Auto-merge is disabled before verifying the PR and delivery grant

A stale or invalid round can therefore disable auto-merge on a PR even though its push is subsequently refused. This is an unrequested side effect of a failed delivery.
findings.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the asynchronous call before pushing.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict round finishes after the PR head has moved and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then refuses the push because the head no longer matches the reviewed SHA.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1865-1870: `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.autoMerge) await gh(["pr", "merge", prUrl, "--disable-auto"], ctx.signal);` executes before `const { grant, run } = stored();` and `assertFactoryBranchPush(...)`. src/core/delivery.ts:77-80 subsequently throws `head moved` when the remote or PR SHA differs from the expected head.
verification.trigger: The PR head moves during the conflict round and auto-merge is enabled on that newer head. Delivery disables auto-merge before rejecting the stale resolution, leaving the newer PR's auto-merge unexpectedly disabled.

findings.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
findings.detail: The request requires "one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA, conflicting file names and resulting SHA, but does not describe how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reviewer cannot learn the resolution from the comment.
findings.suggestion: Include a concise, checked description of the actual resolution in the idempotent comment.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict in a shared function is resolved and pushed; the PR comment names that file but gives no account of which behavior was retained or changed.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1895-1899 constructs and posts only: `Merged base ${ctx.state.reviewBaseSha}. Conflicted files: ${JSON.stringify(ctx.state.conflictFiles ?? candidates.suggestion: Tie the checkpoint to a trusted factory-authored comment or another durable publication record rather than trusting arbitrary comment text.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR participant posts `<!-- limitless-conflict-round:<run-id> -->` before the round delivers; the merge is pushed but no factory resolution summary is posted.

candidates.title: A stale saved snapshot can start a round for a draft PR
candidates.detail: When a saved poller snapshot exists, trigger processing uses it without refreshing the PR. A PR can become draft or close without changing its head, so the saved observation still passes the start checks. Delivery eventually checks draft status, but the forbidden round and its model work have already started.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR state before starting a pending conflict trigger, and leave the trigger pending if its current state cannot be verified.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller saves an open non-draft PR, the owner converts it to draft, and a land conflict trigger is processed before the next poll. A conflict round starts from the stale snapshot.

candidates.title: A stale poller snapshot permanently discards a land conflict trigger
candidates.detail: The request says a landing queue conflict must start a conflict round and that the trigger must survive restart. Whenever any saved PR snapshot exists, this path uses it without refreshing it. If its head predates the approved head, startConflictTrigger marks the trigger skipped as "PR head moved". The later poll updates the snapshot, but the skipped trigger is never reconsidered, so the blocked entry has no round.
candidates.suggestion: Refresh the PR observation for a land trigger, or leave a trigger pending when its saved observation is older than the trigger head and retry after a fresh observation.
candidates.failure_scenario: The poller last observed head A, the PR advances to B and B is approved before the next poll, then the land queue detects a conflict at B. The saved A snapshot causes the only land trigger to be skipped permanently.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before verifying the PR and delivery grant
candidates.detail: The new conflict delivery path changes GitHub state before assertFactoryBranchPush validates that the PR is open, still has the authorized head and branch, and still belongs to the expected repository. A stale or invalid round can therefore disable auto-merge on a PR even though its push is subsequently refused. This is an unrequested side effect of a failed delivery.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the current grant and PR identity before disabling auto-merge, and revalidate after the asynchronous call before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict round finishes after the PR head has moved and auto-merge is enabled. Delivery disables auto-merge, then refuses the push because the head no longer matches the reviewed SHA.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires "one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA, conflicting file names and resulting SHA, but does not describe how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reviewer cannot learn the resolution from the comment.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, checked description of the actual resolution in the idempotent comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a shared function is resolved and pushed; the PR comment names that file but gives no account of which behavior was retained or changed.

findings.title: A stale poller snapshot can permanently discard a land conflict
findings.detail: The land-trigger consumer treats any saved GitHub snapshot as current and immediately marks a rejected trigger as skipped. A snapshot can predate the land queue's observation. The poller emits pr.conflicting only on entry into the conflicting state, so a later refresh need not generate another trigger.
findings.suggestion: Verify the land trigger against a fresh PR observation, or retain it pending until a sufficiently recent observation can decide eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: The saved snapshot says the PR is draft and CONFLICTING. The PR is made ready, then the land queue detects a conflict before the next poll. The trigger is skipped as draft; the next poll still sees CONFLICTING, emits no new conflict event, and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 uses the saved snapshot directly: `if (snapshot) store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now());`. src/db/store.ts:1124–1125 rejects `seen.isDraft` with `"PR is draft"`; :1139 permanently writes `state = 'skipped'`. src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 emits only when `next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING"`.
verification.trigger: The saved observation is draft and CONFLICTING. The PR becomes ready and landing detects a conflict before polling refreshes. The land trigger is permanently skipped using the stale draft flag; subsequent observations remaining CONFLICTING create no replacement trigger, leaving the conflict unresolved.

findings.title: A conflict observed while the owning run is finishing is lost
findings.detail: A poller trigger is permanently skipped unless the owning run has already reached succeeded or needs_human. A factory PR can be open and tracked while its owning run is still finishing delivery. Once skipped, the poller will not emit another pr.conflicting event while mergeability remains CONFLICTING.
findings.suggestion: Keep the trigger pending while the owning run is still delivering, and reconsider it when that run reaches a terminal state.
findings.failure_scenario: The poller observes a newly opened factory PR as CONFLICTING while its owner is still running. The trigger is marked skipped as not a factory PR; the owner subsequently succeeds, but subsequent polls see the same conflicting state and never start a round.

WHERE id = ?`. src/integrations/github-poller.ts:206 emits only on transition: `if (next.mergeable === "CONFLICTING" && prev?.mergeable !== "CONFLICTING") add("pr.conflicting");`. This window exists because src/pipeline/engine.ts:2172 persists `{ prUrl: url }` before awaiting `mergePullRequest(...)` at lines 2185–2192, while success is recorded only at line 213. src/db/store.ts:2546–2550 allows running owners' PRs to be polled.

Its trigger becomes skipped. Once the owner succeeds, unchanged CONFLICTING observations emit no replacement trigger, so no conflict round starts.

findings.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
findings.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
findings.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:24–31 explicitly leaves lookup failures pending: “// Lookup failures leave the durable trigger pending for startup to try again.” The catch assigns “lookupError ??= error;” and continues. src/land/queue.ts:266–268 catches and logs the processing failure without scheduling another attempt. Startup processing runs only behind “if (!this.conflictStartup)” (src/land/queue.ts:128–135). Poller recovery requires a PR observation: “if (trigger.prUrl === pr.url) store.startConflictTrigger(...)” (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373–374). Polling can be disabled via “githubPoll: github.poll !== false” (src/config.ts:369).
verification.trigger: With polling disabled and no saved PR snapshot, a land conflict records a pending trigger while gh pr view temporarily fails. After gh recovers, no retry is scheduled; absent another land failure or a daemon restart, the conflict round remains pending indefinitely.

findings.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
findings.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
findings.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
findings.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:21 calls `store.startConflictTrigger(trigger.id, snapshot, now())` whenever saved data exists. src/db/store.ts:1126–1127 rejects a saved head differing from the trigger with `"PR head moved"`; :1139 changes its state to `'skipped'`. src/db/store.ts:1071 subsequently selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`.
verification.trigger: The poller snapshot still names A when the landing queue records a conflict trigger for approved head B. Processing consumes the stale snapshot and permanently skips the land trigger, so that trigger never starts a conflict round. Recovery requires a separate later trigger.

findings.title: The non-factory poller case bypasses the poller
findings.detail: The non-factory branch manually inserts and consumes a trigger instead of running the poller. It verifies the store's refusal but cannot catch a regression in how polling handles a conflicting non-factory PR, despite the test name and the requested poller acceptance case.
findings.suggestion: Drive a non-factory conflicting PR through the fake GitHub poller and assert that it starts no round.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change makes the poller start rounds for non-factory observations while the direct store-level setup in this test still passes.

findings.title: Missing draft state is treated as permission to proceed
findings.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
findings.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review-round.ts:109–120 validates other head fields but never validates isDraft, then returns `isDraft: pr?.isDraft === true`. src/db/store.ts:1124–1125 rejects only truthy draft status: `: seen.isDraft ? "PR is draft"`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1864 likewise checks `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.isDraft) throw new Error("the PR is draft");`. However, review-round.ts:91 explicitly requests `isDraft`, as does the poller's GraphQL query (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:37); normal production omission is not established.
verification.trigger: An otherwise valid observation omitting isDraft admits a conflict round for a draft PR. If the delivery lookup also omits isDraft, it becomes false and the draft guard permits pushing. The code permits this outcome, but the required production lookup omissions are unproven.

duplicates.failure_scenario: The poller last saved head A, the PR advances to head B, and the land queue approves B and finds a conflict before the next poll. The trigger for B is permanently skipped against snapshot A.

candidates.title: Failed trigger lookups are not retried during normal operation
candidates.detail: A lookup error leaves the trigger pending, but this catch only logs the error. The queue processes pending triggers only at startup or after another land entry blocks. If polling is disabled or does not produce another observation for the PR, a transient `gh` failure leaves the conflict unresolved indefinitely until a restart or unrelated block.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange a bounded, durable retry for pending lookups during normal operation, without depending on another land failure or daemon restart.
candidates.failure_scenario: A land conflict is recorded while `gh pr view` temporarily fails and there is no saved PR snapshot. The command later recovers, but no further land conflict or PR poll occurs, so the pending trigger never starts.

candidates.title: A stale saved PR observation can start or discard a land trigger
candidates.detail: When any saved GitHub snapshot exists, the trigger consumer uses it without checking the current PR. A snapshot from before the land conflict can say the PR is draft or has a different head, causing the durable trigger to be permanently skipped; it can also say the PR is open and ready after it has become draft or closed, starting a round that should not start. Poller startup likewise consumes pending triggers from the saved snapshot before polling. The restart test supplies a current snapshot and therefore does not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Verify land and resumed triggers against a current PR observation before consuming them, and test stale snapshots against changed draft, state and head values.
candidates.failure_scenario: The last poll recorded head A; the PR advances to head B and the landing queue detects a conflict at B before the next poll. Processing compares B to the saved A and marks the only land trigger skipped, so no conflict round starts from that trigger.

candidates.title: The non-factory poller case bypasses the poller
candidates.detail: The non-factory branch manually inserts and consumes a trigger instead of running the poller. It verifies the store's refusal but cannot catch a regression in how polling handles a conflicting non-factory PR, despite the test name and the requested poller acceptance case.
candidates.suggestion: Drive a non-factory conflicting PR through the fake GitHub poller and assert that it starts no round.
candidates.failure_scenario: A future change makes the poller start rounds for non-factory observations while the direct store-level setup in this test still passes.

candidates.title: Missing draft state is treated as permission to proceed
candidates.detail: The PR lookup converts a missing or invalid `isDraft` field to false. Conflict delivery therefore proceeds when GitHub's response does not establish that the PR is ready for review. The poller admission path likewise treats an absent `isDraft` as false. This fails open at a condition the request explicitly requires.
candidates.suggestion: Require a boolean draft state in both the direct lookup and poller snapshot before starting or delivering a conflict round; refuse or leave the trigger pending when it cannot be confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR lookup or stored snapshot omits `isDraft` for a draft PR. The conflict round is admitted and the delivery check sees `false`, allowing a push to the draft branch.

candidates.title: Auto-merge is disabled before validating the current PR head
candidates.detail: The new delivery path changes the PR's auto-merge setting before checking that the PR is still open, belongs to the expected repository and branch, and remains at the reviewed head. A stale round can therefore mutate a PR even though the subsequent delivery guard rejects it.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the stored grant and current PR identity before disabling auto-merge, then revalidate after the awaited mutation and before pushing.
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR head changes while a conflict round runs and a user enables auto-merge for the new head. The stale round disables auto-merge, then fails its head check without pushing.

candidates.title: The PR comment does not summarize the resolution
candidates.detail: The request requires that "The PR gets one comment summarizing the resolution." The comment reports the base SHA and conflicted file names, but contains no account of how the conflicting changes were reconciled. A reader cannot assess the resolution from it.
candidates.suggestion: Include a concise, reviewed summary of the actual resolution in the comment, with the existing publication and redaction checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A conflict in a file is resolved by combining two behavioral changes; the resulting comment names the file and commit but does not explain the combined behavior.

findings.title: Cached first attempts lose the workspace needed by retries after restart
findings.detail: A completed first attempt is reused from state after restart, but the resumed stage cleans the checkout before reaching this line. A pending or newly started retry therefore runs without the build output or other files produced by that first attempt. Previously, a resumed gate stage reran the first attempt and recreated those files before retrying.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the workspace required by a pending retry, or replay the local first attempt before performing the retry after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate setup creates an ignored build directory, a check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts before or during its retry. On resume, checkoutCommitted removes the directory, the cached initial result is reused, and the retry fails because its build output is missing.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 calls `await checkoutCommitted(...)` before the initial execution. src/git/repos.ts:476 cleans with `["git", "clean", "-ffdxq"]`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 returns `results[purpose]` when cached, skipping setup. src/gates/run.ts:280 retries with `runner({ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected })`.
verification.trigger: Restart during a regression retry whose check depends on ignored setup output. Resume deletes the output, reuses the initial result without running setup, and retries against the incomplete workspace, producing a false failure.

findings.title: Executor events are never consumed
findings.detail: The shared execution path awaits only `result` and never reads `execution.events`. Gate reporting and landing logs currently work only because the local executor calls hooks directly; an executor implementing the advertised interface has no way to deliver its streamed check events to those consumers.
findings.suggestion: Consume the event stream in the shared execution path and forward events to the appropriate gate and landing reporting hooks, coordinating stream completion and errors with the result.
findings.failure_scenario: An injected executor yields check events and returns a valid GateRun. The stage verdict is computed, but no per-check pipeline events or landing check output are recorded.

findings.title: Restarting a retry removes the first attempt's build output
findings.detail: A resumed gates stage cleans the checkout before retrieving its saved initial result and attaching to the pending retry. The retry therefore runs without files created by the initial attempt, despite the existing requirement that retries see the same build output. Prepare likewise discards changes before resuming its baseline retry.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or reconstruct the first attempt's required workspace state before resuming a local retry, with restart coverage for checks that depend on generated files.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup or initial check creates an untracked build artifact, a later check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its retry. The resumed retry cannot find the artifact and produces a different verdict.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1157 unconditionally calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue))` on stage entry. src/git/repos.ts:476 implements cleanup with `["git", "clean", "-ffdxq"]`, removing build artifacts. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:23 then skips the completed initial execution: `if (results[purpose]) return results[purpose];`. The resumed regression retry cannot rebuild those artifacts: src/gates/run.ts:280 calls `runner({ ...cfg, setup: [], checks: selected })`. Its failure remains blocking at src/gates/run.ts:288: `blocking: !retry.ok`.
verification.trigger: Setup or a successful initial check creates an untracked build artifact needed by a later check. That check fails transiently, and the daemon restarts during its regression retry. Resume deletes the artifact, reuses the persisted initial result, and reruns only the failed check without setup, producing a blocking failure instead of a successful flaky retry.

findings.title: A checkpoint failure leaves started work uncancelled
findings.detail: The executor starts work before persisting its handle, but if persistence rejects, execution exits without attaching or cancelling. An executor whose start actually launches work can continue indefinitely without a durable handle, and a subsequent attempt can start duplicate work.
findings.suggestion: On persistence failure, attach to the returned handle and cancel the execution before propagating the failure, while preserving the original error.
findings.failure_scenario: A remote executor starts a gate suite and the state save fails because the database write fails; the run fails while the untracked suite continues.

findings.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart
findings.detail: The local handle contains the gate request, including commands and paths, but the persisted copy is transformed by `redactGateData`. On restart, local attach executes that transformed request rather than the trusted gate configuration. Credential redaction or terminal-control stripping can change a valid command or path, so the resumed run can check different behavior or fail unexpectedly.
findings.suggestion: Keep sensitive request data out of the persisted handle and reconstruct the local request from trusted run state when reattaching, without transforming executable input.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured gate command contains a registered credential or a terminal control character; after a restart, the local executor runs the redacted or stripped command.

verification.trigger: A pending local gate request contains a registered credential or a terminal sequence removed by stripVTControlCharacters. After restart, attachment executes the altered persisted command rather than the original command.

findings.title: Executor event streams are never consumed
findings.detail: The shared execution path awaits only the result and never reads `execution.events`. The local executor invokes hooks directly, masking the issue, but an injected executor that reports progress and check results through the interface loses those events; landing logs and pipeline gate events are absent.
findings.suggestion: Consume the event stream while awaiting the result and route events to the appropriate hooks, propagating stream failures according to the executor contract.

findings.detail: The local handle contains the complete request, but redactGateData transforms every string before the handle is stored. A restart attaches using that transformed request, so a gate command or working directory containing a registered credential or terminal control character can differ from the original. The initial attachment uses the unsanitized handle, making behavior depend on whether the daemon restarted.

An executor whose start actually launches work can continue indefinitely without a durable handle, and a subsequent attempt can start duplicate work.

candidates.title: Redacting the local handle changes the request replayed after restart

On restart, local attach executes that transformed request rather than the trusted gate configuration. Credential redaction or terminal-control stripping can change a valid command or path, so the resumed run can check different behavior or fail unexpectedly.

candidates.title: Executor event streams are never consumed

candidates.title: Persisting a sanitized local request can change the command replayed after restart

A restart attaches using that transformed request, so a gate command or working directory containing a registered credential or terminal control character can differ from the original. The initial attachment uses the unsanitized handle, making behavior depend on whether the daemon restarted.

candidates.failure_scenario: A base gate command contains a string registered for credential redaction. The daemon stops after saving the handle; on resume, local attachment executes the command with that string replaced by the redaction marker.

candidates.detail: The restart cases use a fake LAN executor whose handle has no request, while the local replay test serializes a handle directly without passing it through the persistence redaction path. Consequently they cannot catch a local request being changed before restart.

candidates.failure_scenario: A persisted local handle has a gate command altered by redaction; all current restart and local-attachment tests still pass.

candidates.title: Legacy resume test cannot distinguish local selection from injected selection
candidates.detail: The legacy-state test resumes with no injected executor, so local is the only available choice. It does not test the stated compatibility rule when another executor is selected. The selection code uses the injected executor whenever there is no stored handle.

candidates.title: Redacting the local handle changes the command replayed after restart

On restart, `localExecutor.attach` executes that altered request rather than the original trusted gate configuration. A resumed gate can therefore test different conditions and report a pass for a check that would have failed.

candidates.failure_scenario: A base gate command compares a value against a registered credential. The daemon restarts while that gate is pending; the persisted command contains the redaction marker instead of the original value, so the replay evaluates a different condition and can pass incorrectly.

A restart during landing checks starts another execution instead of attaching to the existing one, leaving remote work duplicated and its result unobserved.
candidates.suggestion: Persist the landing execution handle in durable queue state before attaching, and restore it when resuming the checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A landing check is running on an executor whose work survives daemon restart. The daemon restarts before the result arrives; the queue starts a second execution because the first handle was never stored.

findings.title: Cargo home allowance exposes registry credentials to gate commands
findings.detail: The gate profile grants file reads throughout Cargo home, but neither the built-in deny list nor the later specific-deny rules exclude Cargo's credentials or credentials.toml files. Changing CARGO_HOME for the gate process does not prevent an untrusted command from reading the original files by absolute path. This leaves registry tokens accessible to candidate code despite the requirement that credential stores fall outside the gate allowlist.
findings.suggestion: Exclude Cargo credential files from the effective gate profile while retaining access to the toolchain files Cargo needs, and add a probe using a temporary Cargo home containing a stand-in credential.

That collects only recognizable literals and holdout phrases, so an ordinary sentence unique to the verifier is not added to the redaction catalogue. If a report quotes that sentence outside the holdout section, it is returned unchanged, contrary to the requirement to withhold verifier prose and report lines quoting holdout material.
findings.suggestion: Treat verifier notes as private observations when building the catalogue, and add a test with a plain-prose verifier note quoted in a report.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier note says "The violet otter failed again." for a holdout check, and the report repeats that sentence outside the holdout section. If those words are absent from the holdout scenarios and public sources, the report exposes the sentence.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:254 calls `collect(verify?.notes)` without enabling `privateProse`; lines 243–244 add whole prose only when `privateProse` is true. src/pipeline/prompts.ts:246–247 processes observed text only through `if (observed !== undefined) collectLiterals(observed);`, which does not collect ordinary unquoted prose such as the candidate sentence. src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:352–356 preserves report lines when no catalogue pattern matches, and lines 521–523 return the filtered report.
verification.trigger: A verifier's notes contain holdout-only prose such as “The violet otter failed again.”, absent from scenarios and public sources and containing no syntax-shaped literals. A report repeats it outside the holdout section. The sentence never enters the withholding catalogue and is returned by limitless_get_change.

findings.title: Hidden test fixture is never quoted in the report
findings.detail: The test writes a hidden test file but places only its sentinel in the report. It therefore verifies redaction of a detail copied into the holdout scenario, but does not verify that a report line quoting hidden test text stays withheld.
findings.suggestion: Add a report line quoting the hidden test text and assert that the line is withheld while an unrelated report line remains visible.
findings.failure_scenario: A report quotes hidden test code containing details absent from the holdout scenario, and the change view returns that quotation.

verification.evidence: test/mcp-proxy.test.ts:180 writes hidden code `expect(uppercase('${hidden}')).toBe('PRIVATE');`, but :187 also includes `${hidden}` in the scenario, and :206 reports only `Quoted hidden test: ${hidden}`. Thus the test exercises scenario matching, not hidden-file quotations. src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:239 harvests `privateHoldoutDetails(standalone, publicSources, observed)` from recorded observations; it never reads the hidden file. At :351–356, unmatched report lines pass through unchanged (`: line`).
verification.trigger: A report outside the Holdout scenarios section quotes a hidden-test assertion or literal absent from the scenarios and recorded verifier observations. The quotation matches no catalogue entry and is returned to the MCP reviewer, exposing holdout-only material; the fixture does not cover this case.

findings.title: Diffs quoted in reports still expose multiline credentials
findings.detail: The new line-prefix-aware filter is applied only to the diff field. Reports returned by the same tool still pass through literal privacy matching, so a report containing a unified diff with each credential line prefixed by '+' or '-' exposes the credential. The request explicitly includes other outputs that render diffs or requires them to be listed as follow-ups.
findings.suggestion: Apply equivalent line-prefix-aware credential filtering to diff quotations in reports, or explicitly document this output as a follow-up as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: A persisted report contains '+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret' and 'alpha-secret\nbeta-secret' is registered as a credential; report.text returns both lines.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:652–654 renders reports using `privacy(report) === report ? privacy(withoutHoldoutSection(report, holdoutRedact)) : protect(report)`, without `privatePatchLines`. src/util/private-output.ts:12–14 checks `privateMatches(...)` then `redactCredentials(text)`. A targeted reproduction confirmed both leave `+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret` unchanged.
verification.trigger: A persisted report quotes the two credential lines with '+' prefixes and has no independently matching holdout detail. Report pages expose both fragments.

findings.title: Repeated credential matches make patch filtering quadratic
findings.detail: Every occurrence scans every line range synchronously before paging. An untrusted large patch with many occurrences of a registered multiline value can therefore block the daemon's event loop for a prolonged period, and each page request repeats the work. A targeted invocation of the extracted function took 893 ms for 50,000 lines and 3,514 ms for 100,000 lines, consistent with quadratic growth.
findings.suggestion: Map match offsets to affected ranges using an ordered cursor or binary search, so work grows with the patch size and number of matching lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A changed file contains hundreds of thousands of repetitions of a two-line registered credential; requesting its change view monopolizes the daemon event loop for minutes.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:74 iterates `for (const range of ranges)` for each `withhold` call; lines 80–84 call `withhold(start, start + literal.length)` for every occurrence. This performs quadratic work for repeated credentials. Targeted measurements took approximately 28 ms for 4,000 repetitions and 103 ms for 8,000. Lines 617–629 filter the complete diff before paging.
verification.trigger: Hundreds of thousands of credential repetitions in one added file cause billions of synchronous range comparisons, blocking the daemon event loop despite the page-size cap.

findings.title: Clipped credential matches leave changed lines visible
findings.detail: When a hunk ends partway through a multiline credential, the clipped-prefix match withholds only context lines. The adjacent-pair check does not cover a credential that starts in the middle of a patch line, so a deleted or added line containing that credential fragment remains visible.
findings.suggestion: Map clipped matches to every affected patch line, including additions and deletions, and cover credentials embedded within surrounding line text.
findings.failure_scenario: A ten-line credential starts after a public prefix on a line. Changing that first line produces a hunk containing only the first few credential lines. The old-side prefix matches, but the deleted first line is excluded by the clipped filter and does not match the whole-line pair check, so its credential fragment appears in the patch.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:75 restricts clipped matches with `(!clipped || range.prefix === " ")`; lines 90–91 pass `true` for clipped prefixes. The adjacent-pair fallback at lines 101–102 requires `framed.includes(`\n${pair}`)`. A targeted reproduction withheld the context lines but retained `-key=secret-0`.
verification.trigger: A credential begins after a public prefix on a deleted line, and its remaining lines extend beyond the hunk. The clipped match excludes the deletion, while the public prefix prevents the pair fallback from matching; the credential fragment remains visible.

findings.title: Review prompts still include unredacted line-prefixed diffs
findings.detail: The request also requires other outputs that render diffs to receive the same treatment or be listed as follow-ups. Review prompts include patch text, while the existing literal credential redaction cannot match a multiline credential split by diff prefixes. This path was neither changed nor identified as a follow-up.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same patch-aware credential filtering before diff text is sent to reviewers, or explicitly document this output as the requested follow-up.
findings.failure_scenario: A verify-change diff adds a file containing a registered two-line credential. The review prompt contains the two lines prefixed with `+`, so literal credential redaction does not remove them before the prompt is sent to a model.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:602 returns `patch: patch.stdout`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1435 passes it into review input: `...(ctx.state.flow === "verify-change" ? { patch: reviewDiff.patch } : {})`. src/pipeline/prompts.ts:398 applies `input = redactGateData(input)`, whose string handling calls `redactGateOutput(v)` (src/gates/output.ts:31), then `redactCredentials(stripVTControlCharacters(output))` (line 23). Credential redaction uses literal replacement: `text = text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")` (src/util/proc.ts:684). The patch is embedded with `fence(input.patch.slice(0, PATCH_LIMIT) || "(empty diff)")` (src/pipeline/prompts.ts:460). The new `privatePatchLines` protection is local to src/integrations/mcp-change.ts:49 and is not used here.
verification.trigger: A verify-change head adds a text file containing a registered credential `alpha-secret\nbeta-secret`, within the prompt's patch limit and without a separate private-string audit blocker. Git renders it as `+alpha-secret\n+beta-secret`; literal redaction cannot match the registered value, so both credential lines reach the review model.

findings.title: Keep reviewer execution time out of failed-trial preparation timing
findings.detail: The catch path recomputes preparationMs whenever roundsUsed is absent. Review trials never set roundsUsed, so an exception after the reviewer starts overwrites the already-recorded preparation duration with elapsed time including the reviewer invocation. The reported preparation and trial times are no longer separate for that failure.
findings.suggestion: Record the preparation duration once, and only calculate it in the catch path if preparation did not finish.
findings.failure_scenario: A review invocation runs for several minutes and then throws, for example on an origin-exclusion failure. Its preparationMs includes those minutes even though setup had already completed.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:689-690 records completed preparation: `const preparationMs = Date.now() - preparationStarted;` and `trial.details.preparationMs = preparationMs`. The catch at src/evals/runner.ts:1201-1202 overwrites it with `!trial.details.roundsUsed ? { preparationMs: Date.now() - preparationStarted } : {}`. `roundsUsed` is assigned only for implement cases (`if ("hidden" in item)`, lines 1101-1104). Origin failures explicitly reach this catch via `if (originFailure) throw originFailure` (line 1073).
verification.trigger: A review finishes preparation, spends time invoking reviewers, then throws an origin-exclusion error. The catch overwrites preparationMs with elapsed preparation plus reviewer execution time.

findings.title: Setup variants can make routing policy select the wrong trial arm
findings.detail: The request says production is unchanged and gives the setup-enabled standard prompt a separate cache identity. That identity also makes a setup-enabled system and an otherwise identical system valid in the same eval. Policy selection assumes at most one standard system per target, however, and generatePolicy takes only the first summary. It therefore silently ignores one arm, with the selected evidence depending on system ordering.
findings.suggestion: Define which standard arm is eligible for routing policy and update policy selection to handle both configurations explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains standard systems for the same target with and without setup. Both pass configuration validation, but policy generation uses only the first system's results even if the other arm has different outcomes.

verification.evidence: src/evals/cache.ts:49-50 hashes all configuration except name: `reviewSystemHash({ name: _name, ...config } ...)`. Thus setup variants pass the configuration-hash duplicate check at src/evals/cases.ts:425-432. src/evals/policy.ts:133-143 selects standard single systems for the same target without distinguishing setup, then takes `summarize(...)[0]`. src/evals/stats.ts:327-328 computes separate summaries using `candidates.map(...)` and `trials.filter((t) => candidateOf(t) === candidate)`.
verification.trigger: An eval includes standard single systems for the same target and implementer-report setting, differing only in setup. findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the initial TLS connection
findings.detail: The initial connection accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that connection. A man-in-the-middle can relay the pairing request to the real coordinator, return its code and secret to the worker, and present its own certificate. The owner sees the same code on both sides and approves it; the attacker then observes the claim and issued token. Pinning the attacker's certificate on subsequent requests does not prevent this. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never authenticated or used to bind the exchange.
findings.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to both endpoints' certificate fingerprints and the pairing exchange, so relaying through a different TLS certificate changes the code or causes verification to fail.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, proxies the real coordinator's pairing response, and forwards the approved claim while terminating both TLS connections.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:23-27 sends the initial pairing request with only `{ signal }`; src/workers/tls.ts:103 sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`. src/workers/client.ts:39 subsequently pins `first.fingerprint`. src/db/workers.ts:61 returns `{ code, secret, expiresAt }`, and :89 issues the approved token to whoever presents that secret.
verification.trigger: An active proxy terminates initial TLS and relays the coordinator's pairing response. Both sides show the same code, but the proxy learns the claim secret and approved token; the worker pins the proxy certificate.

findings.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
findings.detail: Private read protection is an in-memory registry. Pairing releases the token and fingerprint registrations on return, and `runWorker` registers them only in the worker CLI process. A daemon running gates or agents in a separate process therefore does not include those files in its sandbox deny paths. The coordinator TLS key has the same lifetime problem when its listener is disabled after the key has been created. Mode 0600 does not protect files from another process running as the same user.
findings.suggestion: Register the configured worker credential and TLS key paths in every process that constructs agent or gate sandboxes, independent of whether a worker or listener is currently running.
findings.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, then run a factory daemon and a gate on the same machine; the daemon's sandbox is built without the worker token path registered, allowing a gate with access to that path to read the token.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:55-57 releases protection with `for (const release of held) release()`. src/util/private-reads.ts:4 keeps registrations in a process-local `new Map<string, number>()`. src/harness/read-policy.ts:190 builds denies from `credentials` and `privateReadPaths()`; :217 applies the broader home deny only when `gate` is true.
verification.trigger: A separate daemon never registers the paired worker files. Editors can read the default worker token; gates can also read it where its location is otherwise readable, such as a configured data directory outside the home. findings.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently blocks restart
findings.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before invoking OpenSSL. If generation fails, times out, or the process stops before both files are complete, the next start either rejects the incomplete pair or tries to parse invalid material. No cleanup or recovery occurs, so the worker listener or pairing command continues to fail on every subsequent start.
findings.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names, validate them, and publish them only after successful generation; clean up incomplete temporary material on failure.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating the empty key file but before OpenSSL creates the certificate; every later listener start throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:18 creates `key.pem` with `writeFileSync(keyPath, "", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 })` before awaiting OpenSSL at lines 19–39. Line 17 throws `new Error("Incomplete worker TLS material")` when only one file exists. The catch at lines 45–47 only calls `release()` and rethrows; it does not remove incomplete files.
verification.trigger: Interruption during initial certificate generation leaves key.pem present and cert.pem absent. Every subsequent listener start throws until the files are manually repaired. This requires an unusual first-start timing window.

findings.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
findings.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. The displayed code comes from the coordinator but is not bound to that certificate or to an authenticated exchange. An intermediary can relay the pairing request and code unchanged, obtain the pairing secret and issued token, and leave the worker pinned to the intermediary's certificate even though the owner compared matching codes.

findings.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, forwards the request to the real coordinator, and relays its code. The owner approves the matching code; the attacker claims the token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.
