candidates.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the initial TLS connection
candidates.detail: The initial connection accepts any certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that connection. A man-in-the-middle can relay the pairing request to the real coordinator, return its code and secret to the worker, and present its own certificate. The owner sees the same code on both sides and approves it; the attacker then observes the claim and issued token. Pinning the attacker's certificate on subsequent requests does not prevent this. The submitted worker certificate fingerprint is never authenticated or used to bind the exchange.
candidates.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to both endpoints' certificate fingerprints and the pairing exchange, so relaying through a different TLS certificate changes the code or causes verification to fail.
candidates.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, proxies the real coordinator's pairing response, and forwards the approved claim while terminating both TLS connections.

candidates.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
candidates.detail: Private read protection is an in-memory registry. Pairing releases the token and fingerprint registrations on return, and `runWorker` registers them only in the worker CLI process. A daemon running gates or agents in a separate process therefore does not include those files in its sandbox deny paths. The coordinator TLS key has the same lifetime problem when its listener is disabled after the key has been created. Mode 0600 does not protect files from another process running as the same user.
candidates.suggestion: Register the configured worker credential and TLS key paths in every process that constructs agent or gate sandboxes, independent of whether a worker or listener is currently running.
candidates.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, then run a factory daemon and a gate on the same machine; the daemon's sandbox is built without the worker token path registered, allowing a gate with access to that path to read the token.

candidates.title: Interrupted certificate creation permanently blocks restart
candidates.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before invoking OpenSSL. If generation fails, times out, or the process stops before both files are complete, the next start either rejects the incomplete pair or tries to parse invalid material. No cleanup or recovery occurs, so the worker listener or pairing command continues to fail on every subsequent start.
candidates.suggestion: Generate both files under temporary names, validate them, and publish them only after successful generation; clean up incomplete temporary material on failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped after creating the empty key file but before OpenSSL creates the certificate; every later listener start throws `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

candidates.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
candidates.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the worker pins the certificate observed on that connection. The displayed code comes from the coordinator but is not bound to that certificate or to an authenticated exchange. An intermediary can relay the pairing request and code unchanged, obtain the pairing secret and issued token, and leave the worker pinned to the intermediary's certificate even though the owner compared matching codes.
candidates.suggestion: Bind the owner-verified pairing code to the coordinator certificate and pairing exchange so a relaying intermediary cannot obtain a usable token or substitute its certificate.
candidates.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, forwards the request to the real coordinator, and relays its code. The owner approves the matching code; the attacker claims the token and the worker pins the attacker's certificate.

candidates.title: Permanent TLS and configuration errors are retried silently forever
candidates.detail: The heartbeat loop catches every request exception and retries without a deadline or diagnostic. This includes a changed coordinator fingerprint and malformed coordinator URL, neither of which can be repaired by retrying. The worker remains running but never sends another heartbeat, and the owner receives no explanation.
candidates.suggestion: Retry only transient transport failures with a bounded policy; propagate permanent validation and certificate-pin failures with their original reason.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing. Every heartbeat fails fingerprint validation, but the worker silently retries indefinitely instead of reporting that it must be paired again.

candidates.title: Existing TLS key loses sandbox protection when the listener is disabled
candidates.detail: The TLS key is registered with the sandbox deny list only when the listener starts. After a listener has created the key, restarting the daemon with workers.listen unset skips registration even though the key remains on disk. Agent sandboxes that can read that data directory can then read the coordinator's private key, contrary to the requirement that it be denied in every agent sandbox.
candidates.suggestion: Register protection for existing worker TLS material independently of whether the listener is enabled, and retain it for the daemon lifetime.
candidates.failure_scenario: Enable the listener once, then disable it and restart the daemon with the data directory outside the default home deny paths. A subsequent agent can read worker-tls/key.pem.

candidates.title: Interrupted certificate generation prevents future startup
candidates.detail: Certificate generation creates the final key path before running openssl, but its error path leaves partial files behind. A timeout, failed openssl invocation, or interruption can therefore leave only the empty key or other incomplete material. Every later start rejects the incomplete material, requiring manual cleanup.
candidates.suggestion: Generate both files in temporary paths and publish them only after successful generation, cleaning up partial temporary files on failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon is interrupted after creating key.pem but before openssl writes cert.pem. Subsequent starts fail with `Incomplete worker TLS material`.

candidates.title: Credential read protection ends with the pairing process
candidates.detail: The worker token and coordinator fingerprint are registered in an in-memory deny list only while `pairWorker` or `runWorker` holds them. Pairing releases both registrations before exiting, and a separately running daemon has its own deny list. Likewise, an existing coordinator TLS key is not registered when the listener is disabled. An agent sandbox created by that daemon therefore does not receive these paths as private-file denies.
candidates.suggestion: Register persisted worker credential and TLS-key paths in every process that constructs agent sandbox policies, independently of whether pairing, the worker loop or the listener is currently running.
candidates.failure_scenario: Pair a worker, exit the pairing command, and run an agent through a separate daemon using the same data directory: that daemon's private-file deny list does not contain the stored worker token or coordinator fingerprint.

candidates.title: Privacy probe masks the cross-process credential protection gap
candidates.detail: The real-Seatbelt test creates the TLS material and registers both worker files in the same process that starts the gate, retaining all registrations throughout the probe. It consequently passes even if a daemon started separately after pairing has no credential paths in its in-memory deny list.
candidates.suggestion: Add a real-Seatbelt probe that persists credentials, releases the pairing registrations, and launches the gate from an independently initialized daemon or process; cover an existing TLS key with the listener disabled as well.
candidates.failure_scenario: The current implementation releases the registrations after pairing, yet this test retains them and reports all three files denied.

candidates.title: Pairing code does not authenticate the coordinator connection
candidates.detail: The initial pairing request accepts any TLS certificate, and the displayed code is supplied by that untrusted connection. An active intermediary can forward the request to the real coordinator, relay its code to the worker, and retain the returned pairing secret. The owner and worker see matching codes, but the intermediary can claim the approved token and the worker pins the intermediary's certificate.
candidates.suggestion: Bind the human-compared code to both the coordinator certificate fingerprint and the pairing exchange, so relaying a coordinator response through a different TLS certificate changes the code.
candidates.failure_scenario: An attacker intercepts the worker's first connection, proxies `/worker/pair` to the coordinator, and relays the real code. After the owner approves it, the attacker claims the worker token.

candidates.title: Worker credentials are not denied to sandboxes in other processes
candidates.detail: `protectPrivateFile` maintains an in-memory registry. Pairing releases its registrations before exiting, and `runWorker` registers the files only in the worker process. A separately running daemon on the same machine does not receive those registrations when it constructs Claude or Codex sandbox policies, so its agents can read the persistent worker token and coordinator fingerprint. Mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every daemon process that launches agents, including when the worker is stopped, and cover separate-process sandbox behavior.
candidates.failure_scenario: A machine runs both a worker and a factory daemon under the same user. An agent launched by the daemon reads `<data>/worker/token` and impersonates that worker.

candidates.title: Disabling the listener leaves its existing TLS key unprotected from agents
candidates.detail: The TLS key is added to the process-local private-read registry only when the listener is enabled. After an owner removes `workers.listen` and restarts the daemon, the existing key remains on disk but is no longer included in agent sandbox deny paths. An agent running as the same user can read it, compromising the certificate trusted by already paired workers if the listener is later re-enabled.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent TLS key path independently of whether the listener is currently enabled, or securely remove and rotate the material when disabling it.
candidates.failure_scenario: A coordinator previously enabled workers, then starts with the listener disabled. A tool-enabled agent reads `<data>/worker-tls/key.pem` before the listener is enabled again.

candidates.title: Store untrusted heartbeat fields only after redaction
candidates.detail: Heartbeat capabilities are serialized directly into SQLite. Several worker-controlled strings can contain coordinator credentials or private strings, but sanitization occurs only when listing workers. This leaves the unredacted values in persistent storage even though the trust-boundary rules require redaction before storage.
candidates.suggestion: Redact and apply private-string policy to worker-supplied capability fields before persisting them, while preserving the fields needed for version matching.
candidates.failure_scenario: A paired worker sends a coordinator credential or private string in `osVersion`; the value is written verbatim to the workers table.

candidates.title: Worker credentials are not denied in the daemon's agent sandboxes
candidates.detail: The request requires the worker token and coordinator fingerprint to be read-denied to gates. The deny registry is process-local, but pairing and the worker loop run as separate CLI processes from the daemon. Their registrations are also released when those commands exit. A daemon on the same machine therefore does not add these files to its agent sandbox deny lists; mode 0600 does not protect them from agents running as the same user.
candidates.suggestion: Register the persistent worker credential paths in every daemon process that can launch agents and gates, including when the worker command is not running.
candidates.failure_scenario: A machine is both a paired worker and a coordinator. An agent launched by its daemon reads the token under the worker data directory and uses it to impersonate the worker.

candidates.title: Disabling the listener removes protection for an existing TLS key
candidates.detail: The request says the TLS key is read-denied in every agent sandbox. When the listener is disabled, startup returns before registering the previously generated key with the process-local deny registry. The key remains on disk, and editor sandboxes do not otherwise deny the worker TLS directory.
candidates.suggestion: Register the existing key path for the daemon lifetime independently of whether the listener is enabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: An owner disables workers after having enabled them, then starts a run. An editor agent can read the retained coordinator TLS private key.

candidates.title: Interrupted certificate generation permanently blocks listener startup
candidates.detail: The key file is created before openssl runs, but a failed or interrupted generation leaves it behind. The next start sees incomplete TLS material and throws instead of generating a certificate, so a transient failure prevents the daemon from starting whenever the worker listener is configured.
candidates.suggestion: Generate the certificate and key in temporary files and publish them together, cleaning up incomplete generation safely.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon is stopped or openssl fails after the empty key file is created but before the certificate is written; every subsequent daemon start fails with "Incomplete worker TLS material".

candidates.title: A changed pinned certificate is retried indefinitely without an explanation
candidates.detail: The request requires the coordinator fingerprint to be pinned. Although the transport detects a mismatch, the heartbeat loop catches that error along with transient connection failures and retries forever. The operator receives no indication that the certificate changed and that intervention is required.
candidates.suggestion: Surface fingerprint mismatch as a terminal error while retaining retries for transient transport failures.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator certificate changes after pairing. The worker remains running but never sends another heartbeat and never reports the pin mismatch.

findings.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
findings.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
findings.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:65 rejects confinement failures: `.refine((r) => !r.confinementError && !launchFailure(r.output), "Worker confinement failed")`. src/server/workers.ts:131-133 handles that rejection with `workers.fail(id, ...)`. src/db/workers.ts:260 transitions attempts using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. src/gates/lan.ts:73-89 handles `job.state === "failed"` by running locally, then `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`, without preserving a terminal confinement failure.
verification.trigger: Both worker attempts report Seatbelt launch failures. They become retryable infrastructure failures; a successful local fallback replaces them with a passing GateRun.

findings.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
findings.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:68–72 copies stored events into the event stream, then returns the final result directly: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. Local fallback likewise uses only the new execution: src/gates/lan.ts:86–89: `const [run] = await Promise.all([execution.result, stream]); ... workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`. Earlier failed check events are never reconciled with either result.
verification.trigger: A worker posts a failed check, then disconnects before submitting its GateRun. The job retries or falls back locally, and that execution passes. The returned GateRun reports a pass despite the recorded failed check.

findings.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
findings.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
findings.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a mismatched pin with `reject(new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed"))`. src/workers/client.ts:146-149 discards that error through `.catch(() => { requestSignal.throwIfAborted(); return undefined; })`; :139 and :157-158 retry indefinitely with a delay capped at 10 seconds.
verification.trigger: A coordinator presents a certificate different from the stored pin while the worker remains un-aborted. The worker silently retries forever instead of reporting the fingerprint mismatch; certificate verification still prevents sending credentials.

findings.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
findings.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers the credential with `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`; assertions at :681–683 inspect only stored `result` and `events`. Coordinator storage independently redacts: src/db/workers.ts:57–60 calls `redactGateData(data)`, and :238 stores `this.sanitize(event)`. No assertion inspects the outgoing worker payload.
verification.trigger: A regression removes worker-side redaction while coordinator redaction remains: the shared credential registry lets stored-output assertions pass without establishing that worker-only credentials were removed before transmission.

findings.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
findings.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:123–124 sets both `baseSha: sha` and `headSha: sha`; the bundle end-to-end test at :657 uses `request(true)`. Production code at src/server/workers.ts:88 includes both via `[...new Set([request.headSha, request.baseSha].filter(Boolean))]`, but the fixture exercises only one distinct SHA.
verification.trigger: A regression omits a distinct base commit from bundle creation: the existing end-to-end test still passes because its base and head are identical, leaving base inclusion untested.

findings.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
findings.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:123-130 validates each event or final result independently through `validCheck(...)` or `validRun(...)`. Lines 135-136 then independently call `workers.event(id, event.data)` or `workers.complete(id, result.data.run)`. src/db/workers.ts:288-291 completes by storing the supplied result without comparing stored events. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns that result: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`.
verification.trigger: A leased worker posts a schema-valid failed event for a requested check, then a schema-valid passing final result for the same check and requested SHA. Both requests are accepted, and the job completes with the passing result despite the recorded failure.

findings.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
findings.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
findings.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:114 redacts using the worker's credentials, then :126 truncates with `combined.slice(-OUTPUT_TAIL)` (:74 sets 6,000). src/workers/client.ts:233 sends `{ run, sha }`. Coordinator storage sanitizes through `redactGateData(data)` at src/db/workers.ts:57-60 and :291, but src/util/proc.ts:683-684 replaces only complete registered secrets: `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`.
verification.trigger: A gate prints a credential registered only on the coordinator, followed by output positioning the tail boundary inside that credential. Worker truncation sends only its suffix, which coordinator literal redaction cannot match, allowing the credential fragment to be stored.

findings.title: A failed check from a lost lease can become a pass
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure retries must “never turn a failing check into a pass.” Check events from an attempt are streamed to hooks, but after that attempt loses its lease the final verdict uses only the later worker's GateRun. A failed check already reported by the first worker is therefore discarded for verdict purposes.
findings.suggestion: Retain completed check failures across infrastructure attempts and ensure a later passing result cannot erase them.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check event, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and the replacement worker reports that check as passing. The returned GateRun marks it as passing.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:276–277 calls `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")` or `this.fail(j.id, "Worker disconnected")`; src/db/workers.ts:257–260 requeues the first failed attempt with `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. A replacement result is stored directly at src/db/workers.ts:290–291: `UPDATE gate_jobs SET state='done',result=?,updated_at=? WHERE id=? AND state=?`. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns that result without incorporating previous failed check events.
verification.trigger: The first worker posts a failing check and loses its lease before posting its GateRun. A replacement worker submits a passing result for the same check. The executor returns that passing result without retaining the earlier failure in the GateRun.

findings.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs
findings.detail: The request says `attach` waits for the stored result so “a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.” Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A persisted timeout or retry job is cancelled and replaced when its stage resumes, even if the worker is still running or has completed it.
findings.suggestion: Provide durable resume handling for every LAN gate execution purpose, preserving the original job identity and any state needed to consume its result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. On resume the pending handle fails the purpose whitelist, is cancelled, and a new job is enqueued.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29–37 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; otherwise it calls `cancelGateExecution(pending.handle, ctx.deps.gateExecutor)`. verification.trigger: Restart the coordinator while an opted-in LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. Resuming the gates stage rejects and cancels its persisted handle, then enqueues a fresh initial execution, discarding the ongoing worker job and repeating gate work.

findings.title: Home-relative paths and file URLs bypass sanitization
findings.detail:
The sanitizer compares link destinations only against literal filesystem roots. A home-relative link such as the one in the request is left broken, and a file URL containing the absolute worktree path is published unchanged, including the owner's username. The direct check below returned both inputs unchanged.

Command: bun -e 'let s=await Bun.file("src/gates/publication.ts").text(); let f=new Function(s.slice(s.indexOf("export function sanitizePublication"),s.indexOf("/** Check both")).replace("export function","function").replace(/: string( \| undefined)?/g,"")+";return sanitizePublication")(); for(let x of ["[file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)","[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)"]) console.log(f(x,"/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run","/Users/alice/.limitless"))'
Output:
[file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)
[file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts)
[/Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts](a.ts)
findings.suggestion: Recognize home-relative paths and local file URLs before comparing them with the configured roots, and add cases for both forms.
findings.failure_scenario: A report contains [file](file:///Users/alice/.limitless/work/run/a.ts) or [file](~/.limitless/work/run/a.ts).

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before each merge command
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can repeat that sequence on retry. A reclaim during the lookup is invisible until the heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.
findings.suggestion: Pass an ownership guard into the helper and check it immediately before each merge command, including retries.
findings.failure_scenario: The old worker enters mergePullRequest, its PR view request is deferred, another owner reclaims the entry, and the view returns before the old heartbeat fires. The old worker then runs gh pr merge.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:701 calls `await mergePullRequest(...)`; ownership is checked only afterward at :715, `this.assertClaim(entry.id)`. Inside src/git/repos.ts:1447, `await sh(view, { cwd, signal })` precedes :1462, `return sh(cmd, { cwd, signal, stdin: body })`, without an ownership check.
verification.trigger: Reclaim the entry while the helper's PR view is pending, then return a valid OPEN response before the heartbeat. The displaced worker issues gh pr merge.

findings.title: Guard the actual push after its preparation awaits
findings.detail: The transaction verifies the claim before calling pushExistingBranch, but that helper awaits commit resolution, transport setup, a remote lookup, and an ancestry check before issuing git push. A reclaim during any of those awaits leaves the old worker able to push before its heartbeat notices.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership inside the push helper immediately before issuing the push, using a guard supplied by the land worker.
findings.failure_scenario: The worker passes the ownership transaction, pauses in the helper's ls-remote call, and another owner reclaims the entry. When ls-remote returns, the stale worker pushes its merge commit.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:517 checks ownership through `this.owned(...)`, then :522 calls `await pushExistingBranch(...)`. That helper awaits `remoteSh(["git", "ls-remote", ...])` at src/git/repos.ts:1313 and `worktreeGit(...merge-base...)` at :1315 before pushing at :1321, without checking ownership.
verification.trigger: Reclaim during the helper's ls-remote request; return the approved remote SHA before the heartbeat, with the ancestry check succeeding. The stale worker pushes its merge commit.

findings.title: Do not discard a checkout reused by the new claimant
findings.detail: All attempts for an entry use the same land-<id> worktree path. After a reclaim, the old worker reaches this unconditional cleanup even when a new worker has already recreated and started using that path. It can remove the new worker's worktree and cause its checks or merge to fail.
findings.suggestion: Isolate checkout paths by claim or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a newer claimant's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI response is deferred, the entry is reclaimed and the new worker creates its checkout, then the old response returns. The old worker detects the lost claim but its finally block removes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:549 calls `this.assertClaim(entry.id)` after the CI observation. Its exception still executes :396–397, `finally { await this.discard(repo, cwd); }`. The path is shared across owners at :812, `return join(this.deps.paths.work, `land-${entry.id}`)`, and discard unconditionally calls :842, `rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
verification.trigger: A new claimant creates the same entry checkout while the old worker awaits CI. Returning the old response throws for lost ownership, but cleanup deletes the new claimant's checkout.

findings.title: CI inspection can still write after the claim is reclaimed
findings.detail: Passing the ownership check as `current` does not guard every write inside `ciDecision`. Its inspection awaits the default branch and check-run responses, then emits feed events and updates the `ci.main` setting before checking `current()`. A claim reclaimed during either read can therefore leave the old worker writing outcomes after ownership was lost.
findings.suggestion: Check ownership after the awaited reads and in the same transaction as each resulting durable write, including CI inspection writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker starts CI inspection, another owner reclaims the entry while the default-branch check response is pending, and the old response contains a failing check. The old worker emits a `ci.main_red` event and updates the CI setting after reclaim.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:584–587 includes `this.store.ownsLandClaim(entry.id, this.owner)` in the callback passed to ciDecision. However, src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:239 awaits `checks(mainSha)`, then :258–264 calls `emit("ci.main_red", ...)` and :267 calls `store.setSetting(...)`; only :268 checks `if (!current()) return true`.
verification.trigger: Reclaim while default-branch checks are pending, then return a failing check matching the PR's failure. The old inspection emits ci.main_red and updates the CI setting before checking ownership.

findings.title: A displaced worker can delete the new owner's worktree

The new owner can then fail or operate on a deleted checkout.
findings.suggestion: Give each attempt an isolated worktree path or otherwise ensure cleanup cannot remove a successor's checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker is waiting for CI, its claim is reclaimed, and the new worker creates the same checkout. When the old CI response arrives, its ownership check throws and its `finally` deletes the new worker's checkout.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:393 awaits CI, whose post-response ownership check at :549 throws when displaced. Cleanup remains unconditional at :397, `await this.discard(repo, cwd)`. verification.trigger: The new owner creates the shared checkout before the old CI response returns. The displaced worker's finally block deletes it. This is the same defect as C3.

findings.title: A worker that lost its claim can remove the new worker's checkout

candidates.title: Do not discard a reclaimed worker's shared worktree

The unconditional cleanup runs even when an ownership check detects a reclaim, so the old worker can remove the newer worker's checkout while it is running. This also conflicts with the request's requirement that a worker that lost its claim writes nothing.
candidates.suggestion: Give attempts separate worktree paths or otherwise ensure stale cleanup cannot remove a newer attempt's checkout.
candidates.failure_scenario: The old worker is awaiting CI, another process reclaims the entry and creates its checkout, and the old CI response arrives; its `finally` removes the new worker's worktree.

findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.

findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:250-252 checks the URL and open state, then unconditionally executes `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. test/land-queue.test.ts:3282 explicitly expects this rejection.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 persists runless entries as `entry.runId ?? ""`. At base 381e4384, src/db/store.ts:100 reads `run_id AS runId`; src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries, and src/db/store.ts:2784 claims states including 'queued' and 'waiting_ci'. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 executes `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` then `if (!run) throw new Error(`run ${entry.runId} is gone`)`; its catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, which at :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`.
verification.trigger: Rollback while a runless entry is queued or waiting for CI. Once its claim is available, the previous daemon claims it, fails to find run "", and persists terminal state blocked with reason "run  is gone"; upgrading again does not automatically resume it.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:184 routes targets without an owning run to `requestUnowned(input)`. src/land/queue.ts:226-227 accepts only a full GitHub PR URL and otherwise throws `"run not found"`. src/cli/main.ts:573 sends `target: sub` without resolving a number.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open PR without a factory run fails instead of queuing it, including when only one GitHub repository is configured.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.

Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 looks up that empty run ID and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone`; :327 and :912 turn the error into persisted state "blocked".

findings.title: Blocked unowned lands disappear from the CLI digest
findings.detail: The new feed entries have a null run ID, but the digest removes every feed item without a run ID before checking whether a blocked land is actionable. Operators relying on the digest therefore do not see these failures, despite the land feed containing them.
findings.suggestion: Teach the digest to resolve unowned land entries by PR URL or land ID and display their current blocked state.
findings.failure_scenario: A confined check fails for an unowned PR; its `land.blocked` feed item exists, but `limitless digest` omits it from blocked lands.

verification.trigger: A confined check blocks an unowned land and emits its feed item, but `limitless digest` deletes the item because its runId is null, omitting it from the blocked-land count and details.

findings.title: The unowned land test does not verify actual confinement

findings.title: Encoded credentials in filenames escape diagnostic redaction
findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic passes a Git-controlled path to `redactCredentials` without decoding it first. The new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts` has the same issue: `redactGateOutput` also performs literal credential redaction. These diagnostics can be stored as events or sent back to an implementer.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress the filename when its decoded forms contain a credential. Apply the same handling to both audit findings and publication diagnostics.

findings.suggestion: Also inspect rename destinations that introduce a path beneath a root hidden directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A round moves report.xml to .tmp-gate/report.xml; the diff reports R100 and no root-hidden-addition warning is produced.

verification.evidence: src/git/repos.ts:577 uses `diff("--name-status", "-M", range)`, enabling rename detection; src/git/repos.ts:1190 preserves the rename status and destination: `return b !== undefined ? { status, path: b, from: a } : { status, path: a };`. src/gates/audit.ts:292 restricts the warning to `if (f.status.startsWith("A"))`. test/gates.test.ts:1052 explicitly expects no warning for `["R100", ".tmp-gate/report.xml", false]`.
verification.trigger: Move an existing report.xml into .tmp-gate/report.xml without changing its content. Git reports R100, so the audit skips the root-hidden-addition warning and provides no corresponding round feedback.

candidates.title: An advisory alone never reaches an implementer before publication
candidates.detail: The new warnings are appended only when another implementation round already occurs. If gates, review, and verification pass, the pipeline proceeds toward publication without giving the implementer an opportunity to remove the scratch file. The added approve-case test explicitly expects only one implementation invocation. This leaves the reported failure mode intact when the scratch output itself does not provoke another round.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange a bounded advisory follow-up before publication when these warnings first appear, while allowing an intentional addition to remain without repeatedly triggering rounds.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementer adds .tmp-gate/report.xml containing output that exceeds the private text decoding limit; gates and review approve the change. No second implementation round runs, so publication still fails on the committed output.

candidates.title: Audit warnings use the cumulative diff rather than the current round
candidates.detail: The new warnings inspect the diff from the run's original base, so a file newly added in a later round can appear as a modification instead of an addition. In that case neither scratch warning fires, even though that round commits the file into publication history.
candidates.suggestion: Evaluate the new addition warnings against the current round's commit diff and preserve the cumulative diff for checks that need it.
candidates.failure_scenario: A tracked file exists at the base, an earlier round deletes it, and a later round recreates it under a root hidden directory with oversized scratch output. The cumulative diff reports M, so the new A-only checks produce no warning or next-round feedback.

candidates.title: Decode credential-bearing paths before redacting them
candidates.detail: The diagnostic redacts only literal credential variants. A percent-encoded credential in a path survives redactCredentials, and redactPrivate does not remove it unless it is also in the private-string list. The resulting publication error exposes the recoverable credential. The new test covers only a literal credential in the path.
candidates.suggestion: Decode or otherwise recognize encoded credential variants before emitting the path, and add a test using a percent-encoded registered credential.
candidates.failure_scenario: A file whose name contains a percent-encoded registered credential has content that triggers the decoding refusal; the error includes the encoded credential.

candidates.title: Identify files whose patch has no index line
candidates.detail: The diagnostic maps a patch section to a path only through its index line. Git omits that line for an empty-file addition and some mode-only changes, so a decoding refusal caused by such a filename falls through to the original generic error without a commit or path. The added tests exercise nonempty files and do not cover this case.
candidates.suggestion: Associate sections with raw diff records even when there is no index line, and test an empty file with a filename that exceeds the decoding limit.
candidates.failure_scenario: A commit adds an empty file whose name contains sufficiently nested percent encoding. Publication is refused, but the error remains 'Published content exceeds the private text decoding limit' without identifying the commit or path.

candidates.title: Encoded credentials in diagnosed paths escape redaction
candidates.detail: The new diagnostic passes the raw filename to `redactCredentials`, which only matches literal credential variants. `redactPrivate` checks encoded forms only against the private-strings entries, not registered credentials. The same issue affects the new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts`. An encoded credential can therefore be stored in an audit event, sent in round feedback, or included in a publication refusal.
candidates.suggestion: Decode or otherwise recognize encoded credential variants before emitting filenames, and redact the complete diagnostic before it reaches logs, events, or prompts. Cover both audit feedback and publication refusals.
candidates.failure_scenario: A registered credential `secret-token-value` appears in an added filename as `%73ecret-token-value`. A scratch warning or decoding-limit refusal includes that filename unchanged, disclosing a readily decodable credential.

candidates.title: Publication diagnostics preserve terminal control characters in filenames
candidates.detail: The diagnosed path is inserted into the refusal without stripping terminal control characters. Git permits such characters in filenames, so untrusted filenames can inject control sequences or forged lines into displayed or logged errors. The audit path uses `redactGateOutput`, which strips these characters, but the new publication diagnostic does not.
candidates.suggestion: Apply terminal-control normalization to the path before including it in the diagnostic, while retaining credential and private-string redaction.
candidates.failure_scenario: An added file whose name contains a newline or ANSI escape sequence also contains content exceeding the decoding limit. The resulting refusal displays the untrusted control sequence as part of its message.

candidates.title: Scratch warnings do not reach the implementer when the round otherwise passes
candidates.detail: The request says to “Feed it back to the implementer as round feedback, so the next round removes it before anything is published.” The warning is appended only when a later implementer invocation already happens. If gates, review, and verification pass, the run proceeds toward publication without giving the implementer a chance to remove the scratch file. The new approve-case test explicitly expects only one implementer invocation.
candidates.suggestion: Arrange an advisory follow-up that gives the implementer the warning before publication while allowing intentional additions to remain.
candidates.failure_scenario: The first round adds .tmp-gate/report.xml and all other checks pass; the warning is recorded, but the file remains in the commit and the implementer never receives it.

candidates.suggestion: Also inspect rename destinations that introduce a path beneath a root hidden directory.
candidates.failure_scenario: A round moves report.xml to .tmp-gate/report.xml; the diff reports R100 and no root-hidden-addition warning is produced.

findings.title: Publication checks omit registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only checks the entries supplied by callers. Production publication callers generally supply private strings, not registered credentials, so encoded credentials in published content remain undetected. The new test supplies credentials explicitly and therefore does not exercise the production call path.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected values used by publication checks, and test through a production publication entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential that is absent from private-strings.txt is base64-encoded in a committed file or PR text. The publication check receives only private entries and permits the encoded credential to be published.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2064 returns only `loadPrivateStrings(configDir, [cwd, ctx.repo.localPath, repos, work])`; :2085 passes those entries to `checkPublicationText(body, location, entries)`. src/gates/publication.ts:80 checks only `publicationMatches(text, entries)[0]`. src/gates/private.ts:157 decodes base64 only when `entries.some(({ value }) => found.includes(normalize(value)))`. findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before nested encodings can be inspected
findings.detail: base64Match returns decoded text only when that first decoded layer already contains a protected value. A base64 encoding of a percent-encoded credential, or a doubly base64-encoded credential, therefore remains unchanged and is accepted. The direct check `bun -e 'import {privateMatches} from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const e=[{value:"secret-credential",entry:1}]; for(const s of [Buffer.from("%73ecret-credential").toString("base64"),Buffer.from(Buffer.from("secret-credential").toString("base64")).toString("base64")]) console.log(s,JSON.stringify(privateMatches(s,e)));'` printed `JTczZWNyZXQtY3JlZGVudGlhbA== []` and `YzJWamNtVjBMV055WldSbGJuUnBZV3c9 []`.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding layers for eligible base64 runs before deciding that a run is unrelated, and cover nested encodings in filename and publication tests.
findings.failure_scenario: A filename or published text contains base64 of `%73ecret-credential`, with `secret-credential` registered as protected; the encoded value survives the check.

verification.evidence: src/gates/private.ts:155–159: `const plain = Buffer.from(run.slice(offset), "base64").toString(); const found = normalize(plain); if (entries.some(({ value }) => found.includes(normalize(value)))) return plain;` otherwise returns `undefined`. src/gates/private.ts:166–167 retains unmatched runs and stops when unchanged: `base64Match(run, entries) ?? run` and `if (next === text) return layers.map(normalize);`. A targeted runtime probe returned no matches for `JTczZWNyZXQtY3JlZGVudGlhbA==`, while matching its decoded `%73ecret-credential`.
verification.trigger: Register `secret-credential` and use base64 of `%73ecret-credential` in a filename or published text. The base64 result is rejected before percent decoding can inspect it, leaving the protected value undetected. Audit uses this matcher at src/gates/audit.ts:454; publication uses it at src/gates/publication.ts:74–81.

A targeted probe with `bun -e 'import {privateMatches} from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const value="synthetic-private-secret"; const e=[{value,entry:1}]; for (const t of [Buffer.from(value).toString("base64"),Buffer.from(Buffer.from(value).toString("base64")).toString("base64"),Buffer.from([...value].map(c=>"%"+c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16)).join("")).toString("base64")]) console.log(t,JSON.stringify(privateMatches(t,e)));'` returned a match for the first input and `[]` for both the double-base64 and base64-of-percent-encoded inputs.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded combinations of supported decoding layers before deciding that a base64 run is unrelated, while retaining a bounded failure-closed policy.

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:535-547: `combined` sums `costUsd` and all usage fields across results. src/evals/runner.ts:1115 calls `sendTo(request, to, ...)` for the verifier; :1139-1142 adds the combined result to trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:269-275 assigns those totals to `details.provider` and `t.model_id`; :172 reports `invocations: rows.length`.
verification.trigger: A review trial uses primary provider A and verifier B. Its combined spend and tokens become one statistical record attributed to A, omitting B's work.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 stores `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens`; :1173-1175 stores round evidence for implementation cases, including a single round. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 sets both cache metrics to `null` whenever `rounds?.length` is nonzero.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read and 20 cache-write tokens. Statistics discard both measurements and report null in its model and provider totals.

findings.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
findings.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, ...)`; :541-547 sums costs and tokens. src/evals/runner.ts:1139-1142 accumulates that result in trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:265-275 uses either round records or a fallback containing `provider: details.provider`, `modelId: String(t.model_id)` and the entire trial totals.
verification.trigger: A panel review iteration invokes reviewer A and verifier B. Both calls' totals are attributed to A, with no contribution for B. Review panels take the trial fallback rather than a persisted implementation-round record; the claimed attribution failure still occurs.

findings.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 accumulates cache totals in trial details across rounds. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 nevertheless sets `read` and `write` to null for round records; :291 consequently sets `inputTokens` to null. src/db/stats.ts:166-168 propagates any null measurement to the aggregate.
verification.trigger: A completed multi-round eval has stored trial-level cache totals. Its statistics discard those available totals, returning null for cache-read, cache-write and uncached input totals.

findings.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
findings.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
findings.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:931 persists `store.recordEvalTrial({ ...trial, status: "running" })` before invocation and scratch preparation at :1013 (`withScratch(cwd, ...)`). src/db/stats.ts:258 excludes zero-usage records only when `t.status === "skipped" || details.preparationFailed`; :271 falls back to `String(t.status)`. At :179-180, every record increments invocations and only `"ok"` counts as successful.
verification.trigger: Query statistics while a zero-usage eval trial is running before its first provider call: it contributes one unsuccessful invocation.

findings.title: Eval successful share can reflect grading failures instead of provider results
findings.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and aggregate the provider invocation status separately from the grading outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully, but its grading process times out. The eval provider statistics count the invocation as unsuccessful.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1209-1212 explicitly changes `roundEvidence.status` to the grading error or timeout even when `result.status === "ok"`. src/db/stats.ts:265-266 selects recorded rounds, :287 uses `status: r.status`, and :180 calculates success with `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: An implement invocation succeeds but grading times out or errors: its recorded round lowers the provider's successful share.

findings.title: Eval aggregation tests do not exercise runner-produced round evidence
findings.detail: The eval test constructs round records directly and assumes their status and duration describe provider calls. The runner can modify round status after grading and records duration through grading, so this fixture does not catch the resulting misclassification of provider success.
findings.suggestion: Add a test using runner-produced eval evidence where the provider succeeds but grading fails or times out, and assert the provider success share.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression or existing defect that treats a grading timeout as a failed provider invocation passes the manually seeded round test.

verification.evidence: test/provider-workload.test.ts:465–483 manually constructs rounds with `status: "ok"` and `status: "timeout"`, then :521–523 expects the timeout's `successfulShare: 0`. Runner-produced evidence differs: src/evals/runner.ts:1209–1212 changes a successful invocation's round status when grading fails: `if (result.status === "ok" && (grade?.implement?.reason === "error" || grade?.implement?.reason === "timeout")) roundEvidence.status = grade.implement.reason;`. src/db/stats.ts:287 consumes `status: r.status`, and :180 calculates success using `r.status === "ok"`.
verification.trigger: A provider invocation succeeds, but hidden grading times out. The runner persists a timeout round, so statistics count the successful provider call as unsuccessful. The manually seeded aggregation test passes without exercising this runner-to-statistics path.

findings.title: Multi-call eval trials are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: The request asks for workload “per provider and model” with “eval invocations shown separately.” A review eval can invoke multiple panel members or samples, including providers other than the trial target. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial, but this code attributes the entire combined record to the trial target and counts it once. The resulting provider, model, invocation-count, and success figures are misleading.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual persisted call evidence where available, and explicitly represent measurements that cannot be attributed from existing records rather than assigning all combined usage to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel eval invokes a target on provider A and a verifier on provider B. Its combined cost and tokens are reported as one invocation for A, while B receives no eval workload.

At :1139-1142 combined usage is added to trial totals. src/db/stats.ts:268-275 converts that trial into one record using `details.provider`, `t.model_id`, and the combined totals.
verification.trigger: A panel trial calls target provider A and verifier provider B: statistics attribute the combined tokens and cost to one trial invocation for A and omit B's workload.

findings.title: Eval rounds discard stored cached-token totals
findings.detail: The request requires input, output, and cached-token statistics. For every trial with rounds, this code sets both cache fields to null even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Because summarize returns null when any contributing value is unknown, one such trial makes the entire provider's eval cache and uncached-input totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial-level cache totals for aggregations where they can be attributed without double counting, and preserve unknown values only for breakdowns that cannot be reconstructed.
findings.failure_scenario: An implement eval has one recorded round and stored cacheReadTokens of 500. Its provider's eval totals report cacheReadTokens and inputTokens as null instead of reporting the available values.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143-1144 stores accumulated `cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens`, including for implement trials whose rounds are recorded at :1174-1175. src/db/stats.ts:280-281 sets both cache measurements to `null` whenever rounds exist; :291 consequently sets `inputTokens` to null.
verification.trigger: An implement trial has one recorded round and known cached-token totals: statistics discard the available cache measurements and report unknown cache and uncached input totals.

findings.title: Historical workload omits stored concierge calls
findings.detail: The request asks for long-term provider workload numbers computed from stored invocations. Historical production reads only the invocations table, while stored concierge calls live in chat_calls and are already counted by the existing provider workload calculation. Consequently the new long-term provider and model totals omit that work even when a provider appears in the legacy today and seven-day fields.
findings.suggestion: Include stored chat calls in the historical workload with an appropriate role and their stored model, status, usage, cost, and duration.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider has a completed concierge call and no pipeline invocations. Its existing today count is one, but the new production totals report zero invocations and zero usage.

verification.evidence: src/concierge.ts:331 persists completed concierge calls with `store.recordChatCall(...)`; src/db/store.ts:1015 stores provider, model, result, cost and timing in `chat_calls`. src/db/stats.ts:80 includes these calls in existing workload totals, but :241 reads historical production exclusively `FROM invocations`. At :312, production is aggregated only from that result.
verification.trigger: A provider has a completed concierge call but no pipeline invocations: existing today totals include it, while historical production reports zero invocations and usage, omitting stored provider workload.

findings.suggestion: Count individual calls when evidence supports it, or expose round counts separately without presenting them as invocation counts or invocation success rates.

findings.title: Missing durations are reported as zero total wall time
findings.detail: The duration aggregation silently drops unknown durations and returns the sum of the remaining values. If every duration is unknown, it reports zero milliseconds; if only some are unknown, it presents a partial sum as the total. This differs from the explicit unknown handling used for the other metrics.
findings.suggestion: Represent total wall time as unknown when any included duration is unavailable, or expose the measured count and clearly identify the sum as partial.
findings.failure_scenario: A provider has one unfinished invocation with no finished timestamp. Its historical totals report one invocation and zero milliseconds of total wall time even though its duration is unknown.

verification.evidence: src/db/stats.ts:240 derives `finished_at - started_at AS duration` without excluding unfinished invocations. src/db/stats.ts:174-175 removes unknown durations: `.flatMap((r) => (r.duration === null || !Number.isFinite(r.duration) ? [] : [Math.max(0, r.duration)]))`. src/db/stats.ts:193 then reports `wallTimeMs: durations.reduce((n, ms) => n + ms, 0)`.
verification.trigger: A provider's only invocation has no finished timestamp; it counts toward invocations but yields wallTimeMs of zero, presenting an unknown total as a measured zero.

findings.title: Cross-origin requests can trigger unbounded historical aggregation
findings.detail: The existing GET endpoint now synchronously loads and aggregates every stored invocation and eval trial when no cutoff is supplied. GET requests are exempt from the origin check, so a web page can repeatedly trigger this work against a local daemon even though it cannot read the response. As history grows, each request consumes increasing CPU and memory and blocks the daemon's event loop.
findings.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: A user with a large invocation history visits a page that repeatedly loads the local /api/stats/providers URL; each request runs the full historical aggregation and can make the daemon unresponsive.

verification.evidence: src/server/http.ts:225-237 excludes GET/HEAD from origin checks (`req.method !== "GET" && req.method !== "HEAD"`). src/config.ts:385 defaults token enforcement off: `requireApiToken: server.require_api_token === true`. src/server/http.ts:754-756 directly calls `computeProviderStatistics(store, since === null ? undefined : parseSince(since))`. src/db/stats.ts:232 defaults `since = -8_640_000_000_000_000`; lines 241-248 synchronously load matching invocations and eval trials with `.all(since)`.
verification.trigger: With API-token enforcement disabled, a page repeatedly issuing cross-origin GETs to the loopback endpoint can trigger synchronous full-history aggregation. A sufficiently large history could stall daemon processing; the responsiveness impact is plausible but unmeasured.

findings.title: Normalizing the log before redaction can expose credential fragments
findings.detail:
The excerpt is redacted after timestamps have been removed from every line. A registered multiline credential containing a timestamp at the start of a line no longer matches its registered value, so its remaining contents are published. A direct Bun probe with the credential `private-first
2026-10-05T00:00:00Z private-second` returned the excerpt `error: failure
private-first
private-second
(fail) test`.
findings.suggestion: Redact the original log before normalization, or preserve a mapping to the original text so credential matching happens before characters are removed.
findings.failure_scenario: A CI log contains a registered multiline credential with a timestamp-shaped line, followed by a failure; the fix trigger and feed publish the credential's other lines.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:64 removes timestamp-shaped prefixes with `line.replace(/^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\S+\s+/, "")` before publication redacts at :52. src/util/proc.ts:1115 registers only the original and CRLF-normalized credential variants: `[secret, secret.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")]`.
verification.trigger: A registered multiline credential contains a timestamp-shaped line. Normalization changes that credential before matching; a direct probe returned its unredacted middle and final lines in the excerpt, which is published and persisted.

findings.title: A later test failure can replace an unrelated earlier error
findings.detail: The search for a Bun test name crosses arbitrary lines until another recognized failure or passing test appears. For `error: build failed\nBuild stopped\n(fail) unrelated test`, the classifier selects `(fail) unrelated test`, even though the first failure is the build error. This can give the fix round the wrong signature and conflate different build errors.
findings.suggestion: Only associate an error block with a subsequent Bun failure when its intervening structure establishes that they belong together.
findings.failure_scenario: A job reports a build or setup error, then a separate test fails without an intervening passing-test line.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:87–89: `if (/^\s*error:/i.test(lines[start] ?? ""))` searches for the next failure or passing-test line, then `if (/^\s*\(fail\)/i.test(...)) index += 1 + next;`. There is no check associating the two errors.
verification.trigger: `error: build configuration missing\nsetup ended\n(fail) unrelated test` selects the unrelated test as its signature. The earlier build error remains in the excerpt but loses its signature identity.

findings.title: A long failing test line can disappear from its own excerpt
findings.detail: The tail window keeps the end of the block, so a sufficiently long `(fail)` line loses its beginning, including the test name. The command `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; const s=ciSignature("test", "error: assertion\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) important-test "+"y".repeat(2500), "fallback"); console.log(JSON.stringify({line:s.line.slice(0,40),excerptContainsName:s.excerpt.includes("important-test"),length:s.excerpt.length}));'` returned `{"line":"(fail) important-test yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy","excerptContainsName":false,"length":1999}`.
findings.suggestion: Reserve excerpt space for the beginning of the selected signature line as well as the preceding diagnostic context.
findings.failure_scenario: A Bun assertion produces a long diff and its failing test line exceeds the remaining excerpt budget.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts:107 takes the trailing window with `window(start + 1, index + 1, Math.max(0, 1999 - head.length), true)`. At :98, that window starts at `Math.max(left, right - limit)`, even inside the chosen failure line.
verification.trigger: An assertion and long diff precede a failing test line longer than the remaining excerpt budget. A probe with a 2,218-character failure line retained only its trailing characters; the excerpt omitted `(fail)` and the test name.

findings.title: Publication padding bypasses exact-match redaction for short credentials
findings.detail: Credentials shorter than eight characters are redacted only when the entire input equals the credential. The new publication helper passes surrounding log text to redaction, so an image value that previously was redacted independently can be published and persisted in the signature. A direct probe registering "short" and a longer credential, then classifying "Image: short\nerror: fail", returned image "short".

verification.trigger: Register short credential `q7z` and another longer credential, then inspect `Image: q7z\n(fail) actual`. Padding defeats exact matching, leaving `q7z` in the returned image and signature and persisted CI record. The feed image receives another redaction, but storage and the composite signature remain exposed.

findings.detail: The new excerpt and signature paths redact the normalized log after ANSI stripping and timestamp removal. A registered credential containing text removed by normalization no longer matches its registered value, so the remaining credential material is published. A direct probe with a credential containing an ANSI escape returned both credential fragments concatenated in the signature and excerpt.
