Verifier: 18 candidates, 18 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Rollback to the previous release does not notify the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the database setting written by this new daemon. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the new release SHA in place. A running new executor continues its job and can continue leasing queued jobs even though the active daemon is now the older release.
findings.suggestion: Use release ownership that the previous release can invalidate or otherwise ensure that a rollback stops the executor before the old daemon resumes work.
findings.failure_scenario: Start an in-place gate on this release, then roll back and start the base-commit daemon. The setting still names this release, so the executor does not cancel the gate as required.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 adds `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha);`; the base version's startup instead proceeds directly to `detachSlots = await attachSlotPools(...)` (base src/cli/daemon.ts:50), without updating that setting. src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes only through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`; otherwise lines 53–57 renew the lease. src/db/workers.ts:388–391 likewise permits leasing when that persisted setting and the request match the executor's release. Rollback restores `previous` and restarts it at src/cli/service.ts:778–782.
verification.trigger: With executor enabled and a gate running, roll back to the base daemon while leaving the executor alive. With no LAN worker traffic to invalidate the job, the persisted release setting remains the newer SHA, so the executor continues the gate and can lease queued newer-release jobs despite the daemon running another release.

findings.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp. An executor whose event loop is stalled remains eligible indefinitely. Once its lease expires, the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits indefinitely while that process exists, so it cannot fall back or proceed with the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, safe path for confirming that an unresponsive executor's gate processes have stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is alive but paused or blocked while running a gate. Its lease expires; the daemon enters waitStopped and never completes the gate or starts the fallback.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 accepts executor liveness solely through `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. Lease expiry calls `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")` (src/db/workers.ts:671–672). The attached daemon then executes `if (inplace) await workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:131). Recovery inside waitStopped requires `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)` (src/db/workers.ts:370); otherwise it repeatedly sleeps (line 384).
verification.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, a leased executor remains alive but indefinitely stops progressing. Its lease expires, yet its process identity still matches, so the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped rather than completing or falling back. A temporary pause delays recovery until the executor resumes.

findings.title: Targeted and timeout retry jobs cannot reattach
findings.detail: The resume predicate explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted or timeout retry therefore cancels the still-running job and repeats work instead of attaching to its matching handle.
findings.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to validate and reattach matching retry jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is leased by the executor. On resume, the purpose fails this allowlist and the retry is cancelled or started again.

verification.evidence: src/app.ts:184-186 selects gateExecutorFor(..., cfg.executorEnabled); src/gates/executor.ts:78 selects the in-place executor when enabled. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1566 runs purpose "timeout", and :1592-1595 runs "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 persists each purpose and handle. On resumed stage entry, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 calls resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", ...). src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires 'pending.purpose === purpose' and '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'; :35-43 cancels and clears rejected handles. src/gates/lan.ts:45-49 implements discard with 'workers.cancel(handle.id)' and 'await workers.waitStopped(handle.id)'.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and alive, restart the daemon during a targeted regression retry or timeout retry. The resumed gates stage rejects and cancels the surviving retry, then starts initial gates again instead of attaching to its result.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback
findings.detail: When the gate executor is configured as LAN, this factory always returns the LAN executor, even when the in-place executor is enabled. Its local path for repositories outside the LAN list runs directly in the daemon, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local path through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the executor, configure LAN gates for one repository, and run a gate in another repository. The gate runs in the daemon and is lost on restart despite a live in-place executor.

verification.evidence: src/app.ts:186 passes both settings: `gateExecutorFor(cfg.gateExecutor, this.workers, cfg.workers.repos, cfg.executorEnabled)`. However, src/gates/executor.ts:79–81 handles LAN configuration with `case "lan": ... return lanExecutor(workers, repos);`, ignoring the in-place flag. src/gates/lan.ts:16 defaults `inplace = false`, line 17 creates `const local = localExecutor();`, and line 71 routes unlisted repositories directly to it: `else if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal);`. Normal baseline execution reaches this executor through src/pipeline/engine.ts:648 (`runGateExecution(...)`) and src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:63–83 (`const executor = ctx.deps.gateExecutor; ... executeGate(..., executor, ...)`). The local executor runs checks inside the daemon at src/gates/executor.ts:130–133 and aborts them on cancellation at lines 116–120.
verification.trigger: Set gates.executor="lan", executor.enabled=true, and workers.repos to one repository; run gates for another repository while a fresh in-place executor is available. Those gates run inside the daemon instead of becoming durable in-place jobs, so a daemon restart interrupts them and requires repeated work.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into local retries
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from executeGate and records an ordinary failed job. The attaching daemon then reruns every failed in-place job locally. This loses the distinction between an infrastructure failure and a ConfinementError, so a failed isolation check can be followed by a successful gate instead of failing closed.
findings.suggestion: Persist a failure classification and propagate confinement and inspection failures to the daemon without retrying them.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement preflight throws ConfinementError, but the daemon's subsequent local preflight succeeds; the gate passes despite the original security check failing.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71 catches every error: `catch (error) { workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error))); }`. src/db/workers.ts:626–632 marks in-place failures `state='failed'` without preserving an error classification. src/gates/lan.ts:130–139 handles every failed job by starting `local.start(request, controller.signal)`. Successful fallback overwrites the job with a completed result at src/gates/lan.ts:149. Confinement preflight explicitly throws `ConfinementError` at src/harness/sandbox.ts:199–200 and :244.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled, its confinement preflight throws; after cleanup, the daemon retries locally. If that preflight and the checks succeed, the gate returns success despite the original confinement failure. The differing preflight outcomes are conditional; their frequency is not established.

findings.title: A cleanup failure can leave the run waiting indefinitely
findings.detail: waitStopped only attempts recovery or reports an error after the executor process disappears. If a job finishes with process discovery or cleanup records remaining, the executor deliberately leaves stopped=0 but continues running. waitStopped then polls forever because the executor is still alive, even though that executor will never revisit the completed job.
findings.suggestion: Make the executor publish a terminal cleanup failure, or have waitStopped detect that the job is no longer being cleaned up and fail closed with a clear error.
findings.failure_scenario: A cancelled gate leaves a cleanup record after process cleanup fails; the executor continues polling for other jobs, while the daemon waits forever to start the replacement gate.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:995–1002 turns failed process termination into a rejected `ProcessTerminationError`. The executor catches errors with `workers.fail(job.id, ...)` (src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71), but sets stopped only when both discovery and cleanup lists are empty (lines 75–80), then continues its polling loop (lines 29–33). src/db/workers.ts:370 permits recovery only when the owning executor is absent; a live owner instead causes repeated sleep (line 384). Replacement startup calls `workers.cancel(j.id); await workers.waitStopped(j.id, signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:58–59).
verification.trigger: A cancellation encounters a process cleanup failure that leaves persisted discovery or cleanup records. The executor remains alive and polls for other jobs without retrying that cleanup or acknowledging stopped. The daemon indefinitely waits to start the replacement gate, even if the residual processes subsequently exit.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic across concurrent starts
findings.detail: The query for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations. Two daemon-side starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue independently. With two executor processes, each can lease one job and run both gates in the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity atomically in the database when creating or leasing an in-place job.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent gate starts for the same cwd pass the existing-job query before either enqueues, and two executors lease their jobs concurrently.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:54-59 queries existing jobs by cwd and waits for them, but src/gates/lan.ts:72 then yields at `await releaseGateSlotScope()` before creating a handle. Enqueue happens later in attach: `workers.enqueue(req, handle.id, true)` (src/gates/lan.ts:80-81). src/gates/executor.ts:200-204 additionally awaits `persist(handle)` between start and attach. Thus concurrent starts can both observe no job before either inserts one. Leasing checks only the individual job: `WHERE id=? AND state='queued'` (src/db/workers.ts:400), with no cwd exclusion. Each executor independently calls `workers.leaseInplace(owner)` (src/gates/inplace.ts:29-30).
verification.trigger: Two concurrent starts with the same cwd both finish the existing-job query before either attaches. Both subsequently enqueue distinct jobs; with two executor processes and sufficient gate capacity, both jobs can run in the same worktree simultaneously. Concurrent same-cwd callers are not established as a normal pipeline occurrence, so severity is medium.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A durable in-place handle for a targeted retry is therefore cancelled even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and lease all match. The retry is restarted instead of receiving the surviving job's result.
findings.suggestion: Provide a resume path for targeted retry purposes and preserve the state needed to resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is running; resume rejects its matching handle, cancels the executor job, and runs the retry again.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:301-318 invokes the retry runner with '{ targeted: true, skipGateSlot }' when retryFiles and valid failed files exist. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1595 maps this to "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 persists that purpose. On resume, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 requests "initial"; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires matching purpose and allows only '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]'. Lines 35-43 cancel the rejected job and clear its handle; src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 starts initial gates again.
verification.trigger: An enabled, live in-place executor runs a targeted retry for valid reported failed files, and the daemon restarts before it finishes. Recovery cancels the retry and repeats gate work.

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness check
findings.detail: Executor availability is based only on PID and birth identity; the executors table has no heartbeat timestamp. A live but stalled executor is treated as available indefinitely. New gates are enqueued instead of immediately using the requested in-process fallback, and a leased job is not considered disconnected until its lease expires.
findings.suggestion: Record and renew an executor heartbeat and require it to be fresh when selecting an executor and sweeping its jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops making progress; the daemon treats it as available and waits for pickup or lease expiry rather than recognizing that no fresh executor is available.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:351–363 checks release and process birth, including `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`, without a heartbeat freshness check. src/gates/lan.ts:61 uses `if (!workers.executor())` to select immediate in-process fallback. Otherwise the job is enqueued on attachment (lines 82–83), and queued jobs fail only after the pickup timer: `now - Math.max(j.updated_at, resumedAt) >= this.times.pickup` (src/db/workers.ts:656–657).
verification.trigger: With executor support enabled, an executor process remains alive but its event loop stops progressing. The daemon treats it as available and queues work instead of immediately falling back; an unleased job waits for pickup timeout, while an already leased job can become stuck awaiting stopped.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs are cancelled on restart instead of reattached
findings.detail: Resume accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A recorded `baseline-retry-targeted` or `regression-retry-targeted` handle therefore fails the resume check even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and executor lease match. The live job is cancelled and the stage starts over, contrary to the requested restart behavior for targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry state to resume the targeted retry and accept its matching handle during stage recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a long targeted regression retry; the new engine cancels that job and repeats gate work instead of receiving its result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1583-1605 calls retryRegressions and dispatches targeted retries through runGateExecution with purpose "regression-retry-targeted" (:1595). src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 saves the purpose and handle. Resumed stage entry calls resumeGateExecution with "initial" (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536). Its guard requires matching purpose and '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)' (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30), then cancels and clears a rejected handle (:35-43). Initial execution follows at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547.
verification.trigger: The daemon restarts while an in-place targeted regression retry is running. Even with the same round, SHA, environment and executor release, recovery cancels the recorded job and repeats gates instead of receiving its result.

findings.title: Restart coverage omits targeted retries
findings.detail: The engine restart cases cover baseline, initial, and rebase gates, but none interrupts a targeted baseline or regression retry. Consequently the tests do not catch the resume-purpose restriction that cancels those jobs.
findings.suggestion: Add a restart test that pauses a targeted retry, resumes the engine, and asserts that the same job completes and its command ran once.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry is running when the daemon stops; the current suite passes without checking whether the resumed engine reattaches to it.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:487–494 enumerates only "baseline", "initial", and "rebase" restart cases. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 creates "regression-retry-targeted", but src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:30 permits resume only for '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'.
verification.trigger: Restart during an in-place targeted retry: the tests never exercise reattachment to that retry and therefore miss its cancellation and repeated work.

findings.title: Pickup timeout test never verifies in-process fallback
findings.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that the queued job becomes failed. It does not attach a daemon-side execution or assert that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
findings.suggestion: Exercise an attached in-place job that is never leased, sweep it past pickup timeout, and assert that the local check runs and its result reaches the caller.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor remains alive but does not pick up a queued job, and the daemon fails to start the local fallback after the sweep marks it failed.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:319–323 enqueues 'missed', calls 'later.sweep()', and asserts only state "failed" and attempt 1. It never attaches or awaits a gate result. The fallback implementation is separately in src/gates/lan.ts:130–139: 'if (job.state === "failed")' then 'await local.start(request, controller.signal)'.
verification.trigger: An executor leaves a job queued until pickup timeout. This test passes after the sweep even if attachment never starts the in-process fallback.

findings.title: Gate result comparison discards most of the result shape
findings.detail: The purported in-process comparison projects each result down to name, ok, and exitCode, while the event assertion checks only names. It would still pass if executor results or events lost output, command, timing, failure metadata, or other fields required by consumers. The test also does not compare the produced gate artifacts.
findings.suggestion: Compare representative complete result and event structures, excluding only nondeterministic values, and verify the corresponding artifact contents.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor drops a check's output or failure metadata while preserving its name and exit code; this test still passes although the reported gate data changed.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:114–115 reduces results with 'map(({ name, ok, exitCode }) => ({ name, ok, exitCode }))'; line 144 compares only these projections. Line 146 checks output for the environment check alone, and lines 152–154 compare event result names alone.
verification.trigger: The executor loses another check's output or failure metadata while preserving name, ok, and exitCode; the result-equivalence assertion still passes.

findings.title: Executor stores gate output without the daemon’s dynamic credential registrations
findings.detail: Credential registrations are process-local. The executor loads configured provider credentials, but it does not receive credentials registered dynamically by the daemon, such as GitHub installation tokens and worker tokens. It redacts and persists check events and results using its own incomplete registry before the daemon sees them, so the daemon’s later redaction cannot remove the copies already stored in gate_jobs.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the executor has the daemon’s complete current redaction set before processing output, or defer persistence of output to a boundary that has that set while preserving restart-safe event handling.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon registers a GitHub installation token during operation, and a gate prints that token. An in-place executor that never registered the token stores it unredacted in the job’s events or result.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:23 obtains a token through `githubToken(signal)`; src/integrations/github-token.ts:18 calls `registerCredential("GH_TOKEN", token)`. Registrations live in process-local sets (`const credentialValues = new Set<string>()`, src/util/proc.ts:1217). The separate executor starts with `runInplaceExecutor(loadConfig(), sha, controller.signal)` at src/cli/main.ts:426, with no registration transfer. It writes check events through `workers.event(...)` at src/gates/inplace.ts:65 and results through `workers.complete(...)` at :69. Those persist `this.sanitize(event)` and `this.sanitize(run)` at src/db/workers.ts:612–613 and :717, using the executor's redactor.
verification.trigger: The daemon dynamically registers a GitHub credential that the executor has never registered. If gate output contains that credential, the executor persists it unredacted in gate_jobs events/results. Later daemon-side redaction cannot undo the stored disclosure.

findings.title: Confinement derives credential paths from the executor environment
findings.detail: The gate receives the daemon’s saved environment, but the executor constructs its read policy from its own process environment. The policy uses environment variables such as AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, GH_CONFIG_DIR, and CARGO_HOME to deny credential paths. When those variables differ between the daemon and executor, a credential path known to the daemon can be omitted from the executor’s deny list, weakening the confinement applied to untrusted gate commands.
findings.suggestion: Build the gate’s confinement policy from the same trusted environment used by the daemon, including its credential-path variables, and refuse execution if that policy cannot be reconstructed.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon has AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointing to a credential file under an otherwise allowed toolchain path, while the executor lacks that variable. A gate can read the file through the in-place executor even though the daemon’s local confinement would deny it.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:27 installs the executor's `readPolicyScope.run(cfg.readPolicy, ...)`. That policy captures its own `process.env` at src/harness/read-policy.ts:44–62. `homeReadPolicy` uses `options.environment ?? process.env` at :144 and derives credential denies from `env.AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` at :169. Toolchain allowances come from `options.toolchains` at :204; overlap with known credentials throws at :209–212. Although the executor forwards `req.env` to gate execution (src/gates/inplace.ts:64), it never installs the daemon's read policy.
verification.trigger: The daemon names a custom credential file through AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, while the executor lacks that variable. If the file lies within an executor-readable toolchain path and is not otherwise denied, the executor permits reading it. The daemon's own policy would identify the credential path and refuse the overlapping allowance. This depends on an unusual environment/path configuration.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The request says the local executor covers “the targeted retry” and that a resumed stage with the same stage, round, purpose and SHA attaches to its job. The purpose whitelist excludes both regression retry purposes and baseline retry purposes. On resume, the surrounding stage first asks to resume its initial gate, so it cancels the still-running retry and starts the stage's gate work again.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the recorded retry at its original point, and include its purpose in the resume validation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage treats the handle as a mismatch, cancels the retry and reruns gate work instead of receiving that job's result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 uses 'options?.targeted ? "regression-retry-targeted" : "regression-retry"'; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 checkpoints this purpose with its handle. Recovery enters src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 with purpose "initial". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires 'pending.purpose === purpose' and restricts resumable purposes to '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]'. Its rejection path cancels the execution and clears state (:35-43); src/gates/lan.ts:45-49 cancels the database job and waits for it to stop.
verification.trigger: Restart during a surviving in-place regression-retry-targeted job. The resumed stage treats its handle as a mismatch, cancels it, and reruns initial gates and any subsequent retries.

findings.title: Executor liveness is process existence, not a fresh heartbeat
findings.detail: The request requires fallback when no executor has a fresh heartbeat and requires the sweep to apply freshness timers against that heartbeat. Executor rows contain no heartbeat timestamp; this method only checks whether the PID and birth time still exist. In addition, `waitStopped` waits indefinitely while that process exists, even after its job lease expires.
findings.suggestion: Record and check a bounded executor heartbeat, and make the stop/fallback path handle an unresponsive owner without assuming that process existence proves progress or safe cleanup.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process becomes unresponsive while its gate is running. Its lease expires, but the daemon regards the executor as alive and waits indefinitely for `stopped` rather than reaching a safe fallback.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 defines liveness as `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. The sweep marks expired in-place leases failed (lines 667–672), and src/gates/lan.ts:131 waits for stopped before fallback. In waitStopped, `if (!worker || !this.executor(worker, false))` guards process recovery (src/db/workers.ts:370); a matching live process instead reaches `await Bun.sleep(this.times.tick)` (line 384), with no deadline.
verification.trigger: An in-place executor becomes indefinitely unresponsive while retaining its process identity. Once its lease expires, the daemon enters waitStopped, but neither recovers its processes nor reaches fallback until the executor resumes or exits. This is the same underlying defect as C2.

findings.title: Rollback to an older release does not notify the executor
findings.detail: The request says that when the daemon's release changes, including a rollback, the executor stops leasing and cancels its running jobs. The release marker is written only by this new daemon code. A rollback to the previous release starts a daemon that does not write that marker, so the executor continues to see its own SHA in the database and does not detect the release change.
findings.suggestion: Use a release identity that remains observable across rollback to the previous release, and test an actual old-daemon/new-executor transition.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release executor is running a gate when deployment rolls back to the base release. The old daemon starts without updating `executor.daemonRelease`, and the executor continues running and leasing as though its daemon release had not changed.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces the only daemon-release notification: `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha);`; base src/cli/daemon.ts:50 starts with `detachSlots = await attachSlotPools(...)` and never writes it. The executor checks `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha` (src/gates/inplace.ts:39), renewing unchanged leases at lines 53–57. New leases use the same stale setting at src/db/workers.ts:388–396. src/cli/service.ts:778–782 restores and restarts the previous release without updating the setting.
verification.trigger: A newer-release executor survives rollback to the base daemon while running a gate. Without LAN worker traffic invalidating its job, it sees its own SHA still recorded as the daemon release, continues running, and remains eligible to lease matching queued jobs. This is the same defect as C1.

candidates.title: Rollback to the previous release does not notify the executor
candidates.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the database setting written by this new daemon. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the new release SHA in place. A running new executor continues its job and can continue leasing queued jobs even though the active daemon is now the older release.
candidates.suggestion: Use release ownership that the previous release can invalidate or otherwise ensure that a rollback stops the executor before the old daemon resumes work.
candidates.failure_scenario: Start an in-place gate on this release, then roll back and start the base-commit daemon. The setting still names this release, so the executor does not cancel the gate as required.

candidates.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
candidates.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp. An executor whose event loop is stalled remains eligible indefinitely. Once its lease expires, the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits indefinitely while that process exists, so it cannot fall back or proceed with the worktree.
candidates.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, safe path for confirming that an unresponsive executor's gate processes have stopped.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor is alive but paused or blocked while running a gate. Its lease expires; the daemon enters waitStopped and never completes the gate or starts the fallback.

candidates.title: Targeted and timeout retry jobs cannot reattach
candidates.detail: The resume predicate explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted or timeout retry therefore cancels the still-running job and repeats work instead of attaching to its matching handle.
candidates.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to validate and reattach matching retry jobs.
candidates.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is leased by the executor. On resume, the purpose fails this allowlist and the retry is cancelled or started again.

candidates.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback
candidates.detail: When the gate executor is configured as LAN, this factory always returns the LAN executor, even when the in-place executor is enabled. Its local path for repositories outside the LAN list runs directly in the daemon, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart.
candidates.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local path through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
candidates.failure_scenario: Enable the executor, configure LAN gates for one repository, and run a gate in another repository. The gate runs in the daemon and is lost on restart despite a live in-place executor.

candidates.title: Confinement failures are converted into local retries
candidates.detail: The executor catches every error from executeGate and records an ordinary failed job. The attaching daemon then reruns every failed in-place job locally. This loses the distinction between an infrastructure failure and a ConfinementError, so a failed isolation check can be followed by a successful gate instead of failing closed.
candidates.suggestion: Persist a failure classification and propagate confinement and inspection failures to the daemon without retrying them.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement preflight throws ConfinementError, but the daemon's subsequent local preflight succeeds; the gate passes despite the original security check failing.

The release marker is written only by this new daemon code. A rollback to the previous release starts a daemon that does not write that marker, so the executor continues to see its own SHA in the database and does not detect the release change.
candidates.suggestion: Use a release identity that remains observable across rollback to the previous release, and test an actual old-daemon/new-executor transition.
candidates.failure_scenario: A new-release executor is running a gate when deployment rolls back to the base release. The old daemon starts without updating `executor.daemonRelease`, and the executor continues running and leasing as though its daemon release had not changed.

verdicts.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 adds `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha);`; the base version's startup instead proceeds directly to `detachSlots = await attachSlotPools(...)` (base src/cli/daemon.ts:50), without updating that setting. src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes only through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`; otherwise lines 53–57 renew the lease. src/db/workers.ts:388–391 likewise permits leasing when that persisted setting and the request match the executor's release. Rollback restores `previous` and restarts it at src/cli/service.ts:778–782.
verdicts.trigger: With executor enabled and a gate running, roll back to the base daemon while leaving the executor alive. With no LAN worker traffic to invalidate the job, the persisted release setting remains the newer SHA, so the executor continues the gate and can lease queued newer-release jobs despite the daemon running another release.

verdicts.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces the only daemon-release notification: `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha);`; base src/cli/daemon.ts:50 starts with `detachSlots = await attachSlotPools(...)` and never writes it. The executor checks `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha` (src/gates/inplace.ts:39), renewing unchanged leases at lines 53–57. New leases use the same stale setting at src/db/workers.ts:388–396. src/cli/service.ts:778–782 restores and restarts the previous release without updating the setting.
verdicts.trigger: A newer-release executor survives rollback to the base daemon while running a gate. Without LAN worker traffic invalidating its job, it sees its own SHA still recorded as the daemon release, continues running, and remains eligible to lease matching queued jobs. This is the same defect as C1.

verdicts.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 accepts executor liveness solely through `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. Lease expiry calls `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")` (src/db/workers.ts:671–672). The attached daemon then executes `if (inplace) await workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:131). Recovery inside waitStopped requires `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)` (src/db/workers.ts:370); otherwise it repeatedly sleeps (line 384).
verdicts.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, a leased executor remains alive but indefinitely stops progressing. Its lease expires, yet its process identity still matches, so the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped rather than completing or falling back. A temporary pause delays recovery until the executor resumes.

verdicts.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:995–1002 turns failed process termination into a rejected `ProcessTerminationError`. The executor catches errors with `workers.fail(job.id, ...)` (src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71), but sets stopped only when both discovery and cleanup lists are empty (lines 75–80), then continues its polling loop (lines 29–33). src/db/workers.ts:370 permits recovery only when the owning executor is absent; a live owner instead causes repeated sleep (line 384). Replacement startup calls `workers.cancel(j.id); await workers.waitStopped(j.id, signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:58–59).
verdicts.trigger: A cancellation encounters a process cleanup failure that leaves persisted discovery or cleanup records. The executor remains alive and polls for other jobs without retrying that cleanup or acknowledging stopped. The daemon indefinitely waits to start the replacement gate, even if the residual processes subsequently exit.

verdicts.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:351–363 checks release and process birth, including `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`, without a heartbeat freshness check. src/gates/lan.ts:61 uses `if (!workers.executor())` to select immediate in-process fallback. Otherwise the job is enqueued on attachment (lines 82–83), and queued jobs fail only after the pickup timer: `now - Math.max(j.updated_at, resumedAt) >= this.times.pickup` (src/db/workers.ts:656–657).
verdicts.trigger: With executor support enabled, an executor process remains alive but its event loop stops progressing. The daemon treats it as available and queues work instead of immediately falling back; an unleased job waits for pickup timeout, while an already leased job can become stuck awaiting stopped.

verdicts.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 defines liveness as `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. The sweep marks expired in-place leases failed (lines 667–672), and src/gates/lan.ts:131 waits for stopped before fallback. In waitStopped, `if (!worker || !this.executor(worker, false))` guards process recovery (src/db/workers.ts:370); a matching live process instead reaches `await Bun.sleep(this.times.tick)` (line 384), with no deadline.
verdicts.trigger: An in-place executor becomes indefinitely unresponsive while retaining its process identity. Once its lease expires, the daemon enters waitStopped, but neither recovers its processes nor reaches fallback until the executor resumes or exits. This is the same underlying defect as C2.

verdicts.evidence: src/app.ts:184-186 selects gateExecutorFor(..., cfg.executorEnabled); src/gates/executor.ts:78 selects the in-place executor when enabled. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1566 runs purpose "timeout", and :1592-1595 runs "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 persists each purpose and handle. On resumed stage entry, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 calls resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", ...). src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires 'pending.purpose === purpose' and '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'; :35-43 cancels and clears rejected handles. src/gates/lan.ts:45-49 implements discard with 'workers.cancel(handle.id)' and 'await workers.waitStopped(handle.id)'.
verdicts.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and alive, restart the daemon during a targeted regression retry or timeout retry. The resumed gates stage rejects and cancels the surviving retry, then starts initial gates again instead of attaching to its result.

verdicts.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:301-318 invokes the retry runner with '{ targeted: true, skipGateSlot }' when retryFiles and valid failed files exist. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1595 maps this to "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 persists that purpose. On resume, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 requests "initial"; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires matching purpose and allows only '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]'. Lines 35-43 cancel the rejected job and clear its handle; src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 starts initial gates again.
verdicts.trigger: An enabled, live in-place executor runs a targeted retry for valid reported failed files, and the daemon restarts before it finishes. Recovery cancels the retry and repeats gate work.

verdicts.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1583-1605 calls retryRegressions and dispatches targeted retries through runGateExecution with purpose "regression-retry-targeted" (:1595). src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 saves the purpose and handle. Resumed stage entry calls resumeGateExecution with "initial" (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536). Its guard requires matching purpose and '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)' (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30), then cancels and clears a rejected handle (:35-43). Initial execution follows at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547.
verdicts.trigger: The daemon restarts while an in-place targeted regression retry is running. Even with the same round, SHA, environment and executor release, recovery cancels the recorded job and repeats gates instead of receiving its result.

verdicts.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 uses 'options?.targeted ? "regression-retry-targeted" : "regression-retry"'; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 checkpoints this purpose with its handle. Recovery enters src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 with purpose "initial". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires 'pending.purpose === purpose' and restricts resumable purposes to '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]'. Its rejection path cancels the execution and clears state (:35-43); src/gates/lan.ts:45-49 cancels the database job and waits for it to stop.
verdicts.trigger: Restart during a surviving in-place regression-retry-targeted job. The resumed stage treats its handle as a mismatch, cancels it, and reruns initial gates and any subsequent retries.

verdicts.evidence: src/app.ts:186 passes both settings: `gateExecutorFor(cfg.gateExecutor, this.workers, cfg.workers.repos, cfg.executorEnabled)`. However, src/gates/executor.ts:79–81 handles LAN configuration with `case "lan": ... return lanExecutor(workers, repos);`, ignoring the in-place flag. src/gates/lan.ts:16 defaults `inplace = false`, line 17 creates `const local = localExecutor();`, and line 71 routes unlisted repositories directly to it: `else if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal);`. Normal baseline execution reaches this executor through src/pipeline/engine.ts:648 (`runGateExecution(...)`) and src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:63–83 (`const executor = ctx.deps.gateExecutor; ... executeGate(..., executor, ...)`). The local executor runs checks inside the daemon at src/gates/executor.ts:130–133 and aborts them on cancellation at lines 116–120.
verdicts.trigger: Set gates.executor="lan", executor.enabled=true, and workers.repos to one repository; run gates for another repository while a fresh in-place executor is available. Those gates run inside the daemon instead of becoming durable in-place jobs, so a daemon restart interrupts them and requires repeated work.

verdicts.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71 catches every error: `catch (error) { workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error))); }`. src/db/workers.ts:626–632 marks in-place failures `state='failed'` without preserving an error classification. src/gates/lan.ts:130–139 handles every failed job by starting `local.start(request, controller.signal)`. Successful fallback overwrites the job with a completed result at src/gates/lan.ts:149. Confinement preflight explicitly throws `ConfinementError` at src/harness/sandbox.ts:199–200 and :244.
verdicts.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled, its confinement preflight throws; after cleanup, the daemon retries locally. If that preflight and the checks succeed, the gate returns success despite the original confinement failure. The differing preflight outcomes are conditional; their frequency is not established.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:23 obtains a token through `githubToken(signal)`; src/integrations/github-token.ts:18 calls `registerCredential("GH_TOKEN", token)`. Registrations live in process-local sets (`const credentialValues = new Set<string>()`, src/util/proc.ts:1217). The separate executor starts with `runInplaceExecutor(loadConfig(), sha, controller.signal)` at src/cli/main.ts:426, with no registration transfer. It writes check events through `workers.event(...)` at src/gates/inplace.ts:65 and results through `workers.complete(...)` at :69. Those persist `this.sanitize(event)` and `this.sanitize(run)` at src/db/workers.ts:612–613 and :717, using the executor's redactor.
verdicts.trigger: The daemon dynamically registers a GitHub credential that the executor has never registered. If gate output contains that credential, the executor persists it unredacted in gate_jobs events/results. Later daemon-side redaction cannot undo the stored disclosure.

verdicts.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:27 installs the executor's `readPolicyScope.run(cfg.readPolicy, ...)`. That policy captures its own `process.env` at src/harness/read-policy.ts:44–62. `homeReadPolicy` uses `options.environment ?? process.env` at :144 and derives credential denies from `env.AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` at :169. Toolchain allowances come from `options.toolchains` at :204; overlap with known credentials throws at :209–212. Although the executor forwards `req.env` to gate execution (src/gates/inplace.ts:64), it never installs the daemon's read policy.
verdicts.trigger: The daemon names a custom credential file through AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, while the executor lacks that variable. If the file lies within an executor-readable toolchain path and is not otherwise denied, the executor permits reading it. The daemon's own policy would identify the credential path and refuse the overlapping allowance. This depends on an unusual environment/path configuration.

verdicts.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:54-59 queries existing jobs by cwd and waits for them, but src/gates/lan.ts:72 then yields at `await releaseGateSlotScope()` before creating a handle. Enqueue happens later in attach: `workers.enqueue(req, handle.id, true)` (src/gates/lan.ts:80-81). src/gates/executor.ts:200-204 additionally awaits `persist(handle)` between start and attach. Thus concurrent starts can both observe no job before either inserts one. Leasing checks only the individual job: `WHERE id=? AND state='queued'` (src/db/workers.ts:400), with no cwd exclusion. Each executor independently calls `workers.leaseInplace(owner)` (src/gates/inplace.ts:29-30).
verdicts.trigger: Two concurrent starts with the same cwd both finish the existing-job query before either attaches. Both subsequently enqueue distinct jobs; with two executor processes and sufficient gate capacity, both jobs can run in the same worktree simultaneously. Concurrent same-cwd callers are not established as a normal pipeline occurrence, so severity is medium.

verdicts.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:487–494 enumerates only "baseline", "initial", and "rebase" restart cases. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 creates "regression-retry-targeted", but src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:30 permits resume only for '["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)'.
verdicts.trigger: Restart during an in-place targeted retry: the tests never exercise reattachment to that retry and therefore miss its cancellation and repeated work.

verdicts.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:319–323 enqueues 'missed', calls 'later.sweep()', and asserts only state "failed" and attempt 1. It never attaches or awaits a gate result. The fallback implementation is separately in src/gates/lan.ts:130–139: 'if (job.state === "failed")' then 'await local.start(request, controller.signal)'.
verdicts.trigger: An executor leaves a job queued until pickup timeout. This test passes after the sweep even if attachment never starts the in-process fallback.

verdicts.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:114–115 reduces results with 'map(({ name, ok, exitCode }) => ({ name, ok, exitCode }))'; line 144 compares only these projections. Line 146 checks output for the environment check alone, and lines 152–154 compare event result names alone.
verdicts.trigger: The executor loses another check's output or failure metadata while preserving name, ok, and exitCode; the result-equivalence assertion still passes.

findings.title: Rollback to an older daemon does not stop the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the persistent `executor.daemonRelease` setting. A daemon from before this change never updates that setting, so after rollback it still contains the newer release SHA. The newer executor continues its running job while the older daemon resumes the run without understanding the in-place handle, allowing both releases to operate on the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Use a coordinator release and liveness mechanism that also detects replacement by a daemon that does not write this setting, and stop the executor's jobs before the older daemon can resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release in-place gate is running when the daemon is rolled back to the base release. The old daemon leaves the setting unchanged and starts its own recovery or gate while the executor continues.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha)`; the base release's startScopedDaemon contains no corresponding write. src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects changes solely through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`, and lines 52–57 otherwise renew the running job's lease.
verification.trigger: Roll back to the base daemon while an executor gate is running. The setting retains the newer SHA, so the executor continues running and renewing instead of cancelling on rollback.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A running `regression-retry-targeted` job therefore gets cancelled on restart even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, release, and lease still match. The stage repeats work instead of attaching to the retry, contrary to the requested coverage of targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the targeted retry at its recorded purpose and attach to its matching job.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted regression retry is running. On resume, the saved handle fails the purpose check and the running job is cancelled.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:301-318 runs a configured retryFiles command with `{ targeted: true, skipGateSlot }`; src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 names it `"regression-retry-targeted"`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88 persists `{ stage, round, purpose, sha, handle }`. On resume, engine.ts:1536 calls `resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, env)`. gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; lines 35-43 cancel the rejected handle and clear it. engine.ts:1547 then runs the initial gates again.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and alive, a regression with valid failedFiles and a retryFiles command starts a targeted retry. Restarting the daemon during that retry causes the resumed stage to reject and cancel its saved handle, even at the same SHA, and repeat earlier gate work.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a worktree indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor freshness is determined solely by whether its PID and birth time still match; there is no heartbeat. If the executor is alive but no longer making progress, the sweep eventually fails its lease, but `waitStopped` continues waiting for that same live process to set `stopped`. Consequently the daemon never reaches the in-process fallback or starts another gate in the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, confirmed process-stop or recovery path before falling back.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor becomes stuck while running a gate but remains alive. Its lease expires, and the daemon waits indefinitely in `waitStopped`.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 defines executor liveness solely as `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. At :366–384, `while (this.job(id)?.stopped === 0)` performs recovery only when `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)`; otherwise it sleeps without a deadline. src/gates/lan.ts:130–131 awaits `workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` before fallback.
verification.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, an executor stalls permanently after leasing a job but retains its process identity. Lease expiry fails the job, yet fallback waits indefinitely for stopped=1. No ordinary-operation cause of a permanent executor stall was established, so severity is medium.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into a local retry
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from `executeGate`, including `ConfinementError`, and marks the job failed. The daemon treats every failed in-place job as eligible for local fallback in `lan.ts`. A confinement inspection failure can therefore be replaced by a passing second execution, hiding the failed security check and allowing the gate to pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the failure classification across the job boundary and propagate confinement failures without retrying them as local gates.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor cannot verify its Seatbelt confinement, but the daemon's subsequent local confinement check succeeds; the local retry passes and the original security failure is lost.

verification.evidence: src/harness/sandbox.ts:282 calls `await (verify ? verify() : backend.verify(roots, opts, run))`; verification can throw `new ConfinementError(...)` (lines 199–201, 222). src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71 catches every error with `workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error)))`. src/db/workers.ts:626–632 marks that in-place job `state='failed'`. src/gates/lan.ts:130–150 handles every failed job by running `local.start(request, controller.signal)` and returning the fallback result, without preserving a blocking confinement verdict.
verification.trigger: Executor confinement verification throws, then daemon-side verification succeeds. The daemon retries locally and can return a passing GateRun despite the original confinement failure. The diagnostic remains recorded, but its blocking classification is lost.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth time; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor remains alive but stops making progress, new jobs are sent to it and previously leased jobs eventually enter `waitStopped`, which continues waiting as long as that process exists. Lease expiry therefore does not produce a bounded fallback or a completed cancellation.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for an unresponsive owner while confirming its gate processes have stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor hangs while running a gate and stops renewing its lease. The sweep marks the job failed, but `waitStopped` waits indefinitely because the executor PID still exists, so the run never falls back or finishes.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:671–672 calls `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")` after lease expiry. However, :370 permits stop recovery only when `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)`, and :359 checks only `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. src/gates/lan.ts:131 waits for stop confirmation before executing fallback.
verification.trigger: A leased executor stops servicing its event loop while remaining alive. The sweep fails its expired job, but waitStopped never reaches recovery or fallback while that process identity persists. This depends on an unusual permanent executor stall.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume whitelist excludes targeted and other retry purposes. When a daemon restarts during a targeted retry, the resumed stage rejects the recorded handle and cancels the surviving job instead of attaching to it. This leaves the requested restart protection incomplete for a gate purpose explicitly named in the request.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the matching retry job and attach to it after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A long `regression-retry-targeted` job is running when the daemon restarts; the resumed gate stage cancels that job and reruns earlier gate work rather than receiving its result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1597 invokes runGateExecution with purpose `"regression-retry-targeted"`; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88 saves that purpose. The resumed gates stage calls `resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, env)` at engine.ts:1536. gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires matching purposes and permits only `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]`; lines 35-43 cancel and clear the targeted job. engine.ts:1547 restarts initial gates. src/pipeline/context.ts:527-534 checkpoints the stage result only after its callback completes.
verification.trigger: A daemon restart interrupts an executor-backed targeted regression retry before the gates stage completes. The resumed stage has no completed result, rejects the retry handle and cancels the running job rather than receiving its result.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
findings.detail: Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. Targeted retries use baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted, so a restart rejects their matching durable handle, cancels the running job and starts the stage over. The new restart tests cover only baseline, initial and rebase, leaving this requested behavior untested.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the matching targeted job, and add a restart test that verifies the same job completes and its command runs once.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a regression-retry-targeted check at the same SHA; the resumed stage cancels that job instead of attaching to it.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 selects `"regression-retry-targeted"`, and src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88 persists its handle and purpose. Resume enters engine.ts:1536 with purpose `"initial"`. gate-execution.ts:29-30 checks `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`, so a targeted handle cannot qualify even with matching stage, round and SHA. Lines 35-43 cancel the job and clear the handle; engine.ts:1547 executes initial gates again.
verification.trigger: With executor-backed local gates active, restart the daemon while a targeted regression retry runs at the unchanged SHA. Resume cancels that surviving retry and repeats the initial gate execution.

findings.title: Executor liveness has no heartbeat freshness check
findings.detail: Executor availability is determined only by whether the recorded PID and birth time still match. The executor table has no heartbeat timestamp, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. New jobs are sent to it until pickup timeout, and waitStopped can wait indefinitely for a stalled owner after cancellation. The tests cover a dead PID and a release mismatch but never a live executor whose heartbeat stops.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and test a live but unresponsive executor for both fallback and cancellation behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops servicing jobs; the daemon treats it as fresh and a cancellation can remain blocked waiting for its acknowledgement.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:351–363 checks executor release and process birth, with no heartbeat timestamp. src/gates/lan.ts:102–105 cancels the job and then executes `await workers.waitStopped(handle.id)`. src/db/workers.ts:366–384 keeps waiting while stopped=0 and the executor identity remains present.
verification.trigger: An executor becomes permanently unresponsive while owning a job. Cancellation waits indefinitely for acknowledgement because the live process continues to pass the availability check. A permanently stalled executor is an unusual trigger not traced to normal execution here.

findings.title: Pickup timeout test does not exercise in-process fallback
findings.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that sweep marks an unclaimed job failed. It never attaches through the gate executor or verifies that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that leaves an in-place job unclaimed, advances through pickup expiry, and asserts the local check executes and its GateRun is returned.
findings.failure_scenario: The sweep marks the job failed, but the attach loop fails to launch or return the in-process fallback; the existing test still passes.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:319–324 only enqueues the missed job, calls `later.sweep()`, and asserts `state` is `"failed"` and `attempt` is `1`; it never attaches or awaits a GateRun. The fallback code in src/gates/lan.ts:130–152 (`await workers.waitStopped(...)`, `local.start(...)`, and returning the fallback result) is therefore outside this test's execution path. The release-change test at test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:414–424 covers another fallback trigger, but not pickup timeout.
verification.trigger: A regression specific to attaching or falling back after an in-place pickup timeout leaves the gate unresolved or unexecuted; the pickup timeout test still passes because it checks only database state.

findings.title: Executor tests replace the confinement they need to verify
findings.detail: The subprocess explicitly installs a no-op confinement wrapper, and the parent uses fakeConfinement. Consequently the test can pass even if executor gates run without the daemon's required confinement. Existing output and environment assertions do not exercise this boundary.
findings.suggestion: Add a platform-gated real confinement probe through the executor that checks both an allowed worktree operation and a denied out-of-scope write.

findings.detail: The startup check accepts any regular file with the owner-read bit set and no group or world permission bits. findings.title: Token exchange ignores caller cancellation and timeout
findings.detail: The provider creates its own 30-second timeout and does not accept the caller's abort signal or deadline. A GitHub operation can therefore remain in the shared token exchange after its caller is cancelled, and the initial token request plus the App lookup can each consume 30 seconds before the requested gh command starts.
findings.suggestion: Propagate cancellation and the operation's deadline through identity acquisition, while preserving safe handling of concurrent callers sharing an exchange.
findings.failure_scenario: A run is cancelled while its first installation-token request is stalled. The run continues waiting for the provider's timeout instead of ending promptly.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2580 passes `ctx.signal` to `findPullRequest`; src/git/repos.ts:1687-1689 calls `githubSh(..., { cwd, signal, timeoutMs: 15_000 })`. However, src/integrations/github-identity.ts:121 awaits `githubIdentity(repo)` before passing those options to `sh`. The provider accepts only `repo` (line 54), awaits the token exchange (line 71), and its fetch uses only `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)` (line 26). Neither caller cancellation nor its timeout applies while obtaining the identity.
verification.trigger: For an App-configured repository with no usable cached token, cancel a run while its installation-token request is stalled. The awaiting operation remains pending until the exchange completes or its independent 30-second timeout expires; the caller's shorter timeout also does not bound identity acquisition.

findings.title: Key validation does not establish that the daemon can read the key
findings.detail: The startup check inspects permission bits but does not verify the file's owner or attempt to read it. A regular 0600 file owned by another user passes this check even though the daemon cannot read it, so startup succeeds and configured GitHub operations fail later.
findings.suggestion: Validate ownership and actual readability at startup, and report a clear configuration error when either check fails.
findings.failure_scenario: The configured key path points to a 0600 file owned by another user. loadConfig accepts it, but the first App token exchange fails when readFileSync attempts to open it.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:390 calls `statSync(privateKeyPath)`; src/config.ts:394 validates only file type and mode bits: `!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077) !== 0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)`. There is no effective-readability check. src/integrations/github-identity.ts:64 attempts `readFileSync(app.privateKeyPath)` only when obtaining an App identity.
verification.trigger: A regular 0600 key file belongs to another user and its parent directories permit traversal. Startup accepts it; the first App identity request fails when opening the file.

findings.title: Validate the key file's owner and exact permissions
findings.detail: The startup check only inspects the file type and selected permission bits. It does not verify that the file belongs to the current user, and it accepts modes such as 0400 and 0700 even though the request requires mode 0600. A file owned by another user can pass the check despite being unreadable to the daemon, deferring failure until a GitHub operation.
findings.suggestion: Require the current user's ownership and mode 0600, and verify that the key is readable at startup.
findings.failure_scenario: A regular key file owned by another user with mode 0600 passes configuration validation, but the daemon cannot read it when it needs to sign a JWT.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:394 checks `!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077) !== 0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)` without comparing the file's uid with the daemon's uid. src/integrations/github-identity.ts:64 later reads the key with `readFileSync(app.privateKeyPath)`; lines 65–68 turn read failure into a GitHubIdentityError.
verification.trigger: A different user's regular 0600 key passes validation despite being unreadable by the daemon, delaying refusal until an App-backed GitHub operation. The ownership configuration is unusual.

findings.title: Protect the configured private key outside the config directory
findings.detail: The configuration accepts an absolute key path or a relative path that escapes the config directory, but the read policy only adds the config directory to its credential deny list. A key at another agent-readable location can therefore be read by an agent or gate running as the same user. The key itself is not registered for output redaction.
findings.suggestion: Add the resolved key file, including its canonical path and relevant aliases, to the shared read-deny policy used by every agent and gate, or reject paths whose confinement cannot be guaranteed.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures a mode-0600 key at an absolute path inside a checkout. An agent or gate reads that file and can publish the App private key.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:387 resolves an arbitrary configured path and src/config.ts:409 retains it as `privateKeyPath`. The read policy receives only `configureReadPolicy(raw.sandbox, configDir)` at src/config.ts:518. src/harness/read-policy.ts:42 protects `configDir` and explicit deny entries, while src/harness/codex.ts:321–324 permits reads except listed denied paths. The App key is not registered through the private-file protection mechanism.
verification.trigger: An absolute private_key_path points to a 0600 file inside an agent-readable checkout outside the config directory and existing deny paths. Same-user agents can read the private key and expose it.

findings.title: Enforce the specified key-file mode and readability at startup
findings.detail: The mode check accepts owner-executable files such as 0700, and checking the owner-read bit does not establish that the daemon can actually read the file. The request requires a readable mode-0600 file and startup refusal otherwise; an unreadable file currently passes configuration and fails only when an App call is attempted.
findings.suggestion: Validate the required mode and verify the file can be opened during configuration loading, reporting a clear startup error.
findings.failure_scenario: A key file has mode 0700, or has mode 0600 but belongs to a different user. Configuration loads even though the required startup validation should refuse it.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:390 uses `key = statSync(privateKeyPath)`; src/config.ts:394 validates only `!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077) !== 0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)`. This accepts 0700 and checks neither ownership nor actual readability. src/cli/main.ts:233–239 loads configuration and constructs `new Factory(cfg, ...)`. Reading the key occurs later at src/integrations/github-identity.ts:64: `readFileSync(app.privateKeyPath)`, whose failure becomes `cannot read or sign with private key` at lines 65–67.
verification.trigger: Configure a stat-accessible regular key owned by another user with mode 0600. Startup accepts it, but an App identity request fails when reading it. Mode 0700 also passes, although owner execution alone does not weaken read protection.

findings.title: Manual landing bypasses the configured App identity
findings.detail: The request requires “one implementation used by every factory gh invocation for a repository” and says configured repositories use the App. This script invokes gh directly without loading or configuring the identity provider, including for the merge. Consequently manual landing uses the owner's login and can merge even when an App token exchange would fail.
findings.suggestion: Initialize the configured identity provider in this script and route its repository-scoped gh calls through it.
findings.failure_scenario: Run scripts/land-pr.sh for an App-configured repository: its private-strings merge step invokes gh with the owner's credentials, so the merge appears owner-authored.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:10 sets `repo="MattFlower/limitless"`; line 22 launches the checker as a separate Bun process; line 153 invokes `check_private "$pr" "$repo" --merge "$sha"`. scripts/check-private-strings.ts:40 sets only `const opts = { cwd: process.cwd() }`; lines 55–56 construct `gh pr merge` and execute `await sh([...merge, "--subject", title, "--body", data.body, "--match-head-commit", sha], opts)`. src/util/proc.ts:1184 uses `env: opts.env ?? (process.env as Record<string, string>)`. This path never loads App configuration or calls the identity provider, whose token injection is in src/integrations/github-identity.ts:121–125.
verification.trigger: Configure the script's repository in github.app.repos, retain the owner's normal gh login with no overriding token in the shell, and successfully run scripts/land-pr.sh. Its final merge uses the owner's credentials and appears owner-authored despite the configured App identity.

findings.title: Key validation does not enforce the required mode or readability
findings.detail: The request says the key must be a regular file with “mode 0600” and that startup refuses otherwise. This check also accepts modes such as 0400 and 0700, and checks the owner-read permission bit without checking whether the process can actually read the file. For example, a 0600 file owned by another user passes startup validation but cannot be read when an App call is attempted.
findings.suggestion: Enforce the required permission bits and verify that the configured key is readable during startup.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a regular private key owned by another user with mode 0600: startup succeeds, but the first App identity request fails to read the key.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:390–394 calls `statSync(privateKeyPath)` and checks `!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077) !== 0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)`; the owner-read bit describes the file owner's permission, not the daemon's ability to read it. No ownership or readability check precedes acceptance at src/config.ts:409. src/integrations/github-identity.ts:64–67 later calls `readFileSync(app.privateKeyPath)` and throws `cannot read or sign with private key` on failure.
verification.trigger: A configured key is a regular file with mode 0600, owned by another user, with searchable parent directories and no access grant to the daemon. Configuration loads successfully; the first App identity request fails instead of startup refusing.

findings.title: Doctor still requires an owner gh login for an App-only configuration
findings.detail: The request says doctor reports the active identity and whether the App token exchange works. Doctor unconditionally marks gh authentication as failed before checking the App identity, even when every configured repository uses the App and the exchange and installation coverage succeed. This reports a working App-only setup as failed.
findings.suggestion: Make the gh authentication check reflect whether any configured repository needs the owner's login.
findings.failure_scenario: With only App-configured repositories and no owner gh login, doctor reports gh authentication failure despite a successful App token exchange and complete repository coverage.

verification.evidence: src/cli/setup.ts:91 unconditionally sets `let ghOk = (await run("gh", "auth", "status")).exitCode === 0;`; line 102 adds `add("gh", ghOk ? "ok" : "fail", ...)`. The App check independently reports success at lines 135–139: `missing.length ? "fail" : "ok"`. Nothing clears the earlier failure. Lines 266–277 compute `ok = checks.every((c) => c.status !== "fail")` and `return ok ? 0 : 1`.
verification.trigger: All configured repositories use the App, its token exchange succeeds and installation coverage is complete, but the owner has no gh login. Doctor still reports failed gh authentication and exits 1.
