verdicts.evidence: docs/GUIDE.md:236 says, “Changing the coordinator's certificate requires pairing again.” src/workers/client.ts:23–29 posts to "/worker/pair" and throws `Pairing refused` for non-200 responses. src/db/workers.ts:41–46 rejects an existing name when `existing.state === "approved"`, regardless of certificate changes or expiry. src/db/workers.ts:101–104 provides manual recovery through `state='revoked',token_hash=NULL`.
verdicts.trigger: Replace the coordinator certificate while retaining its workers database, then run worker pair with an already approved worker's original name. Re-pairing is refused until the owner explicitly revokes that name, blocking the documented recovery flow.

verdicts.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:78–80 persists `state='approved',token_hash=?` during approval. src/workers/client.ts:30–38 keeps `pending.secret` in memory for subsequent claims; token persistence happens only at lines 45–48: `if (claim.token)` followed by `privateFile(..., claim.token)`. A restarted invocation posts a new pairing request at lines 23–29. src/db/workers.ts:43–46 rejects every existing approved name, with no expiry exception.
verdicts.trigger: The worker process exits after owner approval but before storing the claimed token. Restarting worker pair with the same name cannot resume its lost in-memory claim secret and is refused because the coordinator already considers it approved. Manual owner revocation is required to recover.

verdicts.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:67-68 calls `workers.approve(pending.code)` immediately followed by `/worker/pair/claim`; the pairing test repeats this at lines 84-85. The listener restart test at test/workers.test.ts:125-126 only checks `expect((await listen()).tls.fingerprint).toBe(fingerprint)`. No test reopens the store and claims an approved pairing after restart. src/db/workers.ts:66 reconstructs tokens using `createHmac("sha256", this.pairingKey).update(w.pairing_secret_hash)`, but that restart behavior is untested.
verdicts.trigger: Coordinator restarts after approval and before token claim: no test verifies that the reopened database and reloaded TLS key produce a claimable, authenticating token. This confirms a coverage gap, not a demonstrated runtime failure.

verdicts.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:30-31 calls `startWorkerListener(..., factory.cfg.workers.listen)` before mounting integrations. src/server/workers.ts:15-16 returns immediately with `if (!listen) return undefined;`, skipping `certificate(join(paths.home, "worker-tls"))`. Only certificate initialization registers the key: src/workers/tls.ts:12-14 has `keyPath = join(home, "key.pem")` and `const release = protectPrivateFile(keyPath)`. src/util/private-reads.ts:4,30 keeps these protections in an in-memory map. Editor policy uses that map at src/harness/read-policy.ts:190: `const denyRead = policySpellings([...credentials, ...privateReadPaths()], true, fs);`; the home-wide deny applies only to gates (line 217). Consequently restarting with the listener disabled leaves the persisted key outside the editor deny list. Its mode 0600 does not prevent reads by agents running as the same user.
verdicts.trigger: Pair workers, disable workers.listen, and restart the daemon. A tool-enabled editor with read access to the data directory can read worker-tls/key.pem because its sandbox deny was never registered, leaking the coordinator's private key and enabling impersonation using the existing pinned certificate.

findings.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
findings.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
findings.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:65 rejects confinement failures: '.refine((r) => !r.confinementError && !launchFailure(r.output), "Worker confinement failed")'. src/server/workers.ts:131–133 handles that rejection with 'workers.fail(id, ...)' rather than a terminal confinement result. src/db/workers.ts:260 retries using 'j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"'. Once retries or pickup timeouts exhaust, src/gates/lan.ts:73–89 runs the local fallback and returns only its outcome: 'workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);'.
verification.trigger: With the LAN executor enabled for an opted-in repository, workers report Seatbelt launch failures. After attempts or pickup timeouts exhaust, a successful local fallback replaces those failures with a passing GateRun, losing the terminal confinement classification.

findings.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
findings.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:30 selects remote execution for opted-in repositories: `if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal);`. Failed check events are stored independently: src/server/workers.ts:135 `if (action === "events" && event.success) workers.event(id, event.data);`. Disconnects trigger retry: src/db/workers.ts:277 `this.fail(j.id, "Worker disconnected")`, and :260 chooses `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. However, src/gates/lan.ts:68-72 only streams previous events and returns the final result directly: `events.push(...stored.slice(index));` and `return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. Local fallback likewise returns only its new outcome at :89: `return workers.sanitize(run);`. Neither path incorporates earlier failed checks. src/gates/executor.ts:212-215 sends events to hooks but returns `result` unchanged.
verification.trigger: With LAN execution enabled for an opted-in repository, a worker posts a failed check, then disconnects before submitting its GateRun. A replacement worker or local fallback passes that check; the executor returns a passing GateRun despite the recorded failure.

findings.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
findings.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
findings.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a mismatched pin with `new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed")`. src/workers/client.ts:146-148 catches every request error and returns `undefined` unless aborted. Lines 157-158 then sleep and increase the delay to a 10-second cap inside `for (;;)`, without reporting the error. The initial heartbeat uses this call at :177.
verification.trigger: A running worker contacts a coordinator presenting a certificate different from its stored pin. It silently retries indefinitely until externally aborted, leaving the mismatch undisclosed. Certificate pinning still prevents sending bearer data.

findings.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
findings.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`; :459 runs `runWorker(...)` in the same process as the listener. Assertions at :681–683 inspect only persisted `result` and `events`. The coordinator independently redacts these: src/db/workers.ts:59 calls `redactGateData(data)` and :238 stores `events.push(this.sanitize(event))`. src/util/proc.ts:667 defines the shared module-level `credentialValues` registry.
verification.trigger: Worker-side redaction regresses while a gate prints a worker-only credential. This in-process test also registers that credential with the coordinator, whose sanitization masks the disclosure before the asserted storage boundary. The test can pass despite unredacted transmission; current worker-side redaction exists.

findings.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
findings.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:123–124 sets `baseSha: sha, headSha: sha`; the bundle end-to-end test at :657 uses `request(true)` and checks only the head at :677: `expect(run.checks[0]?.output).toContain(req.headSha)`. Production bundle creation at src/server/workers.ts:88 includes both via `new Set([request.headSha, request.baseSha].filter(Boolean))`.
verification.trigger: A regression omits a distinct base commit from bundle creation. The existing end-to-end fixture uses identical base and head SHAs, so it still passes and cannot detect the missing base. Current bundle creation includes both commits.

findings.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
findings.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:123–130 validates events and final results independently using 'validCheck(request, event.data.result, event.data.phase)' and 'validRun(request, result.data.run)'. At lines 135–136 it separately calls 'workers.event(id, event.data)' or 'workers.complete(id, result.data.run)', without comparing them. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns the stored final result. src/gates/executor.ts:211–215 sends streamed checks to hooks but returns the final result unchanged.
verification.trigger: An authenticated worker holding a lease submits a valid failed check event followed by a structurally valid passing result for the same requested check and SHA. The coordinator persists and returns the passing result despite the recorded failure. This requires an inconsistent or crafted worker response; the supplied worker client normally sends the same results in both messages.

findings.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
findings.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
findings.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:74 defines `OUTPUT_TAIL = 6_000`; :114 redacts using the worker's credentials, then :126 stores `combined.slice(-OUTPUT_TAIL)`. src/workers/client.ts:233 posts that already-truncated run. src/db/workers.ts:288-291 persists `JSON.stringify(this.sanitize(run))`. Coordinator sanitization uses `redactGateData(data)` at :59; src/util/proc.ts:683-684 replaces complete registered secrets using `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`. src/util/private-output.ts:23 calls `privacy(field)` without truncation handling, and src/gates/private.ts:70-71 requires the complete protected text when `truncated` is false.
verification.trigger: A LAN gate prints a coordinator-only credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output to place the tail boundary inside the credential. With readable privacy policy and no other matching protected text, the coordinator receives and persists the credential suffix because its complete-secret match cannot recognize it.

findings.title: A failed check from a lost lease can become a pass
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure retries must “never turn a failing check into a pass.” Check events from an attempt are streamed to hooks, but after that attempt loses its lease the final verdict uses only the later worker's GateRun. A failed check already reported by the first worker is therefore discarded for verdict purposes.
findings.suggestion: Retain completed check failures across infrastructure attempts and ensure a later passing result cannot erase them.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check event, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and the replacement worker reports that check as passing. The returned GateRun marks it as passing.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:135 persists accepted check events with `workers.event(id, event.data)`. src/db/workers.ts:276 expires a lost lease with `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")`; :254 excludes the previous worker and :260 requeues the first failed attempt using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. A replacement's result is accepted separately at src/server/workers.ts:136: `else if (result.success) workers.complete(id, result.data.run);`. src/db/workers.ts:290-291 stores that result without reconciling previous events. src/gates/lan.ts:72 then returns it directly: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. Earlier failed events therefore do not constrain the returned checks.
verification.trigger: An opted-in LAN gate job emits a failing check and loses its lease before final submission. Another available worker leases the same job and submits a valid GateRun with that check passing; the returned GateRun marks it passing.

findings.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs
findings.detail: The request says `attach` waits for the stored result so “a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.” Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. A persisted timeout or retry job is cancelled and replaced when its stage resumes, even if the worker is still running or has completed it.
findings.suggestion: Provide durable resume handling for every LAN gate execution purpose, preserving the original job identity and any state needed to consume its result.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a LAN timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. On resume the pending handle fails the purpose whitelist, is cancelled, and a new job is enqueued.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1237 runs purpose "timeout"; :1262-1268 runs "regression-retry" or "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:59-61 persists their handles; :71 preserves LAN handles on shutdown. However, :29-33 requires both `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` to reuse a handle; :36-39 cancels any rejected handle. On stage replay, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1215 first requests "initial", so the saved retry is rejected immediately. src/gates/executor.ts:60 calls `executor.discard?.(handle)` after restart; src/gates/lan.ts:22-23 implements discard with `workers.cancel(handle.id)`. executor.ts:188 then starts a replacement, and lan.ts:30 calls `workers.enqueue(req)`.
verification.trigger: With the LAN executor enabled for an opted-in repository, restart the daemon while a timeout rerun or regression retry is leased. The saved retry handle survives shutdown, but replay rejects and cancels it, enqueues a new initial execution, and repeats already completed gate work instead of reattaching.

The coordinator checks its own untouched checkout after the remote execution, so it cannot detect this change and can record passing gate evidence for the requested commit even though a gate ran against another commit.

candidates.failure_scenario: A requested gate checks out an earlier commit containing passing tests and then runs those tests. The worker posts the original pre-gate SHA, and the coordinator accepts the passing result for the requested head.

findings.title: Dot segments classify paths outside the worktree as inside it

verification.evidence: src/gates/publication.ts:6 only removes trailing slashes from roots. A file:// destination is consumed as a Markdown link and returned unchanged, exposing the local path or causing the private-strings check to block delivery.

candidates.title: Appending a round section rewrites the existing PR body
candidates.detail: The request lists “Rewriting already published PR bodies” as out of scope. Sanitizing pr.body together with the new section changes existing published text, including text a user may have edited, whenever it contains a matching path.
candidates.suggestion: Sanitize the newly generated round section before appending it, without transforming the existing body.
candidates.failure_scenario: An existing PR body contains a worktree path and a new review round is appended; the edit replaces the path in the previously published body as well as adding the round section.

findings.title: Recheck ownership inside the merge helper before each merge command
findings.detail: The ownership check precedes mergePullRequest, but that helper awaits a GitHub PR lookup before issuing gh pr merge and can repeat that sequence on retry. A reclaim during the lookup is invisible until the heartbeat, so the old worker can still issue a merge after losing its claim.

findings.title: Do not discard a checkout reused by the new claimant
findings.detail: All attempts for an entry use the same land-<id> worktree path. After a reclaim, the old worker reaches this unconditional cleanup even when a new worker has already recreated and started using that path. It can remove the new worker's worktree and cause its checks or merge to fail.

findings.title: PR numbers cannot target unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number or URL, but the unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A valid number that has no matching factory run is rejected as "run not found", even when its repository is configured.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets in the configured repository context, and report ambiguity when the repository cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 forwards `{ target: sub, ... }` unchanged. src/land/queue.ts:183-184 resolves an owning run, then calls `requestUnowned(input)` if absent. src/land/queue.ts:226-227 accepts only `^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$` and otherwise executes `throw new Error("run not found")`.
verification.trigger: Run `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open unowned PR on a configured repository. The bare number fails URL validation and the request is refused.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.
findings.suggestion: Support the head repository when fetching and updating the approved branch, while retaining the pinned-head and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:228-230 validates the target repository is configured; :251 checks `pr.state !== "OPEN"`; :252 then unconditionally executes `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed")`. test/land-queue.test.ts:3282 explicitly expects this rejection.
verification.trigger: Request an open contributor-fork PR by full URL, targeting a configured GitHub repository, with its exact current head SHA. The cross-repository guard refuses to queue it despite satisfying the requested eligibility conditions.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/land/queue.ts:260-261 creates the unowned entry with `runId: null`; src/db/store.ts:2721 persists `entry.runId ?? ""`. At base 381e4384, src/db/store.ts:100 selects `run_id AS runId`; src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries, and src/db/store.ts:2784-2785 claims queued or expired waiting_ci entries. Base src/land/queue.ts:349 calls `this.context(entry)`; :819-821 executes `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` then `if (!run) throw new Error(`run ${entry.runId} is gone`)`. The catch at :325-327 calls `this.block(...)`, which at :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`.
verification.trigger: An unowned land remains queued or waiting for CI when deployment rolls back to the base release. Once claimable, the old queue reads runId "", finds no owning run, and persists terminal state blocked with reason "run  is gone", preventing automatic resumption after upgrading again.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 forwards `{ target: sub, ... }` unchanged. src/land/queue.ts:183-184 calls `requestUnowned(input)` when no run owns the PR. src/land/queue.ts:226-227 requires a full GitHub PR URL and otherwise executes `throw new Error("run not found")`.
verification.trigger: Run `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open PR with no owning factory run. The bare number is rejected before GitHub lookup.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands

After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.

findings.detail: The test named as a confined land uses `recordingConfinement`, whose wrapper returns the command unchanged and whose verification only records a call. It therefore passes even if the gate command can write outside its allowed roots. This leaves the request's central confined-check behavior untested for an unowned entry.

The unowned test requests the land at test/land-queue.test.ts:3232 and checks only `expect(landConfinement.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` at line 3241. src/harness/sandbox.ts:316 executes `run({ ...payload, cmd: backend.wrap(payload.cmd, roots) })`. findings.title: Revalidate the PR base before landing
findings.detail: The unowned request snapshots the PR's base branch, but the subsequent land and merge paths do not verify that GitHub still targets that branch. GitHub can change a PR's base without changing its head SHA, so the pinned-head check does not detect a retarget. The queue can run checks from one base and then squash-merge into another, violating the requirement that the destination base's checks govern the land.
findings.suggestion: Re-read and validate the PR's base branch before the merge, and block if it differs from the branch used for the base merge and checks. Ensure the validation is tied as closely as possible to the merge operation.

findings.detail: The warning is appended only when a later implementation stage already runs. findings.title: Encoded credentials in filenames escape diagnostic redaction
findings.detail: The new publication diagnostic passes a Git-controlled path to `redactCredentials` without decoding it first. That function replaces only literal credential variants, so a percent-encoded credential remains recoverable in the error message. The new audit filename handling in `src/gates/audit.ts` has the same issue: `redactGateOutput` also performs literal credential redaction. These diagnostics can be stored as events or sent back to an implementer.
findings.suggestion: Decode supported filename encodings before credential redaction, or suppress the filename when its decoded forms contain a credential. Apply the same handling to both audit findings and publication diagnostics.
findings.failure_scenario: A new file is named with a percent-encoded registered credential and contains text that triggers the publication decoding refusal. The resulting error includes the encoded credential in the path; an audit warning for a file under a root hidden directory can expose it in the same way.

verification.evidence: Delivery calls `await checkPrivateRange(cwd, range, entries)` at src/pipeline/engine.ts:2101. The new diagnostic constructs its filename using `privacy.redactPrivate(redactCredentials(path), entries)` at src/git/repos.ts:758. Credential redaction performs literal replacement only: `text = text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")` (src/util/proc.ts:847); registered variants contain only the original and JSON-escaped secret (src/util/proc.ts:839). Audit filenames similarly use `privateMatches(f.file, entries)` followed by `redactGateOutput(f.file)` at src/gates/audit.ts:425, without adding registered credentials to entries.
verification.trigger: A filename contains a percent-encoded registered credential absent from private-strings.txt, and its content triggers a decoding refusal. The diagnostic retains the recoverable encoded credential. A root-hidden-addition warning can likewise retain it in its filename.

findings.title: Publication diagnostics preserve terminal control characters in filenames

findings.title: Publication checks omit registered credentials
findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only checks the entries supplied by callers. Production publication callers generally supply private strings, not registered credentials, so encoded credentials in published content remain undetected. The new test supplies credentials explicitly and therefore does not exercise the production call path.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected values used by publication checks, and test through a production publication entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: A registered credential that is absent from private-strings.txt is base64-encoded in a committed file or PR text. The publication check receives only private entries and permits the encoded credential to be published.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2064 returns `loadPrivateStrings(configDir, [cwd, ctx.repo.localPath, repos, work])`; :2085 passes those entries to `checkPublicationText(body, location, entries)`. src/git/repos.ts:841 likewise scans committed content with `checkPublicationText(stdout, "Published content", entries)`. src/gates/publication.ts:80 uses only `publicationMatches(text, entries)[0]`. Registered credentials are added separately only for diagnostic filenames at src/git/repos.ts:767: `const protectedNames = [...entries, ...registeredCredentials().map((value) => ({ value, entry: 1 }))]`.
verification.trigger: A committed file or outgoing PR body contains a base64-encoded registered credential absent from private-strings.txt. Content scanning never supplies that credential to the decoder, so publication proceeds with the recoverable secret. The runtime probe was blocked by the missing entities dependency; the code establishes the bypass.

findings.detail: The new base64 decoder only checks the entries supplied by its caller. Production publication callers generally supply private-strings entries alone, so a registered credential encoded in base64 is not detected. The new test explicitly constructs a combined list, but production callers do not. This leaves the requested protection for published content ineffective for credentials.
findings.suggestion: Include registered credentials in the protected entries at the publication boundary and test a production publication path with a registered credential absent from private-strings.txt.

Production callers supply private entries at src/pipeline/engine.ts:2084-2085 and src/git/repos.ts:841.

findings.title: Base64 decoding stops before nested encodings can be inspected
findings.detail: base64Match returns decoded text only when that first decoded layer already contains a protected value. A base64 encoding of a percent-encoded credential, or a doubly base64-encoded credential, therefore remains unchanged and is accepted. The direct check `bun -e 'import {privateMatches} from "./src/gates/private.ts"; const e=[{value:"secret-credential",entry:1}]; for(const s of [Buffer.from("%73ecret-credential").toString("base64"),Buffer.from(Buffer.from("secret-credential").toString("base64")).toString("base64")]) console.log(s,JSON.stringify(privateMatches(s,e)));'` printed `JTczZWNyZXQtY3JlZGVudGlhbA== []` and `YzJWamNtVjBMV055WldSbGJuUnBZV3c9 []`.
findings.suggestion: Inspect bounded successive decoding layers for eligible base64 runs before deciding that a run is unrelated, and cover nested encodings in filename and publication tests.
findings.failure_scenario: A filename or published text contains base64 of `%73ecret-credential`, with `secret-credential` registered as protected; the encoded value survives the check.

verification.evidence: src/gates/private.ts:155–159 decodes base64 but returns it only when the plaintext already contains the protected value: `const found = normalize(plain); if (entries.some(({ value }) => found.includes(normalize(value)))) return plain;`. src/gates/private.ts:166–167 then preserves rejected runs and stops: `base64Match(run, entries) ?? run` and `if (next === text) return layers.map(normalize)`. A targeted probe with `secret-credential` protected and `JTczZWNyZXQtY3JlZGVudGlhbA==` as input returned `base64Match: null` and `matches: []`. src/gates/audit.ts:437 includes registered credentials, but :454–456 retains filenames when `publicationMatches(file, protectedText).length` is zero. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1448–1455 records those findings in state and audit events.
verification.trigger: Register `secret-credential`, then add a file whose name contains `JTczZWNyZXQtY3JlZGVudGlhbA==` (base64 of `%73ecret-credential`) and triggers an audit finding. The decoder rejects the intermediate percent-encoded plaintext, so the recoverable credential remains in the finding and audit event.

findings.title: Review eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
findings.detail: Review systems can invoke several finders, samples, and verifiers, including models on different providers. Their trial totals combine those calls, but the fallback creates one record using the trial's primary provider and model. This assigns other providers' tokens and costs to the primary provider and undercounts invocations.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
findings.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1115 invokes the selected verifier with `return sendTo(request, to, ...)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:926 returns `result: combined(results, last, ...)`; combined sums costs and usage (src/pipeline/review.ts:541–547). src/db/stats.ts:269–275 creates one fallback record using `provider: details.provider` and the trial's combined tokens/cost. src/db/stats.ts:179 reports `invocations: rows.length`.
verification.trigger: Request provider statistics after a review eval with primary provider A and verifier provider B. Both calls' spend is attributed to A and counted as one execution; B receives no record from this trial.

findings.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
findings.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
findings.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 accumulates `trial.details.cacheReadTokens` and `cacheWriteTokens`. Even a single-round implementation stores round evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1173–1175: `if ("hidden" in item) { trial.details.rounds ??= []; trial.details.rounds.push(roundEvidence); }`. src/db/stats.ts:280–281 then uses `rounds?.length ? null` for both cache metrics.
verification.trigger: A single-round implementation eval stores 100 cache-read and 20 cache-write tokens. Provider statistics select its round record and return null for both cache totals at model and provider levels.

findings.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
findings.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
findings.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/review.ts:926 combines panel results; src/pipeline/review.ts:541–547 sums every member's cost and tokens. src/db/stats.ts:265–275 selects recorded rounds or one trial fallback, assigning the latter `provider: details.provider` and `modelId: String(t.model_id)` with combined trial totals. Panel reviews reach this fallback; their combined work is still attributed to one model.
verification.trigger: A panel eval calls reviewer A and verifier B. Statistics attribute both calls' tokens and costs to A and omit B. This duplicates C1's attribution defect; ordinary panel reviews use the trial fallback rather than a stored implementation round.

findings.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
findings.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
findings.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
findings.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

verification.evidence: src/evals/runner.ts:1143–1144 preserves cumulative cache splits in trial details. src/db/stats.ts:280–281 discards them whenever rounds exist: `const read = rounds?.length ? null : ...` and likewise for write. src/db/stats.ts:291 consequently sets inputTokens to null; src/db/stats.ts:171–173 propagates any null measurement to aggregate totals.

findings.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
findings.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
findings.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

findings.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.

candidates.suggestion: Aggregate individual stored call evidence where available, and represent unattributable combined work explicitly rather than assigning it all to the primary provider.
candidates.failure_scenario: A review eval calls provider A as its primary reviewer and provider B as a verifier. The report shows one invocation and the combined spend under A, with no invocation or spend under B.

candidates.title: Implementation evals lose stored cache token totals
candidates.detail: Every eval with rounds is assigned null cache-read and cache-write tokens, even when the trial contains those accumulated measurements and has only one round. Because the summation returns null if any row is unknown, one implementation eval also makes the corresponding provider totals unknown.
candidates.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed, including single-round trials, and preserve known aggregate totals where per-round splits cannot be recovered.
candidates.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial stores 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its model and provider statistics report both values as null, including when it is the only eval for that provider.

candidates.title: Eval cutoff and day use the queued trial creation time
candidates.detail: Eval trials are created when the run is prepared, before they wait for provider capacity and execute. Filtering and grouping every round by that timestamp can exclude work performed after the cutoff and place it on an earlier day.
candidates.suggestion: Use stored execution timestamps when available; if historical trial records lack them, expose that limitation instead of treating creation time as the invocation time.
candidates.failure_scenario: A trial is queued before midnight and executes after midnight. A since cutoff at midnight excludes its provider work, and the unfiltered daily breakdown assigns the work to the preceding day.

candidates.title: Eval round totals attribute multiple provider calls to one model
candidates.detail: A recorded eval round can include retries or panel calls, but its stored tokens and costs are the combined trial delta while its provider and model identify the round target. Treating that round as one invocation assigns all of the combined work to that target and omits the other calls from their providers and models.
candidates.suggestion: Use individually attributed call records where available; otherwise expose the attribution as unknown rather than presenting combined spend as belonging to the target.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval panel calls a reviewer on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The resulting round reports both calls' cost and tokens under A and reports no work for B.

candidates.title: Discarding eval cache splits makes available totals unknown
candidates.detail: When rounds exist, the code forces cache-read and cache-write values to null even though the enclosing trial stores accumulated cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Consequently a single ordinary multi-round trial makes its provider's aggregate cache and uncached input totals null, despite those totals being available in stored data.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve trial-level cache totals for aggregates that can be attributed accurately, and mark only unavailable per-round breakdowns unknown.
candidates.failure_scenario: A completed multi-round eval has cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens in its details. Its eval totals nevertheless return null for both cache metrics and inputTokens.

candidates.title: Count a running eval trial before any provider invocation exists
candidates.detail: A running trial with no recorded rounds is converted into a workload record even when it is still preparing and has no invocation status or usage. This silently reports an invocation and an unsuccessful share for work that may never reach a provider.
candidates.suggestion: Only count a trial fallback when persisted evidence establishes that a provider call occurred; represent in-progress preparation separately if needed.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval trial is persisted as running while its workspace is being prepared, with zero usage and no rounds or invocationStatus. The statistics report one failed eval invocation before any model call.

candidates.title: Eval successful share can reflect grading failures instead of provider results
candidates.detail: For implementation evals, the runner can change a round's status from `ok` to `error` or `timeout` when grading fails, even though the provider invocation succeeded. This aggregation uses that modified round status as the provider invocation status, understating the successful share.
candidates.suggestion: Preserve and aggregate the provider invocation status separately from the grading outcome.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementation model returns successfully, but its grading process times out. The eval provider statistics count the invocation as unsuccessful.

candidates.title: Eval aggregation tests do not exercise runner-produced round evidence
candidates.detail: The eval test constructs round records directly and assumes their status and duration describe provider calls. The runner can modify round status after grading and records duration through grading, so this fixture does not catch the resulting misclassification of provider success.
candidates.suggestion: Add a test using runner-produced eval evidence where the provider succeeds but grading fails or times out, and assert the provider success share.
candidates.failure_scenario: A regression or existing defect that treats a grading timeout as a failed provider invocation passes the manually seeded round test.

candidates.title: Invalid cutoff is reflected in an unredacted HTTP error
candidates.detail: parseSince includes the decoded, caller-supplied value in its exception. The HTTP handler returns exception messages directly, without credential redaction, so a registered credential supplied as the cutoff is returned in the response. The targeted command `bun -e 'import {parseSince} from "./src/core/since.ts"; try { parseSince("example-secret-token"); } catch (e) { console.log(e.message); }'` printed `--since: invalid ISO-8601 timestamp example-secret-token; use YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO timestamp`.
candidates.suggestion: Avoid including the supplied value in the error, or redact it before it crosses the HTTP response boundary.
candidates.failure_scenario: A client sends a registered credential as an invalid, URL-encoded `since` value; URL parsing decodes it and the API returns it verbatim in the error body.

candidates.title: Multi-call eval trials are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
candidates.detail: The request asks for workload “per provider and model” with “eval invocations shown separately.” A review eval can invoke multiple panel members or samples, including providers other than the trial target. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial, but this code attributes the entire combined record to the trial target and counts it once. The resulting provider, model, invocation-count, and success figures are misleading.
candidates.suggestion: Aggregate individual persisted call evidence where available, and explicitly represent measurements that cannot be attributed from existing records rather than assigning all combined usage to the target.
candidates.failure_scenario: A panel eval invokes a target on provider A and a verifier on provider B. Its combined cost and tokens are reported as one invocation for A, while B receives no eval workload.

candidates.title: Eval rounds discard stored cached-token totals
candidates.detail: The request requires input, output, and cached-token statistics. For every trial with rounds, this code sets both cache fields to null even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Because summarize returns null when any contributing value is unknown, one such trial makes the entire provider's eval cache and uncached-input totals unknown.
candidates.suggestion: Use the stored trial-level cache totals for aggregations where they can be attributed without double counting, and preserve unknown values only for breakdowns that cannot be reconstructed.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implement eval has one recorded round and stored cacheReadTokens of 500. Its provider's eval totals report cacheReadTokens and inputTokens as null instead of reporting the available values.

candidates.title: Historical workload omits stored concierge calls
candidates.detail: The request asks for long-term provider workload numbers computed from stored invocations. Historical production reads only the invocations table, while stored concierge calls live in chat_calls and are already counted by the existing provider workload calculation. Consequently the new long-term provider and model totals omit that work even when a provider appears in the legacy today and seven-day fields.
candidates.suggestion: Include stored chat calls in the historical workload with an appropriate role and their stored model, status, usage, cost, and duration.
candidates.failure_scenario: A provider has a completed concierge call and no pipeline invocations. Its existing today count is one, but the new production totals report zero invocations and zero usage.

findings.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.

findings.detail: The request sets a budget of “About 80 source lines plus tests.” This change adds roughly 250 source lines across the statistics, CLI, HTTP, and date parsing code, substantially exceeding that budget.

candidates.title: Multi-provider eval costs are attributed to the trial's provider
candidates.detail: Review panels can invoke finders and verifiers on different providers and models. The runner combines their usage and costs into the trial totals, but this code assigns all of those totals to details.provider and the trial model. The resulting provider and model workload numbers can therefore charge one provider for work performed by another.
candidates.suggestion: Attribute calls from the stored per-call evidence where available; represent an unresolvable split as unknown rather than assigning the combined amount to one provider.
candidates.failure_scenario: A review trial targets provider A but also invokes a verifier on provider B. The full combined token count and cost appear under A, while B receives none.

candidates.title: Implementation evals discard stored cache token totals
candidates.detail: Every eval with round evidence forces both cache measurements to null, even though the runner accumulates cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens on the trial. Consequently, a normal implementation eval makes the corresponding provider totals unknown, including when the trial has only one round and its cache split is unambiguous.
candidates.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals where they can be attributed, and preserve them at an appropriate aggregate level when individual rounds cannot be split.
candidates.failure_scenario: A single-round implementation trial records 100 cache-read tokens and 20 cache-write tokens. Its eval statistics report both as null, as do the containing provider totals.

candidates.title: Recorded rounds are reported as individual invocations
candidates.detail: A round can contain multiple provider calls: the runner retries a failed resumed session within the same round and sums both calls into one round record. Counting each round as one invocation understates workload and its success share reflects only the final result, despite the API naming the field invocations.
candidates.suggestion: Count individual calls when evidence supports it, or expose round counts separately without presenting them as invocation counts or invocation success rates.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementation round makes a failed resumed call followed by a successful fresh call. Statistics report one successful invocation instead of two calls with one failure.

candidates.title: Combined eval calls are attributed to one provider and counted as one invocation
candidates.detail: For evals without recorded implementation rounds, the fallback treats the entire trial as one provider invocation. Review panels and sampled reviews can make multiple calls, including calls to other providers, while the runner combines their usage into the trial totals. This assigns all of that usage to the trial target and omits the other providers' calls, so provider and model workload numbers are wrong.
candidates.suggestion: Aggregate per-call evidence where it is persisted, and make unavailable attribution explicit rather than assigning combined usage to a single provider.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls a finder on provider A and a verifier on provider B. The report counts one invocation and assigns both calls' tokens and cost to A; B receives no workload.

candidates.title: Missing durations are reported as zero total wall time
candidates.detail: The duration aggregation silently drops unknown durations and returns the sum of the remaining values. If every duration is unknown, it reports zero milliseconds; if only some are unknown, it presents a partial sum as the total. This differs from the explicit unknown handling used for the other metrics.
candidates.suggestion: Represent total wall time as unknown when any included duration is unavailable, or expose the measured count and clearly identify the sum as partial.
candidates.failure_scenario: A provider has one unfinished invocation with no finished timestamp. Its historical totals report one invocation and zero milliseconds of total wall time even though its duration is unknown.

candidates.title: Eval rounds discard available cache-token totals
candidates.detail: Every eval trial with recorded rounds reports unknown input and cache-token totals, even when the trial stores those measurements and has only one round. The test explicitly expects null for round cache splits, so it would not catch this loss of available workload data.
candidates.suggestion: Attribute the stored cache totals when they can be assigned unambiguously, and test a single-round trial with nonzero stored cache-read and cache-write tokens.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval trial has one recorded round and details.cacheReadTokens = 20 and details.cacheWriteTokens = 5; its provider and model report null for both cached-token metrics and uncached input.

candidates.title: Round aggregation test asserts missing cache measurements
candidates.detail: The seeded round test expects null cache metrics but does not seed the trial-level cache measurements recorded by the eval runner. Consequently it passes while the aggregation discards cache data for an unambiguous single-round trial.
candidates.suggestion: Add a single-round eval with nonzero trial-level cache totals and assert the provider/model input, cache-read and cache-write aggregates.
candidates.failure_scenario: A single-round eval stores cache usage in its trial details, but the statistics endpoint returns null for those metrics and the existing test still passes.

candidates.title: Cross-origin requests can trigger unbounded historical aggregation
candidates.detail: The existing GET endpoint now synchronously loads and aggregates every stored invocation and eval trial when no cutoff is supplied. GET requests are exempt from the origin check, so a web page can repeatedly trigger this work against a local daemon even though it cannot read the response. As history grows, each request consumes increasing CPU and memory and blocks the daemon's event loop.
candidates.suggestion: Bound or protect the historical computation against unsolicited cross-origin requests, and avoid loading the entire history synchronously for the existing workload endpoint.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user with a large invocation history visits a page that repeatedly loads the local /api/stats/providers URL; each request runs the full historical aggregation and can make the daemon unresponsive.

candidates.title: Multi-call evals are counted and attributed as one invocation
candidates.detail: The request requires workload “per provider and model” and eval invocations separately. A review panel or sampled review can make several provider calls in one trial, but this code turns a trial without implement-round evidence into one record under the trial target. The runner combines panel members' spend into that trial, so other providers' costs and tokens are attributed to the target and the invocation count is understated.
candidates.suggestion: Aggregate individual persisted call evidence where available, and preserve or explicitly identify attribution that cannot be recovered from older records.
candidates.failure_scenario: An eval review panel calls provider A once and provider B twice. The result reports one invocation and all combined spend under A, with no workload for B.

candidates.title: Implement evals discard stored cached-token totals
candidates.detail: The request requires input, output, and cached tokens. For every eval with round evidence, the code sets both cache measurements to null even though the runner stores their accumulated values in the trial details. Consequently, even a single-round implement eval with a complete cache split reports its input and cached tokens as unknown.
candidates.suggestion: Use the stored trial cache totals when they can be attributed to the selected provider and model, including the single-round case.
candidates.failure_scenario: A one-round implement eval records 100 input tokens and 20 cache-read tokens; its eval statistics return null for inputTokens and cacheReadTokens.

findings.title: Long failing test names can disappear from the excerpt
findings.detail: When an assertion line is followed by a Bun failure line, the excerpt takes the end of the intervening text. If the failure line alone exceeds the remaining budget, this discards its beginning, including the `(fail)` marker and the beginning of the selected signature. findings.suggestion: Reserve space for the beginning of the selected signature line before filling the remaining excerpt budget with assertion and stack context.

findings.title: An unrelated later test failure can replace the first error as the signature
findings.detail: When the first failure-shaped line starts with `error:`, the search advances to any later `(fail)` line unless another failure-shaped or passing line intervenes. It does not establish that the lines belong to the same Bun assertion block. For a build error followed by a test failure, the signature identifies the later test and the excerpt combines evidence from two failures, potentially discarding the later test's diagnostic. A targeted check, `bun -e 'import {ciSignature} from "./src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts"; console.log(ciSignature("test", "error: first failure\n"+"x".repeat(3000)+"\n(fail) second failure", "fallback"));'`, returned `line: "(fail) second failure"` with an excerpt starting `error: first failure`.
findings.suggestion: Associate an assertion with a following Bun test name only when the intervening output establishes that they belong to the same failure; otherwise retain the first error line.
findings.failure_scenario: A job logs `error: first failure`, then ordinary output, then `(fail) second failure`; the record and fix-round signature identify the second failure while the excerpt begins with the first.

Publication padding prevents exact-value redaction, exposing the credential in the returned image and signature and allowing it to be persisted in ci_failures.

findings.title: Check for an unreported push before falling back after reconciliation
findings.detail: A failed resume check cancels the old job and goes straight to `prepare()`. If the worktree is dirty, or the remote lookup fails, `prepare()` returns null and the executor runs locally without checking whether the cancelled worker already pushed. The existing failed-job path checks the remote before local fallback; this new path bypasses that protection and can continue a run with an unaccepted worker commit on its branch.
findings.suggestion: After cancelling an unreconciled job, verify the branch against the stored request before permitting a local fallback; treat an unavailable remote check as an unresolved failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes but its report has not been accepted. After restart, the coordinator worktree is dirty, so resume fails, the job is cancelled, prepare returns null, and a local session runs instead of stopping for the unreported push.

findings.title: Keep renewing the lease while a fenced worker reports a pushed commit
findings.detail: The request requires a pushed result to be reported with a signal that neither the fence nor job cancellation aborts, bounded by the attempt deadline. The new result request does survive the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller, and heldJobs() excludes jobs with an aborted controller. Subsequent heartbeats therefore stop renewing this job's lease while the result request is still retrying. If reporting is delayed past the lease, the coordinator rejects the eventual report and the pushed commit can leave the run NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed job in the heartbeat's held-job list while its independent result report is pending, until the report is accepted, the lease is refused, or the attempt deadline expires.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during an outage and its fence fires. After the coordinator returns, heartbeats succeed but result requests temporarily fail for longer than the remaining lease. The lease expires, and the later result is rejected despite being within the attempt deadline.

findings.title: Keep explicitly local panel finders on the coordinator
findings.detail: The shared review call supplies checkout metadata to every production panel finder, while worker eligibility has no indication that a finder was configured as local. The `free_only` routing constraint does not guarantee an ineligible target: the provider configuration accepts a free `claude-cli` or `codex-cli` provider without a backend. Such a finder is dispatched to a worker, contrary to the requirement that local finders stay local.
findings.suggestion: Pass the finder's local designation through the call seam and exclude it from worker eligibility.
findings.failure_scenario: A panel finder has `local: true`, routing selects a free `codex-cli` provider, and review workers are enabled for the repository. The finder creates a worker job instead of running on the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 converts the local flag only into `...(finder?.local ? { billing: "free_only" as const } : {})`; line 1864 invokes the shared call. That call supplies checkout metadata unconditionally for GitHub branches (lines 1840–1843). src/router/router.ts:379–380 permits free CLI targets: `const paid = !c.chain && c.billing !== undefined && m.billing !== "free" ? 1 : 0; if (paid && c.billing === "free_only") continue;`. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 accepts readonly review calls with checkout and a Claude/Codex target without backend credentials; it has no local-finder exclusion. Lines 154–157 enqueue the job.
verification.trigger: A production local:true panel finder selects a free codex-cli target without backend fields, with review workers enabled for its GitHub repository and available worker capacity. It creates a worker job instead of remaining on the coordinator, bypassing the required local-finder exclusion.

findings.title: Local panel finders can be dispatched to workers
findings.detail: Eligibility does not identify local finders; it assumes their targets always have backend, openai, or decisions fields. The catalog also permits a free claude-cli or codex-cli provider without those fields, so a local finder routed to such a provider is sent to a worker. This violates the requirement that local finders stay local and can make a time-limited finder wait for worker pickup.
findings.suggestion: Carry an explicit local-finder flag to the executor and exclude those calls from worker dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a free codex-cli provider and a panel finder marked local that selects its model, with review workers enabled for the repository. The executor enqueues the finder instead of running it locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 marks local finders only with `...(finder?.local ? { billing: "free_only" as const } : {})`; they still use `call(request, constraints, finder?.target, deadline)` (1864), which supplies checkout metadata (1840–1843). src/router/config-catalog.ts:57–59 permits `kind: "codex-cli"` with `billing: "free"`; line 188 maps that kind to harness `"codex"`. src/router/router.ts:192–200 adds backend/openai/decisions fields only when corresponding endpoints exist. Thus this target passes src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40: `call.role === "review" && spec.mode === "readonly" && !!call.checkout && !publication && !spec.target.backend && !spec.target.openai && !spec.target.decisions`; eligibility never checks local-finder status or free-only routing.
verification.trigger: Enable review workers for a GitHub repository and configure a local panel finder targeting a free codex-cli provider without endpoint overrides. Its production review call receives checkout metadata and passes worker eligibility, enqueueing a worker job despite the requirement that local finders remain local.

findings.title: A pinned review model can send a local finder to a worker
findings.detail: Local finders receive the same checkout metadata as production finders. Their free-only routing constraint does not keep them local when the run pins a review model: the router lets a pinned chain override billing constraints. If that model uses a supported harness without backend credentials, the worker executor dispatches the local finder.
findings.suggestion: Carry the local-finder designation to the dispatch decision, or omit checkout metadata for local finders. Add a panel test with a local finder and a pinned Claude or Codex review model.
findings.failure_scenario: A GitHub run enables worker reviews, configures a local panel finder, and pins a Claude review model. The local finder creates a worker job instead of running locally.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1859 marks local finders with `billing: "free_only"`, but lines 1840–1843 also give them checkout metadata. src/pipeline/context.ts:545 reads `const chain = shadow ? undefined : this.run.models?.[opts.role as RunRole];`, and line 595 passes that chain to routing. src/router/router.ts:379 makes the paid filter conditional on `!c.chain`, and lines 391–395 return the pinned candidates. Thus a pinned Claude target bypasses free_only. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:26–40 then considers the readonly review eligible without checking whether it originated from a local finder; line 157 enqueues it.

findings.title: Generator cannot start from the checked-in repository
findings.detail: The generator unconditionally reads the default cases file, but this commit contains no `evals/implement/cases.json` or even an `evals` directory. Consequently, the documented CLI exits with ENOENT before it can inspect a PR or create a dataset. The tests supply a separately created case file, so they do not exercise the default path.
findings.suggestion: Provide the existing dataset at the expected path or initialize a valid empty dataset when it is absent, while preserving existing cases when present.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the documented generator command from a fresh checkout of this commit; reading `evals/implement/cases.json` fails before any case can be generated.

verification.evidence: src/evals/cases.ts:269 resolves `../../evals/${role}/cases.json`. scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:108-109 uses `deps.casePath ?? defaultCasePath("implement")` then unconditionally calls `readFileSync(casePath, "utf8")`. `git ls-tree HEAD evals` returns no entries: the dataset is absent from this commit.
verification.trigger: Run the documented CLI from a fresh checkout with configuration available: opening evals/implement/cases.json throws ENOENT before processing any PR.

findings.title: CLI never looks up available production complexity
findings.detail: The only production entry point does not supply `lookupRun`, so every generated case receives `medium` even when its report identifies a locally available run whose triage complexity is different. The injected lookup is used only by programmatic callers and tests; documenting the default does not satisfy the requirement to record complexity when it can be found.
findings.suggestion: Wire the CLI to an available run-record lookup and preserve the recorded complexity, with an explicit unknown fallback only when the record cannot be found.
findings.failure_scenario: Generate a case for a factory PR whose footer identifies a run recorded with `small` complexity: the CLI writes `medium` instead.

verification.evidence: scripts/implement-replay-cases.ts:306-322 supplies only `cache` to `generateReplayCases`, omitting `lookupRun`. Lines 65-67 read production complexity only inside `if (runId && lookupRun)`, and line 87 returns `complexity: complexity ?? "medium"`. src/db/store.ts:1766-1768 provides persisted run access through `getRun(id)`.
verification.trigger: With the dataset present, generate an otherwise valid replay whose footer names an available production run with small complexity: the CLI never queries that run and persists medium.

findings.title: Operational failures leave the CLI with a successful exit status
findings.detail: All per-PR errors are converted into table rows, and the CLI exits successfully even if every PR fails because GitHub access, cache access, or validation infrastructure failed. Automation cannot distinguish a completed generation from a failed invocation using its exit status.
findings.suggestion: Track operational errors separately from ordinary validation exclusions and set a nonzero exit status when an operational error prevents generation.
findings.failure_scenario: The `gh pr view` call fails due to authentication or a service error; the command prints an error row but exits with status 0.

findings.detail: Validation runs the hidden command immediately after setup, leaving untracked setup artifacts in the worktree.
