findings.title: Rollback to the previous release does not notify the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the database setting written by this new daemon. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the new release SHA in place. A running new executor continues its job and can continue leasing queued jobs even though the active daemon is now the older release.
findings.suggestion: Use release ownership that the previous release can invalidate or otherwise ensure that a rollback stops the executor before the old daemon resumes work.
findings.failure_scenario: Start an in-place gate on this release, then roll back and start the base-commit daemon. The setting still names this release, so the executor does not cancel the gate as required.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 adds `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha)`; the base daemon has no such write (the base-to-head diff adds it). src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes only through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`, then lines 52–57 renew the lease when unchanged. src/db/workers.ts:388 similarly permits leasing when that setting matches. src/cli/service.ts:778–782 restores and restarts the previous release.
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled and running a gate, roll back to the base release using the same database. The old daemon leaves executor.daemonRelease naming the newer release. The surviving executor continues renewing and running its gate, and can lease remaining matching jobs, bypassing the required cancellation on rollback.

findings.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp. An executor whose event loop is stalled remains eligible indefinitely. Once its lease expires, the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits indefinitely while that process exists, so it cannot fall back or proceed with the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, safe path for confirming that an unresponsive executor's gate processes have stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor is alive but paused or blocked while running a gate. Its lease expires; the daemon enters waitStopped and never completes the gate or starts the fallback.

verification.evidence: src/gates/executor.ts:78 selects `inplace && workers ? lanExecutor(workers, [], true) : localExecutor()`. src/db/workers.ts:359 considers the executor available when `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`. Lease expiry calls `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")` at src/db/workers.ts:671–672. Fallback then calls `await workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:131), whose recovery branch requires `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)` (src/db/workers.ts:370); otherwise it only sleeps (line 384).
verification.trigger: With the local executor enabled, its process remains alive but indefinitely stops progressing during a leased gate. Lease expiry marks the job failed, but waitStopped keeps recognizing its process identity and never reaches recovery or fallback. A prolonged executor stall is an unusual trigger.

findings.title: Targeted and timeout retry jobs cannot reattach
findings.detail: The resume predicate explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted or timeout retry therefore cancels the still-running job and repeats work instead of attaching to its matching handle.
findings.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to validate and reattach matching retry jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is leased by the executor. On resume, the purpose fails this allowlist and the retry is cancelled or started again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1566 starts purpose "timeout"; src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1595 starts "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88 persists each job's purpose and handle. On resumed stage entry, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 calls `resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, env)`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires `pending.purpose === purpose && ["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`; lines 35-43 cancel rejected handles and clear their state. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 then starts initial gates again.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and running a targeted or timeout retry, the daemon restarts. The resumed gates stage rejects and cancels the surviving retry, then repeats initial gate work instead of attaching to its result.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback
findings.detail: When the gate executor is configured as LAN, this factory always returns the LAN executor, even when the in-place executor is enabled. Its local path for repositories outside the LAN list runs directly in the daemon, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local path through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
findings.failure_scenario: Enable the executor, configure LAN gates for one repository, and run a gate in another repository. The gate runs in the daemon and is lost on restart despite a live in-place executor.

verification.evidence: src/app.ts:186 passes both settings: `gateExecutorFor(cfg.gateExecutor, this.workers, cfg.workers.repos, cfg.executorEnabled)`. However, src/gates/executor.ts:79–81 handles LAN with `return lanExecutor(workers, repos);`, omitting the in-place flag. src/gates/lan.ts:16 defaults `inplace = false`, and line 71 routes unlisted repositories directly to the daemon: `else if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal);`. That executor runs `runLocalGates` (src/gates/executor.ts:130–133), with execution state held in process-local maps (lines 86–88), rather than creating an in-place job.
verification.trigger: Set gates.executor to LAN, enable executor.enabled, configure repository A in workers.repos, and run gates for repository B while a matching in-place executor is alive. B's gates run inside the daemon instead of the executor; a daemon restart interrupts them and requires repeated work.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into local retries
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from executeGate and records an ordinary failed job. The attaching daemon then reruns every failed in-place job locally. This loses the distinction between an infrastructure failure and a ConfinementError, so a failed isolation check can be followed by a successful gate instead of failing closed.
findings.suggestion: Persist a failure classification and propagate confinement and inspection failures to the daemon without retrying them.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement preflight throws ConfinementError, but the daemon's subsequent local preflight succeeds; the gate passes despite the original security check failing.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:70–71 catches every error: `catch (error) { workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error))); }`. src/db/workers.ts:626–632 turns in-place failures into `state='failed'`. src/gates/lan.ts:130–139 handles that state by calling `local.start(request, controller.signal)` and `local.attach(...)`. No ConfinementError classification survives this path; src/gates/lan.ts:147–150 completes the job with the fallback result.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and available, its confinement preflight throws ConfinementError. If a process-specific or transient difference lets the daemon's subsequent preflight succeed, local checks can pass and complete the job despite the original confinement failure.

findings.title: A cleanup failure can leave the run waiting indefinitely
findings.detail: waitStopped only attempts recovery or reports an error after the executor process disappears. If a job finishes with process discovery or cleanup records remaining, the executor deliberately leaves stopped=0 but continues running. waitStopped then polls forever because the executor is still alive, even though that executor will never revisit the completed job.
findings.suggestion: Make the executor publish a terminal cleanup failure, or have waitStopped detect that the job is no longer being cleaned up and fail closed with a clear error.
findings.failure_scenario: A cancelled gate leaves a cleanup record after process cleanup fails; the executor continues polling for other jobs, while the daemon waits forever to start the replacement gate.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:75–80 sets `stopped=1` only when both `listProcessDiscoveries(undefined, req.cwd)` and `listProcessCleanups(undefined, req.cwd)` are empty; the surrounding loop continues leasing at lines 29–30. src/gates/lan.ts:58–59 cancels previous worktree jobs and awaits `workers.waitStopped(j.id, signal)`. That method attempts recovery only under `if (!worker || !this.executor(worker, false))` (src/db/workers.ts:370); a live executor instead causes repeated sleeps (line 384).
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled, cancellation encounters a process-cleanup failure that leaves discovery or cleanup records. The executor survives and continues polling, leaving stopped=0 permanently. A replacement gate waits indefinitely rather than reporting the cleanup failure or retrying confirmation. The prerequisite cleanup failure is unusual.

findings.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic across concurrent starts
findings.detail: The query for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations. Two daemon-side starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue independently. With two executor processes, each can lease one job and run both gates in the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity atomically in the database when creating or leasing an in-place job.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent gate starts for the same cwd pass the existing-job query before either enqueues, and two executors lease their jobs concurrently.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:54-59 queries existing jobs by cwd and waits only for those returned. It then yields at line 72, `await releaseGateSlotScope()`, without reserving the cwd. Enqueue happens later in attach (lines 80-81): `workers.enqueue(req, handle.id, true)`. src/gates/executor.ts:200-204 also awaits persistence between start and attach. src/db/workers.ts:322 inserts jobs without a cwd constraint; leaseInplace at lines 390-402 selects queued jobs and updates with only `WHERE id=? AND state='queued'`, so separate executors can lease distinct jobs sharing a cwd.
verification.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, two concurrent starts for the same cwd both query before either attaches and enqueues. Both jobs are inserted; two same-release executor processes with available gate capacity can lease and run them simultaneously, allowing overlapping checks and worktree mutations. This requires unusual concurrent callers for one worktree; ordinary stages run sequentially.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A durable in-place handle for a targeted retry is therefore cancelled even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and lease all match. The retry is restarted instead of receiving the surviving job's result.
findings.suggestion: Provide a resume path for targeted retry purposes and preserve the state needed to resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is running; resume rejects its matching handle, cancels the executor job, and runs the retry again.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1595 invokes `runGateExecution` with purpose "regression-retry-targeted". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88 saves that purpose and handle. Restart enters src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 with purpose "initial". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires matching purposes and restricts them to `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]`; lines 35-43 cancel the pending job and clear its handle. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 runs initial gates again.
verification.trigger: The daemon restarts during a long targeted retry leased by a live in-place executor. Recovery cancels the retry and repeats gate work rather than receiving the existing job's result.

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness check
findings.detail: Executor availability is based only on PID and birth identity; the executors table has no heartbeat timestamp. A live but stalled executor is treated as available indefinitely. New gates are enqueued instead of immediately using the requested in-process fallback, and a leased job is not considered disconnected until its lease expires.
findings.suggestion: Record and renew an executor heartbeat and require it to be fresh when selecting an executor and sweeping its jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops making progress; the daemon treats it as available and waits for pickup or lease expiry rather than recognizing that no fresh executor is available.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:354 queries `SELECT * FROM executors`, then availability depends on release matching and `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth` (lines 357–359). src/gates/lan.ts:60 uses `if (!workers.executor())` to select immediate in-process fallback. The executor table contains only `id`, `pid`, `birth`, and `release_sha` (src/db/migrations/20261024T012933-inplace-gates.sql:4). Queued jobs fail only after the pickup timer at src/db/workers.ts:656–657.
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled, an existing executor process stops progressing while retaining its PID and birth identity. New gates treat it as available and enqueue jobs, waiting for the pickup timeout instead of immediately using the required stale-executor fallback. A prolonged event-loop stall is an unusual trigger.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs are cancelled on restart instead of reattached
findings.detail: Resume accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A recorded `baseline-retry-targeted` or `regression-retry-targeted` handle therefore fails the resume check even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and executor lease match. The live job is cancelled and the stage starts over, contrary to the requested restart behavior for targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry state to resume the targeted retry and accept its matching handle during stage recovery.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a long targeted regression retry; the new engine cancels that job and repeats gate work instead of receiving its result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 selects "regression-retry-targeted" for targeted regression retries, and src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86-88 checkpoints its handle. On restart, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 requests resume for "initial". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 rejects the pending retry through purpose equality and the `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]` allowlist; lines 35-43 cancel it and clear the checkpoint. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 starts initial gates again.
verification.trigger: An executor is running a targeted regression retry when the daemon restarts. The resumed stage cancels that surviving job and repeats gate work instead of attaching.

findings.title: Restart coverage omits targeted retries
findings.detail: The engine restart cases cover baseline, initial, and rebase gates, but none interrupts a targeted baseline or regression retry. Consequently the tests do not catch the resume-purpose restriction that cancels those jobs.
findings.suggestion: Add a restart test that pauses a targeted retry, resumes the engine, and asserts that the same job completes and its command ran once.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted retry is running when the daemon stops; the current suite passes without checking whether the resumed engine reattaches to it.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:487–494 parameterizes restart coverage with only "baseline", "initial", and "rebase". Targeted retries reach runGateExecution through src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595: `options?.targeted ? "regression-retry-targeted" : "regression-retry"`. src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:30 restricts resumable purposes to `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)`.
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled, restart during a targeted retry. The restart tests never exercise that purpose, so cancellation and repeated work instead of reattachment go undetected.

findings.title: Pickup timeout test never verifies in-process fallback
findings.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that the queued job becomes failed. It does not attach a daemon-side execution or assert that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
findings.suggestion: Exercise an attached in-place job that is never leased, sweep it past pickup timeout, and assert that the local check runs and its result reaches the caller.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor remains alive but does not pick up a queued job, and the daemon fails to start the local fallback after the sweep marks it failed.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:319–324 enqueues `missed`, calls `later.sweep()`, asserts `state` is "failed" and `attempt` is 1, then ends. The actual fallback requires attachment: src/gates/lan.ts:130–139 handles `job.state === "failed"`, waits for shutdown, and calls `local.start(request, controller.signal)`.
verification.trigger: A live executor leaves an in-place job queued past its pickup deadline. This test verifies the failed row but never attaches or verifies local execution, so a broken pickup-timeout fallback would pass this test.

findings.title: Gate result comparison discards most of the result shape
findings.detail: The purported in-process comparison projects each result down to name, ok, and exitCode, while the event assertion checks only names. It would still pass if executor results or events lost output, command, timing, failure metadata, or other fields required by consumers. The test also does not compare the produced gate artifacts.
findings.suggestion: Compare representative complete result and event structures, excluding only nondeterministic values, and verify the corresponding artifact contents.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor drops a check's output or failure metadata while preserving its name and exit code; this test still passes although the reported gate data changed.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:114–115 reduces results to `[...run.setup, ...run.checks].map(({ name, ok, exitCode }) => ({ name, ok, exitCode }))`; line 144 compares only that projection. Line 146 separately checks only the environment check's output. src/gates/run.ts:27–32 defines additional fields including `durationMs`, `output`, `failures`, `timedOut`, and `confinementError`.
verification.trigger: Executor results lose another check's output or failure metadata while preserving name, ok, and exitCode. The comparison still passes, leaving result-shape regressions undetected.

findings.title: Executor stores gate output without the daemon’s dynamic credential registrations
findings.detail: Credential registrations are process-local. The executor loads configured provider credentials, but it does not receive credentials registered dynamically by the daemon, such as GitHub installation tokens and worker tokens. It redacts and persists check events and results using its own incomplete registry before the daemon sees them, so the daemon’s later redaction cannot remove the copies already stored in gate_jobs.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the executor has the daemon’s complete current redaction set before processing output, or defer persistence of output to a boundary that has that set while preserving restart-safe event handling.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon registers a GitHub installation token during operation, and a gate prints that token. An in-place executor that never registered the token stores it unredacted in the job’s events or result.

verification.evidence: src/util/proc.ts:1216–1224 keeps registered credentials in process-local Sets. The daemon dynamically registers a fetched GitHub token at src/integrations/github-token.ts:17–18: `registerCredential("GH_TOKEN", token)`. The separate executor writes checks and results through `workers.event(...)` and `workers.complete(...)` at src/gates/inplace.ts:65,69. Their persistence paths use `this.sanitize(...)` at src/db/workers.ts:612–613,717, whose privacy filter uses that process's `registeredCredentials()` (src/util/private-output.ts:11). Executor startup calls `runInplaceExecutor(loadConfig(), sha, ...)` (src/cli/main.ts:426), without transferring daemon registrations.
verification.trigger: An available in-place executor runs a gate that prints a token dynamically registered only in the daemon, and the token is absent from the executor's configured credentials and private-string policy. The executor persists the token in gate-job events or results before daemon-side redaction can protect it.

findings.title: Confinement derives credential paths from the executor environment
findings.detail: The gate receives the daemon’s saved environment, but the executor constructs its read policy from its own process environment. The policy uses environment variables such as AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, GH_CONFIG_DIR, and CARGO_HOME to deny credential paths. When those variables differ between the daemon and executor, a credential path known to the daemon can be omitted from the executor’s deny list, weakening the confinement applied to untrusted gate commands.
findings.suggestion: Build the gate’s confinement policy from the same trusted environment used by the daemon, including its credential-path variables, and refuse execution if that policy cannot be reconstructed.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon has AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointing to a credential file under an otherwise allowed toolchain path, while the executor lacks that variable. A gate can read the file through the in-place executor even though the daemon’s local confinement would deny it.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:426 loads the executor's own configuration. src/harness/read-policy.ts:44–62 captures credential-path variables, including `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, from `process.env`. src/gates/inplace.ts:27 installs that configuration with `readPolicyScope.run(cfg.readPolicy, ...)`. Although execution receives `req.env` (src/gates/executor.ts:145), confinement selects `options.environment ?? process.env` and derives the AWS deny from it (src/harness/read-policy.ts:144,169). Known credential paths overlapping toolchain allowances cause ConfinementError at src/harness/read-policy.ts:209–212; the daemon's credential paths are not transmitted in GateRequest (src/gates/executor.ts:36–48).
verification.trigger: The daemon identifies a custom AWS credential file inside an allowed toolchain path through AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, while the separately started executor lacks that variable. With in-place execution enabled, the executor omits that credential path from its policy and permits a gate to read a file the daemon's local confinement would refuse.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The request says the local executor covers “the targeted retry” and that a resumed stage with the same stage, round, purpose and SHA attaches to its job. The purpose whitelist excludes both regression retry purposes and baseline retry purposes. On resume, the surrounding stage first asks to resume its initial gate, so it cancels the still-running retry and starts the stage's gate work again.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the recorded retry at its original point, and include its purpose in the resume validation.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage treats the handle as a mismatch, cancels the retry and reruns gate work instead of receiving that job's result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1592-1595 starts purpose "regression-retry-targeted", persisted by src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:85-88. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 resumes the gates stage using purpose "initial". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and only allows "baseline", "initial", or "rebase"; lines 35-43 cancel and clear the rejected job. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547 then reruns initial gates.
verification.trigger: The daemon restarts while an in-place executor runs `regression-retry-targeted`, even with unchanged SHA, round, release and environment. Recovery treats its handle as a mismatch, cancels it and repeats gate work.

findings.title: Executor liveness is process existence, not a fresh heartbeat
findings.detail: The request requires fallback when no executor has a fresh heartbeat and requires the sweep to apply freshness timers against that heartbeat. Executor rows contain no heartbeat timestamp; this method only checks whether the PID and birth time still exist. In addition, `waitStopped` waits indefinitely while that process exists, even after its job lease expires.
findings.suggestion: Record and check a bounded executor heartbeat, and make the stop/fallback path handle an unresponsive owner without assuming that process existence proves progress or safe cleanup.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process becomes unresponsive while its gate is running. Its lease expires, but the daemon regards the executor as alive and waits indefinitely for `stopped` rather than reaching a safe fallback.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359 checks executor liveness using `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`, without freshness. The sweep marks expired in-place leases failed at lines 671–672. src/gates/lan.ts:131 then awaits `workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)`. In waitStopped, recovery is conditional on `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)` (src/db/workers.ts:370), and a still-existing executor leaves the loop sleeping at line 384.
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled, its process becomes indefinitely unresponsive during a gate while remaining alive. The lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped rather than reaching confirmed cleanup and safe fallback. This duplicates C2 and requires an unusual prolonged executor stall.

findings.title: Rollback to an older release does not notify the executor
findings.detail: The request says that when the daemon's release changes, including a rollback, the executor stops leasing and cancels its running jobs. The release marker is written only by this new daemon code. A rollback to the previous release starts a daemon that does not write that marker, so the executor continues to see its own SHA in the database and does not detect the release change.
findings.suggestion: Use a release identity that remains observable across rollback to the previous release, and test an actual old-daemon/new-executor transition.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release executor is running a gate when deployment rolls back to the base release. The old daemon starts without updating `executor.daemonRelease`, and the executor continues running and leasing as though its daemon release had not changed.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha)`, which is absent from the base daemon. src/gates/inplace.ts:39 uses only that setting to detect a daemon release change; lines 52–57 otherwise renew the running job. src/db/workers.ts:388–396 checks the same stale setting before leasing. src/cli/service.ts:778–782 explicitly restores and restarts the previous release.
verification.trigger: A newer-release executor survives rollback while running an in-place gate. Starting the base daemon does not update executor.daemonRelease, so the executor does not detect the rollback, continues its gate and remains eligible to lease matching queued jobs instead of stopping.

candidates.title: Rollback to the previous release does not notify the executor
candidates.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the database setting written by this new daemon. The previous release never writes that setting, so rolling back leaves the new release SHA in place. A running new executor continues its job and can continue leasing queued jobs even though the active daemon is now the older release.
candidates.suggestion: Use release ownership that the previous release can invalidate or otherwise ensure that a rollback stops the executor before the old daemon resumes work.
candidates.failure_scenario: Start an in-place gate on this release, then roll back and start the base-commit daemon. The setting still names this release, so the executor does not cancel the gate as required.

candidates.title: Process existence is treated as a fresh executor heartbeat
candidates.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat timestamp. An executor whose event loop is stalled remains eligible indefinitely. Once its lease expires, the daemon marks the job failed, but waitStopped waits indefinitely while that process exists, so it cannot fall back or proceed with the worktree.
candidates.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, safe path for confirming that an unresponsive executor's gate processes have stopped.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor is alive but paused or blocked while running a gate. Its lease expires; the daemon enters waitStopped and never completes the gate or starts the fallback.

candidates.title: Targeted and timeout retry jobs cannot reattach
candidates.detail: The resume predicate explicitly accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A restart during an in-place targeted or timeout retry therefore cancels the still-running job and repeats work instead of attaching to its matching handle.
candidates.suggestion: Persist and restore the retry context needed to validate and reattach matching retry jobs.
candidates.failure_scenario: A daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is leased by the executor. On resume, the purpose fails this allowlist and the retry is cancelled or started again.

candidates.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local fallback
candidates.detail: When the gate executor is configured as LAN, this factory always returns the LAN executor, even when the in-place executor is enabled. Its local path for repositories outside the LAN list runs directly in the daemon, so those local gates cannot survive a daemon restart.
candidates.suggestion: Route the LAN executor's local path through the in-place executor when it is enabled and available.
candidates.failure_scenario: Enable the executor, configure LAN gates for one repository, and run a gate in another repository. The gate runs in the daemon and is lost on restart despite a live in-place executor.

candidates.title: Confinement failures are converted into local retries
candidates.detail: The executor catches every error from executeGate and records an ordinary failed job. The attaching daemon then reruns every failed in-place job locally. This loses the distinction between an infrastructure failure and a ConfinementError, so a failed isolation check can be followed by a successful gate instead of failing closed.
candidates.suggestion: Persist a failure classification and propagate confinement and inspection failures to the daemon without retrying them.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor's confinement preflight throws ConfinementError, but the daemon's subsequent local preflight succeeds; the gate passes despite the original security check failing.

candidates.title: A cleanup failure can leave the run waiting indefinitely
candidates.detail: waitStopped only attempts recovery or reports an error after the executor process disappears. If a job finishes with process discovery or cleanup records remaining, the executor deliberately leaves stopped=0 but continues running. waitStopped then polls forever because the executor is still alive, even though that executor will never revisit the completed job.
candidates.suggestion: Make the executor publish a terminal cleanup failure, or have waitStopped detect that the job is no longer being cleaned up and fail closed with a clear error.
candidates.failure_scenario: A cancelled gate leaves a cleanup record after process cleanup fails; the executor continues polling for other jobs, while the daemon waits forever to start the replacement gate.

candidates.title: Worktree exclusion is not atomic across concurrent starts
candidates.detail: The query for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations. Two daemon-side starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue independently. With two executor processes, each can lease one job and run both gates in the same worktree.
candidates.suggestion: Enforce worktree exclusivity atomically in the database when creating or leasing an in-place job.
candidates.failure_scenario: Two concurrent gate starts for the same cwd pass the existing-job query before either enqueues, and two executors lease their jobs concurrently.

candidates.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
candidates.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A durable in-place handle for a targeted retry is therefore cancelled even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and lease all match. The retry is restarted instead of receiving the surviving job's result.
candidates.suggestion: Provide a resume path for targeted retry purposes and preserve the state needed to resume them.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted retry is running; resume rejects its matching handle, cancels the executor job, and runs the retry again.

candidates.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness check
candidates.detail: Executor availability is based only on PID and birth identity; the executors table has no heartbeat timestamp. A live but stalled executor is treated as available indefinitely. New gates are enqueued instead of immediately using the requested in-process fallback, and a leased job is not considered disconnected until its lease expires.
candidates.suggestion: Record and renew an executor heartbeat and require it to be fresh when selecting an executor and sweeping its jobs.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops making progress; the daemon treats it as available and waits for pickup or lease expiry rather than recognizing that no fresh executor is available.

candidates.title: Targeted retry jobs are cancelled on restart instead of reattached
candidates.detail: Resume accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A recorded `baseline-retry-targeted` or `regression-retry-targeted` handle therefore fails the resume check even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, and executor lease match. The live job is cancelled and the stage starts over, contrary to the requested restart behavior for targeted retries.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry state to resume the targeted retry and accept its matching handle during stage recovery.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a long targeted regression retry; the new engine cancels that job and repeats gate work instead of receiving its result.

candidates.title: Restart coverage omits targeted retries
candidates.detail: The engine restart cases cover baseline, initial, and rebase gates, but none interrupts a targeted baseline or regression retry. Consequently the tests do not catch the resume-purpose restriction that cancels those jobs.
candidates.suggestion: Add a restart test that pauses a targeted retry, resumes the engine, and asserts that the same job completes and its command ran once.
candidates.failure_scenario: A targeted retry is running when the daemon stops; the current suite passes without checking whether the resumed engine reattaches to it.

candidates.title: Pickup timeout test never verifies in-process fallback
candidates.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that the queued job becomes failed. It does not attach a daemon-side execution or assert that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
candidates.suggestion: Exercise an attached in-place job that is never leased, sweep it past pickup timeout, and assert that the local check runs and its result reaches the caller.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor remains alive but does not pick up a queued job, and the daemon fails to start the local fallback after the sweep marks it failed.

candidates.title: Gate result comparison discards most of the result shape
candidates.detail: The purported in-process comparison projects each result down to name, ok, and exitCode, while the event assertion checks only names. It would still pass if executor results or events lost output, command, timing, failure metadata, or other fields required by consumers. The test also does not compare the produced gate artifacts.
candidates.suggestion: Compare representative complete result and event structures, excluding only nondeterministic values, and verify the corresponding artifact contents.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor drops a check's output or failure metadata while preserving its name and exit code; this test still passes although the reported gate data changed.

candidates.title: Executor stores gate output without the daemon’s dynamic credential registrations
candidates.detail: Credential registrations are process-local. The executor loads configured provider credentials, but it does not receive credentials registered dynamically by the daemon, such as GitHub installation tokens and worker tokens. It redacts and persists check events and results using its own incomplete registry before the daemon sees them, so the daemon’s later redaction cannot remove the copies already stored in gate_jobs.
candidates.suggestion: Ensure the executor has the daemon’s complete current redaction set before processing output, or defer persistence of output to a boundary that has that set while preserving restart-safe event handling.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon registers a GitHub installation token during operation, and a gate prints that token. An in-place executor that never registered the token stores it unredacted in the job’s events or result.

candidates.title: Confinement derives credential paths from the executor environment
candidates.detail: The gate receives the daemon’s saved environment, but the executor constructs its read policy from its own process environment. The policy uses environment variables such as AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, GH_CONFIG_DIR, and CARGO_HOME to deny credential paths. When those variables differ between the daemon and executor, a credential path known to the daemon can be omitted from the executor’s deny list, weakening the confinement applied to untrusted gate commands.
candidates.suggestion: Build the gate’s confinement policy from the same trusted environment used by the daemon, including its credential-path variables, and refuse execution if that policy cannot be reconstructed.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon has AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE pointing to a credential file under an otherwise allowed toolchain path, while the executor lacks that variable. A gate can read the file through the in-place executor even though the daemon’s local confinement would deny it.

candidates.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
candidates.detail: The request says the local executor covers “the targeted retry” and that a resumed stage with the same stage, round, purpose and SHA attaches to its job. The purpose whitelist excludes both regression retry purposes and baseline retry purposes. On resume, the surrounding stage first asks to resume its initial gate, so it cancels the still-running retry and starts the stage's gate work again.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the recorded retry at its original point, and include its purpose in the resume validation.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage treats the handle as a mismatch, cancels the retry and reruns gate work instead of receiving that job's result.

In addition, `waitStopped` waits indefinitely while that process exists, even after its job lease expires.
candidates.suggestion: Record and check a bounded executor heartbeat, and make the stop/fallback path handle an unresponsive owner without assuming that process existence proves progress or safe cleanup.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process becomes unresponsive while its gate is running. Its lease expires, but the daemon regards the executor as alive and waits indefinitely for `stopped` rather than reaching a safe fallback.

candidates.suggestion: Use a release identity that remains observable across rollback to the previous release, and test an actual old-daemon/new-executor transition.
candidates.failure_scenario: A new-release executor is running a gate when deployment rolls back to the base release. The old daemon starts without updating `executor.daemonRelease`, and the executor continues running and leasing as though its daemon release had not changed.

findings.title: Rollback to an older daemon does not stop the executor
findings.detail: The executor detects a release change only through the persistent `executor.daemonRelease` setting. A daemon from before this change never updates that setting, so after rollback it still contains the newer release SHA. The newer executor continues its running job while the older daemon resumes the run without understanding the in-place handle, allowing both releases to operate on the same worktree.
findings.suggestion: Use a coordinator release and liveness mechanism that also detects replacement by a daemon that does not write this setting, and stop the executor's jobs before the older daemon can resume them.
findings.failure_scenario: A new-release in-place gate is running when the daemon is rolled back to the base release. The old daemon leaves the setting unchanged and starts its own recovery or gate while the executor continues.

verification.evidence: src/gates/inplace.ts:39 detects release changes only through `store.getSetting("executor.daemonRelease", "") !== releaseSha`; src/db/workers.ts:389 likewise gates leasing on that setting. src/cli/daemon.ts:50 introduces `factory.store.setSetting("executor.daemonRelease", factory.bootSha)`. The base release's startScopedDaemon has no corresponding update, so rollback leaves the new release's value intact.
verification.trigger: Roll back to the base daemon while a new-release executor is running. The persisted release setting remains unchanged, so the executor continues its gate instead of cancelling it when the daemon release changes.

findings.title: Targeted retries cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume predicate accepts only baseline, initial, and rebase purposes. A running `regression-retry-targeted` job therefore gets cancelled on restart even when its stage, round, SHA, environment, release, and lease still match. The stage repeats work instead of attaching to the retry, contrary to the requested coverage of targeted retries.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry progress to resume the targeted retry at its recorded purpose and attach to its matching job.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while a long targeted regression retry is running. On resume, the saved handle fails the purpose check and the running job is cancelled.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 passes `options?.targeted ? "regression-retry-targeted" : "regression-retry"`; src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86 persists `{ stage, round, purpose, sha, handle: ... }`. On resumed stage entry, src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536 calls `resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, env)`. Validation requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30). Failure invokes `cancelGateExecution(...)` and clears the handle (lines 35-43). src/gates/lan.ts:46-49 implements discard with `workers.cancel(handle.id)` and `await workers.waitStopped(handle.id)`. The engine then runs initial gates again (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547).
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled and a targeted regression retry running, restart the daemon at the same SHA, stage and round. Resuming requests purpose "initial", rejects and cancels the saved targeted job, and repeats initial gates instead of attaching to the retry.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor can block a worktree indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor freshness is determined solely by whether its PID and birth time still match; there is no heartbeat. If the executor is alive but no longer making progress, the sweep eventually fails its lease, but `waitStopped` continues waiting for that same live process to set `stopped`. Consequently the daemon never reaches the in-process fallback or starts another gate in the worktree.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a bounded, confirmed process-stop or recovery path before falling back.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor becomes stuck while running a gate but remains alive. Its lease expires, and the daemon waits indefinitely in `waitStopped`.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:130–131: `if (job.state === "failed") { if (inplace) await workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal);`. src/db/workers.ts:366–384 loops while `stopped === 0`, performs recovery only when `!worker || !this.executor(worker, false)`, and otherwise sleeps. src/db/workers.ts:359 defines executor liveness solely as `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`.
verification.trigger: With the in-place executor enabled, its event loop permanently stalls during a leased job while its process remains alive. Lease expiry fails the job, but fallback waits indefinitely for stopped=1. This requires an unusual executor stall; an ordinary long-running subprocess does not suffice.

findings.title: Confinement failures are converted into a local retry
findings.detail: The executor catches every error from `executeGate`, including `ConfinementError`, and marks the job failed. The daemon treats every failed in-place job as eligible for local fallback in `lan.ts`. A confinement inspection failure can therefore be replaced by a passing second execution, hiding the failed security check and allowing the gate to pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the failure classification across the job boundary and propagate confinement failures without retrying them as local gates.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor cannot verify its Seatbelt confinement, but the daemon's subsequent local confinement check succeeds; the local retry passes and the original security failure is lost.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:105 explicitly requires that `a ConfinementError propagates so it can never grade a check`. However, src/gates/inplace.ts:70 catches every exception and calls `workers.fail(job.id, redactCredentials(String(error)))`. src/gates/lan.ts:130-150 handles every failed job by running `local.start(request, controller.signal)` and returning the fallback result. There is no confinement-error exclusion or preservation in the returned GateRun.
verification.trigger: The executor's confinement verification throws, while the daemon's subsequent verification succeeds. The daemon reruns the gate locally and can return a clean passing result despite the original confinement failure. This requires differing confinement conditions between the processes.

findings.title: A live but unresponsive executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only PID and birth time; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor remains alive but stops making progress, new jobs are sent to it and previously leased jobs eventually enter `waitStopped`, which continues waiting as long as that process exists. Lease expiry therefore does not produce a bounded fallback or a completed cancellation.
findings.suggestion: Track executor freshness and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for an unresponsive owner while confirming its gate processes have stopped.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor hangs while running a gate and stops renewing its lease. The sweep marks the job failed, but `waitStopped` waits indefinitely because the executor PID still exists, so the run never falls back or finishes.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:671–672: expired in-place leases call `this.fail(j.id, "Lease expired")`. src/db/workers.ts:630 marks the job failed without setting stopped. src/gates/lan.ts:131 awaits `workers.waitStopped(handle.id, controller.signal)` before fallback. src/db/workers.ts:370 permits recovery only if the owning executor is absent; executor presence checks only process birth at line 359.
verification.trigger: An enabled executor permanently stops servicing its event loop while remaining alive during a gate. The sweep fails its expired lease, but the daemon cannot reach fallback while waiting for the stalled executor to acknowledge shutdown.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after restart
findings.detail: The resume whitelist excludes targeted and other retry purposes. When a daemon restarts during a targeted retry, the resumed stage rejects the recorded handle and cancels the surviving job instead of attaching to it. This leaves the requested restart protection incomplete for a gate purpose explicitly named in the request.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the matching retry job and attach to it after restart.
findings.failure_scenario: A long `regression-retry-targeted` job is running when the daemon restarts; the resumed gate stage cancels that job and reruns earlier gate work rather than receiving its result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 creates purpose `"regression-retry-targeted"`, persisted by src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86. Restart enters `resumeGateExecution(ctx, "gates", "initial", cwd, env)` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536). Its guards require `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30); rejection cancels and clears the saved execution (lines 35-43). Initial gates execute again at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547.
verification.trigger: A daemon restart interrupts attachment to a live in-place regression-retry-targeted job. Even with unchanged SHA and a valid executor lease, resumed stage entry cancels that job and repeats earlier gate work.

findings.title: Targeted retry jobs cannot reattach after a restart
findings.detail: Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. Targeted retries use baseline-retry-targeted or regression-retry-targeted, so a restart rejects their matching durable handle, cancels the running job and starts the stage over. The new restart tests cover only baseline, initial and rebase, leaving this requested behavior untested.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry context to resume the matching targeted job, and add a restart test that verifies the same job completes and its command runs once.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor is running a regression-retry-targeted check at the same SHA; the resumed stage cancels that job instead of attaching to it.

verification.evidence: The targeted retry callback uses `options?.targeted ? "regression-retry-targeted" : "regression-retry"` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595). Resume instead supplies `"initial"` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536). src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30 requires matching purpose and limits accepted purposes to `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"]`; lines 35-43 cancel mismatches and clear their durable handle. src/gates/lan.ts:46-49 cancels the job and waits for it to stop.
verification.trigger: Restart while an enabled in-place executor runs a targeted regression retry at the same SHA. The resumed gates stage rejects its saved purpose and cancels the live job instead of receiving its result.

findings.title: Executor liveness has no heartbeat freshness check
findings.detail: Executor availability is determined only by whether the recorded PID and birth time still match. The executor table has no heartbeat timestamp, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. New jobs are sent to it until pickup timeout, and waitStopped can wait indefinitely for a stalled owner after cancellation. The tests cover a dead PID and a release mismatch but never a live executor whose heartbeat stops.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and test a live but unresponsive executor for both fallback and cancellation behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops servicing jobs; the daemon treats it as fresh and a cancellation can remain blocked waiting for its acknowledgement.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:354–359 queries executors and accepts a matching release and `processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth`, without a heartbeat timestamp. src/gates/lan.ts:45–49 cancels a discarded job and awaits `workers.waitStopped(handle.id)`. src/db/workers.ts:366–384 keeps waiting while stopped=0 and the owning process identity exists.
verification.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, an executor's event loop permanently stalls during a job while its process survives. Cancellation or resumed-handle mismatch enters a stop wait with no timeout, preventing the worktree from progressing until the executor resumes or exits.

findings.title: Pickup timeout test does not exercise in-process fallback
findings.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that sweep marks an unclaimed job failed. It never attaches through the gate executor or verifies that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that leaves an in-place job unclaimed, advances through pickup expiry, and asserts the local check executes and its GateRun is returned.
findings.failure_scenario: The sweep marks the job failed, but the attach loop fails to launch or return the in-process fallback; the existing test still passes.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:319–323 enqueues `missed`, calls `later.sweep()`, and asserts only `state` equals `"failed"` and `attempt` equals `1`. It never attaches to that job. The fallback being left untested is src/gates/lan.ts:130–139: `if (job.state === "failed")`, `await workers.waitStopped(...)`, then `local.start(request, controller.signal)` and `local.attach(...)`.
verification.trigger: An in-place job exceeds its pickup timeout. If attachment fails to start or return the in-process fallback, this test still passes because it checks only the database transition.

findings.title: Executor tests replace the confinement they need to verify
findings.detail: The subprocess explicitly installs a no-op confinement wrapper, and the parent uses fakeConfinement. Consequently the test can pass even if executor gates run without the daemon's required confinement. Existing output and environment assertions do not exercise this boundary.
findings.suggestion: Add a platform-gated real confinement probe through the executor that checks both an allowed worktree operation and a denied out-of-scope write.
findings.failure_scenario: The executor launches a gate without its required confinement; every new executor test still passes because the test fixture disables confinement.

verification.evidence: test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:86 wraps every executor subprocess in `confinementScope.run({ verify: async () => {}, wrap: cmd => cmd }, ...runInplaceExecutor(...))`. src/gates/inplace.ts:28 selects `confinementScope.getStore() ?? seatbeltForPort(cfg.port)`, so the injected backend bypasses the production confinement. The parent callback also uses `confinementScope.run(fakeConfinement, ...)` at test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts:101.
verification.trigger: An executor-specific confinement regression permits a gate operation that production should deny. The new executor tests cannot detect that regression because verification does nothing and commands execute without a sandbox wrapper. This establishes a coverage gap, not an existing production confinement breach.

findings.title: Executor output is redacted with an incomplete credential registry
findings.detail: Credential registration is process-local. The executor loads configuration, but it does not register credentials acquired by the daemon at runtime, such as its API token, GitHub token, or worker tokens. Gate output is redacted and truncated in the executor and then written to job events and results using that executor's registry. A credential known only to the daemon can therefore be persisted unredacted, and truncation can prevent the daemon from recognizing it later.
findings.suggestion: Make the executor's redaction policy cover the daemon's dynamically registered credentials before it captures, truncates, or persists gate output.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a daemon-registered API or GitHub token that is absent from the executor's credential registry; the token appears in the stored gate event or result.

verification.evidence: src/cli/daemon.ts:31 calls `createApiToken`, which registers the daemon token in src/server/api-token.ts:10: `registerCredential("LIMITLESS_API_TOKEN", token)`. The executor entry point instead calls only `runInplaceExecutor(loadConfig(), sha, controller.signal)` (src/cli/main.ts:426); loadConfig registers provider keys (src/config.ts:264-267), not this daemon-generated token. Credential values are process-local sets (src/util/proc.ts:1216-1218). Executor check results go directly to `workers.event` (src/gates/inplace.ts:65), whose sanitization uses that process's registry (src/db/workers.ts:129-133,612); completion similarly persists `JSON.stringify(this.sanitize(run))` (src/db/workers.ts:717).
verification.trigger: An in-place gate emits a daemon-registered token absent from the executor's registry and private-string policy. The executor stores the token in gate events or results before daemon-side redaction can protect it.

findings.title: A live but stalled executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
findings.detail: Executor availability checks only the PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor process remains alive but stops polling or renewing, the daemon continues to consider it available. For a leased job, waitStopped also waits indefinitely for that same process instead of reaching a confirmed-stop recovery path.
findings.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for a stale owner.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process stalls while running a gate and remains alive. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped to become 1 and cannot fall back or start the next gate.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:359: `return processBirthSync(e.pid) === e.birth;`. src/db/workers.ts:671–672 fails an expired lease. src/gates/lan.ts:130–131 waits for stopped before fallback; src/db/workers.ts:370–384 performs recovery only for an absent executor and otherwise repeatedly sleeps. src/gates/lan.ts:54–59 also waits for previous jobs before starting another gate.
verification.trigger: An enabled executor permanently stalls during a leased gate without exiting. Lease expiry marks the job failed, but its stopped flag remains zero, blocking both fallback and subsequent gates in that worktree.

findings.title: Worktree exclusivity check races with job creation
findings.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations with awaits between them. Two concurrent starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue distinct jobs, which separate executor processes can lease simultaneously. This defeats the required one-job-per-worktree guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Serialize reservation and enqueue for a worktree with an atomic database constraint or transaction, retaining the reservation until process cleanup is confirmed.
findings.failure_scenario: Two gate starts for the same cwd run concurrently while two executors are available. Both pass the empty-job scan, enqueue, and execute checks in the same worktree at once.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:54-59 scans existing jobs and waits: "for (const j of workers.jobs(...))" / "await workers.waitStopped(j.id, signal)". It then yields at line 72: "await releaseGateSlotScope()"; insertion happens later at lines 80-81: "workers.enqueue(req, handle.id, true)". src/db/workers.ts:400 leases with "WHERE id=? AND state='queued'", without a cwd exclusion. However, src/scheduler.ts:138 guards normal duplicate run execution with "if (this.active.has(run.id)) continue", and src/git/repos.ts:357 assigns "const path = join(paths.work, runId)".
verification.trigger: If two starts for the same cwd overlap before either attaches, both can pass the scan and insert separate jobs. Two executors with available slots can then run checks concurrently, interfering with artifacts or results. The ordinary scheduler serializes each run, so a production path producing these overlapping starts remains unproven.

findings.title: Restart discards running retry jobs
findings.detail: The request says that a resumed stage whose handle matches its stage, round, purpose, and SHA attaches to it, and explicitly includes the targeted retry. This allowlist rejects timeout and regression retry purposes even when all of those fields match. The stage’s initial resume check also cancels a recorded retry before it can be attached.
findings.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the recorded retry, and validate its matching handle without restricting resumption to the first execution.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor runs `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage cancels that job and repeats earlier gates instead of receiving the retry result.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:86 saves the retry purpose supplied at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1595 (`"regression-retry-targeted"`). Resumed gates begin with purpose `"initial"` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1536). Validation requires `pending.purpose === purpose` plus `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` (src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29-30). Rejection calls `cancelGateExecution` and clears the saved handle (lines 35-43), before initial gates run again (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1547).
verification.trigger: A normal daemon restart occurs during a long targeted regression retry with the in-place executor enabled. Recovery cancels the surviving retry and repeats earlier gates, losing completed and ongoing work rather than reattaching.

findings.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness
findings.detail: The request requires a fresh executor heartbeat and says the sweep applies freshness timers against it. Executor records contain only process identity and release, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. After a leased job expires, `waitStopped` also waits indefinitely while that process remains alive, preventing fallback.
findings.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a safe way to confirm its job processes have stopped when the executor stops responding.
findings.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding while a gate is running. The lease expires, yet the daemon waits indefinitely for `stopped=1` rather than completing the gate or safely failing over.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:351–363 checks executor release and process birth, with no heartbeat freshness check. src/gates/lan.ts:131 awaits stopped before local fallback. src/db/workers.ts:366–384 has no deadline and recovers only when the executor process is absent. src/gates/inplace.ts:61 and 80 place lease renewal and stopped acknowledgement in the executor's own event loop.
verification.trigger: With in-place execution enabled, a permanent executor event-loop stall leaves its PID alive but prevents renewals and stopped acknowledgement. After lease expiry, the daemon waits indefinitely instead of completing fallback; external cancellation can interrupt the result wait but cannot authorize another gate in that worktree.

findings.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local repositories
findings.detail: The request says that when the executor is enabled and alive, the daemon’s local gate path creates an in-place job. With `[gates] executor = "lan"`, this branch always selects the LAN executor, whose fallback for repositories outside `workers.repos` runs directly in the daemon regardless of `[executor] enabled`.
findings.suggestion: Route the LAN executor’s local fallback through the enabled in-place executor while retaining LAN dispatch for configured repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: A coordinator uses LAN gates for one repository and enables the local executor; a different repository’s local gate still runs in the daemon and is lost on restart.

verification.evidence: src/app.ts:184-186 passes both settings: `gateExecutorFor(cfg.gateExecutor, this.workers, cfg.workers.repos, cfg.executorEnabled)`. src/gates/executor.ts:77-81 uses `inplace` only for `case "local"`; `case "lan"` returns `lanExecutor(workers, repos)`. That executor creates `const local = localExecutor()` (src/gates/lan.ts:17) and routes unlisted repositories directly to it: `else if (!repos.includes(req.repo)) return local.start(req, signal)` (src/gates/lan.ts:71). On resume, a stored local handle selects `localExecutor(hooks)` (src/gates/executor.ts:195-198), whose attach invokes `runLocalGates` again (src/gates/executor.ts:130-134).
verification.trigger: Configure `[gates] executor = "lan"`, enable `[executor] enabled`, and run gates for a repository outside `workers.repos`, even with a fresh same-release executor heartbeat. Those gates run inside the daemon; a daemon restart interrupts them and resume repeats the checks instead of attaching to an in-place job.

findings.title: Resume accepts jobs without a held lease
findings.detail: The request states, “A job is only re-attached while the executor still holds its lease.” `canResume` also accepts queued jobs and completed jobs without checking a held lease. This deviates from the requested restart boundary.
findings.suggestion: Require a current executor-held lease for reattachment, or explicitly define and implement a separate completed-result recovery rule.
findings.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after saving a handle while the job is still queued; the resumed stage reattaches to that unleased job instead of starting fresh.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:35-40 explicitly accepts an unleased job: "j.state === 'queued' ? !!workers.executor() : j.state === 'leased' && !!j.worker && !!workers.executor(j.worker) && (j.lease_expires_at ?? 0) > workers.now()". src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:27-34 preserves a matching handle when "executor?.canResume?.(pending.handle, env)" succeeds. src/gates/executor.ts:200-204 then uses "const handle = stored ?? (await executor.start(req, signal))" and "executor.attach(handle, signal, req, hooks)".
verification.trigger: With the executor enabled, a matching queued job and saved handle survive a daemon restart while a same-release executor remains alive, potentially busy with another gate. Resume attaches to that unowned queued job instead of rejecting it and starting fresh, bypassing the required held-lease condition.

candidates.detail: The pickup test stops after asserting that sweep marks an unclaimed job failed. It never attaches through the gate executor or verifies that the check subsequently runs locally and returns its result, so a regression in the failed-job fallback path would pass.
candidates.suggestion: Add a test that leaves an in-place job unclaimed, advances through pickup expiry, and asserts the local check executes and its GateRun is returned.
candidates.failure_scenario: The sweep marks the job failed, but the attach loop fails to launch or return the in-process fallback; the existing test still passes.

candidates.title: Executor tests replace the confinement they need to verify
candidates.detail: The subprocess explicitly installs a no-op confinement wrapper, and the parent uses fakeConfinement. Consequently the test can pass even if executor gates run without the daemon's required confinement. Existing output and environment assertions do not exercise this boundary.
candidates.suggestion: Add a platform-gated real confinement probe through the executor that checks both an allowed worktree operation and a denied out-of-scope write.
candidates.failure_scenario: The executor launches a gate without its required confinement; every new executor test still passes because the test fixture disables confinement.

candidates.title: Executor output is redacted with an incomplete credential registry
candidates.detail: Credential registration is process-local. The executor loads configuration, but it does not register credentials acquired by the daemon at runtime, such as its API token, GitHub token, or worker tokens. Gate output is redacted and truncated in the executor and then written to job events and results using that executor's registry. A credential known only to the daemon can therefore be persisted unredacted, and truncation can prevent the daemon from recognizing it later.
candidates.suggestion: Make the executor's redaction policy cover the daemon's dynamically registered credentials before it captures, truncates, or persists gate output.
candidates.failure_scenario: A gate prints a daemon-registered API or GitHub token that is absent from the executor's credential registry; the token appears in the stored gate event or result.

candidates.title: A live but stalled executor is treated as fresh indefinitely
candidates.detail: Executor availability checks only the PID and birth identity; there is no heartbeat or freshness timestamp. If the executor process remains alive but stops polling or renewing, the daemon continues to consider it available. For a leased job, waitStopped also waits indefinitely for that same process instead of reaching a confirmed-stop recovery path.
candidates.suggestion: Track and check executor heartbeat freshness, and provide a bounded, fail-closed recovery path for a stale owner.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process stalls while running a gate and remains alive. Its lease expires, but the daemon waits indefinitely for stopped to become 1 and cannot fall back or start the next gate.

candidates.title: Worktree exclusivity check races with job creation
candidates.detail: The scan for existing jobs and the later enqueue are separate operations with awaits between them. Two concurrent starts for the same worktree can both observe no existing job and enqueue distinct jobs, which separate executor processes can lease simultaneously. This defeats the required one-job-per-worktree guarantee.
candidates.suggestion: Serialize reservation and enqueue for a worktree with an atomic database constraint or transaction, retaining the reservation until process cleanup is confirmed.
candidates.failure_scenario: Two gate starts for the same cwd run concurrently while two executors are available. Both pass the empty-job scan, enqueue, and execute checks in the same worktree at once.

candidates.title: Restart discards running retry jobs
candidates.detail: The request says that a resumed stage whose handle matches its stage, round, purpose, and SHA attaches to it, and explicitly includes the targeted retry. This allowlist rejects timeout and regression retry purposes even when all of those fields match. The stage’s initial resume check also cancels a recorded retry before it can be attached.
candidates.suggestion: Persist enough retry-stage state to resume the recorded retry, and validate its matching handle without restricting resumption to the first execution.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts while an executor runs `regression-retry-targeted`; the resumed stage cancels that job and repeats earlier gates instead of receiving the retry result.

candidates.title: Executor availability has no heartbeat freshness
candidates.detail: The request requires a fresh executor heartbeat and says the sweep applies freshness timers against it. Executor records contain only process identity and release, so a live but stalled executor remains available indefinitely. After a leased job expires, `waitStopped` also waits indefinitely while that process remains alive, preventing fallback.
candidates.suggestion: Track executor heartbeat freshness and provide a safe way to confirm its job processes have stopped when the executor stops responding.
candidates.failure_scenario: An executor process remains alive but its event loop stops responding while a gate is running. The lease expires, yet the daemon waits indefinitely for `stopped=1` rather than completing the gate or safely failing over.

candidates.title: LAN configuration bypasses the in-place executor for local repositories
candidates.detail: The request says that when the executor is enabled and alive, the daemon’s local gate path creates an in-place job. With `[gates] executor = "lan"`, this branch always selects the LAN executor, whose fallback for repositories outside `workers.repos` runs directly in the daemon regardless of `[executor] enabled`.
candidates.suggestion: Route the LAN executor’s local fallback through the enabled in-place executor while retaining LAN dispatch for configured repositories.
candidates.failure_scenario: A coordinator uses LAN gates for one repository and enables the local executor; a different repository’s local gate still runs in the daemon and is lost on restart.

candidates.title: Resume accepts jobs without a held lease
candidates.detail: The request states, “A job is only re-attached while the executor still holds its lease.” `canResume` also accepts queued jobs and completed jobs without checking a held lease. This deviates from the requested restart boundary.
candidates.suggestion: Require a current executor-held lease for reattachment, or explicitly define and implement a separate completed-result recovery rule.
candidates.failure_scenario: The daemon restarts after saving a handle while the job is still queued; the resumed stage reattaches to that unleased job instead of starting fresh.

findings.title: Key validation does not enforce the required owner and mode
findings.detail: The startup check accepts any regular file with the owner-read bit set and no group or world permission bits. It does not check the file's owner, and it accepts modes such as 0700 and 0400 despite requiring mode 0600. A file owned by another user can therefore pass the metadata check even when the daemon cannot read it, deferring failure until a configured repository first needs a token.
findings.suggestion: Check the file owner and enforce the requested mode and readability during configuration loading, with a clear startup error.
findings.failure_scenario: A key file owned by another user has mode 0600. Its metadata passes this check, but the daemon cannot read it and App-authenticated GitHub calls fail later.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:233 starts with `const cfg = loadConfig()`. src/config.ts:390 only calls `statSync(privateKeyPath)`; :394 checks `!key.isFile() || (key.mode & 0o077) !== 0 || !(key.mode & 0o400)`, without checking effective readability. src/integrations/github-identity.ts:64 later calls `readFileSync(app.privateKeyPath)` and :67 reports `cannot read or sign with private key`.
verification.trigger: An unprivileged daemon is configured with a stat-accessible, mode-0600 key owned by another UID. Startup accepts it, but App GitHub operations fail when reading the key.

The check also accepts modes such as 0400 and 0700 despite requiring mode 0600.

findings.title: Key validation does not enforce the required mode or ownership
findings.detail: The mode check accepts owner execute bits, so a key with mode 0700 passes despite the required mode 0600. The failure then occurs later during token acquisition instead of at startup.

findings.detail: The configuration accepts any absolute key path, but the agent read policy automatically denies the config directory, not the configured key file. A key placed in a repository checkout or another agent-readable location can therefore be read by an agent or gate despite the requirement that the key never reach them.

Its merge therefore uses the owner's gh login even when the repository is configured for the App; its PR reads and the direct gh calls in land-pr.sh have the same gap.
