candidates.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub awaits. Re-reading the old run's status does not check whether another run has since claimed the same issue, so an in-flight reconciliation can apply an old terminal label after a newer run has started.
candidates.suggestion: Recheck issue ownership after awaited operations and before each label mutation, coordinating it with run admission.
candidates.failure_scenario: While reconciliation of an old failed run is awaiting its label read, a new run for the same issue starts. The old reconciliation then removes in-progress or adds failed based on its stale latest-run map.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-enabled repositories
candidates.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation skips every repository absent from githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler itself is started only when the queue has configured repositories and trusted accounts. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path, including CLI and MCP runs, with gh as the fallback identity.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and handle linked issues for all applicable repositories.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless run` with `Closes #7` for a repository that is not in githubQueue.repos. No lifecycle label or comment is posted.

candidates.title: Transient lifecycle events disappear before they are checkpointed
candidates.detail: Events are inferred only from the current run snapshot. A needs_human or failed state that begins and ends between polls is never recorded. The same loss occurs when an earlier comment fails: the loop breaks before saving later events as pending, so a status change before the next poll erases them.
candidates.suggestion: Durably record each lifecycle transition when it occurs, then reconcile its effects independently of the current status.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human while the started comment write is failing, then is resumed before the next poll. No needs-you comment is ever posted.

candidates.title: A second needs-human episode is treated as already delivered
candidates.detail: Comment checkpoints are keyed only by run and event name. Once a needs_human comment is marked done, a resumed run that later reaches needs_human again cannot post its new reason. Label reconciliation can still switch back to needs-you, leaving the issue with a stale explanation.
candidates.suggestion: Key lifecycle effects by a durable transition or status episode rather than only by event type.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run needs human input, resumes after the owner responds, and later needs human input for a different reason. The second reason is never commented.

candidates.title: Re-approval can come from a priority label that is no longer applied
candidates.detail: The post-failure check accepts any trusted priority labeled event, even if that label was subsequently removed. The separate approved check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so the current approval need not be the one applied after failure.
candidates.suggestion: Require a currently applied, trusted priority label whose latest application occurred after the failure label.
candidates.failure_scenario: Priority:2 was applied before failure; a trusted user applies and removes priority:1 after failure. The issue remains eligible using the old priority:2 label despite the later approval having been withdrawn.

candidates.title: An unrelated comment can impersonate a completed lifecycle write
candidates.detail: Recovery treats any issue comment containing the predictable marker as proof that the factory posted its pending comment, without checking its author. An issue participant can supply that marker and cause the actual lifecycle comment to be permanently marked done.
candidates.suggestion: Verify the recovered comment was authored by the configured factory identity and matches the pending body before marking the effect done.
candidates.failure_scenario: After a comment POST fails, another issue participant posts a comment containing the run's marker. On the next poll the factory records the failed comment as delivered and never retries it.

candidates.title: A 404 during label removal is silently recorded as success
candidates.detail: The catch treats every HTTP 404 as an already-removed label. GitHub can also return 404 for an inaccessible repository or issue, so a permission or installation failure can be checkpointed as a successful label transition and will not be retried.
candidates.suggestion: Confirm the label is absent with a successful fresh read before recording the removal as complete; otherwise log and retry the error.
candidates.failure_scenario: The initial label read succeeds, but the App loses repository access before the DELETE. GitHub returns 404 and the reconciliation cursor records the label set as complete even though the label remains.

candidates.title: Status transitions between polls never produce their comments
candidates.detail: Lifecycle comments are derived from the current run status. A needs_human episode that begins and ends between polls is never recorded as pending, so its required comment is permanently lost. The pending-comment tests cover a transition only after a poll has already observed it.
candidates.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur and reconcile those records. Add a test that enters and leaves needs_human between polls, then restarts and checks for exactly one comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resumed before the next issue-queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

candidates.title: A removed priority label can supply re-approval
candidates.detail: The re-approval check accepts any trusted priority-label event after failure, even if that label is no longer present. The separate approved-label check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before failure. The tests only exercise re-approval using the currently present label and miss this combination.
candidates.suggestion: Require a currently applied, trusted priority label whose applicable labeling event is later than the failure event. Add a test with an old current priority and a later trusted priority that has since been removed.
candidates.failure_scenario: priority:1 remains from before failure; a trusted user adds and then removes priority:2 after failure. The issue becomes eligible despite having no current priority approval applied after failure.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside the issue queue configuration
candidates.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation requires the repository to be in githubQueue.repos with trusted accounts configured, and the poller does not start without that configuration. The request requires updates for linked runs from all start paths. The new test explicitly asserts no updates for disabled or unlisted repositories, thereby protecting this omission.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for linked GitHub issues independently of queue admission configuration, and test a CLI or MCP run when queue polling is disabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: An owner starts a run with Closes #7 in a GitHub repository that is not enabled for automatic issue picking; the issue receives neither labels nor comments.

candidates.title: Restart coverage does not exercise each lifecycle transition
candidates.detail: The interruption matrix only interrupts the initial started event. The needs-human, failure, cancellation, PR, and merge tests restart after their writes have completed, so they do not establish that a restart between each transition's label change and comment preserves the required effect.
candidates.suggestion: Exercise interruption after the label update and before the comment for each applicable transition, then reopen the store and verify the final labels and exactly one comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A regression that loses a failed or needs-human comment after its label write can pass the current restart tests.

candidates.title: Do not accept an arbitrary issue comment as proof of a factory write
candidates.detail: Recovery treats any comment containing the predictable lifecycle marker as proof that the factory posted its comment. Issue comments are untrusted: their author is neither retrieved nor checked. An attacker who can comment can therefore suppress a pending lifecycle notification.
candidates.suggestion: Authenticate the author of a matching comment against the GitHub identity used for the write, and require an exact, validated marker before recording the effect as done.
candidates.failure_scenario: A comment POST fails or the daemon restarts after marking it pending. Another issue participant posts a comment containing `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:<run-id>:failed -->`. On the next poll, reconciliation marks the failed notification done without posting it.

candidates.title: Tie re-approval to a priority label that is still applied
candidates.detail: The post-failure check accepts any historical trusted priority-label event, even if that label has since been removed. The separately computed `approved` set can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so a withdrawn re-approval still permits the issue to run.
candidates.suggestion: Require the latest trusted application of a currently applied priority label to be later than the failure event.
candidates.failure_scenario: An issue retains `priority:2` from before failure. A trusted account applies `priority:1` after failure and subsequently removes it to withdraw approval. The old `priority:2` satisfies `approved`, while the historical `priority:1` event satisfies this check, so the failed issue is picked again.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are limited to repositories in the issue queue
candidates.detail: The request covers “any start path,” but reconciliation skips every repository outside `githubQueue.repos`, and the reconciler is not started at all when the queue is disabled. A CLI, MCP, label-triggered, or comment-triggered run against another repository therefore receives none of the required lifecycle labels or comments.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and cover linked issues from every supported start path.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #12` for a repository that is not configured in `githubQueue.repos`; no in-progress label or lifecycle comments are posted.

candidates.title: Transitions occurring between polls are never recorded
candidates.detail: The requirement says each lifecycle event is a durable side effect and must not lose a label change or comment across restarts. The reconciler derives needs-human, failed, and cancelled events solely from the current run status; it creates no pending effect when the transition occurs. If the run advances again before the next poll, that event is permanently invisible.
candidates.suggestion: Durably enqueue lifecycle effects at the state transition and reconcile those recorded effects on each poll.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches `needs_human` and is resumed before the next queue poll, or the daemon restarts and the run is resumed before reconciliation. No needs-you label or reason comment is ever posted.

candidates.title: A removed priority label can satisfy re-approval
candidates.detail: The request requires a trusted priority application after the failure label. This check accepts any historical trusted priority event after failure, even if that priority label was subsequently removed. A different priority label that was already present before the failure can then supply `approved`, so the issue is picked without a currently applied post-failure approval.
candidates.suggestion: Require the post-failure trusted event to be the latest application of a currently present, approved priority label.
candidates.failure_scenario: An issue has trusted `priority:2` before failure; afterward a trusted account briefly applies and removes `priority:3`. The remaining pre-failure `priority:2` makes the issue eligible.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are restricted to queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation only runs when the issue queue has trusted accounts and only processes repositories listed in that queue. Consequently, CLI, MCP, label-triggered, and comment-triggered runs against other repositories receive no lifecycle labels or durable lifecycle comments, even though the request covers any start path.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and include all repositories with linked issues.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is configured for GitHub integration but not in githubQueue.repos; `limitless run` with `Closes #7` starts and no in-progress label or start comment is posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:156 returns immediately when `!q?.repos.length || !q.trusted.length`; line 203 calls `reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)` from that queue poll. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:11–13 defines `lifecycleManaged` using `cfg.githubQueue.repos.some(...)`, and lines 109–116 filter observation and delivery through it.
verification.trigger: A GitHub-integrated repository outside githubQueue.repos starts a CLI or MCP run containing Closes #7. Lifecycle reconciliation excludes it, so the issue receives neither lifecycle labels nor comments.

findings.title: Failure and needs-human comments omit the reason
findings.detail: Both event bodies always contain only a UI link and never inspect the run's reason. The fixed message is required as a fallback when publication checks block the reason, but this code uses it for every run. The new tests explicitly assert that the original reason is absent.
findings.suggestion: Include the recorded reason after credential redaction and private-string checking, falling back to fixed text when it cannot be published.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails with `error: "tests failed"`; the issue receives only `failed: see ...` and the owner cannot see the requested reason in the comment.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:82–83 constructs only `needs you: see ${link}.` and `failed: see ${link}.`; line 95 wraps that fixed text in the comment. test/issue-queue.test.ts:1392 explicitly asserts the comment does not contain `original reason`.
verification.trigger: An eligible, non-discreet run fails with a publishable error such as "tests failed", or reaches needs_human with a reason. Its comment links the UI but omits the reason, reducing the requested diagnostic information.

findings.title: A blocked comment is marked done without posting the required fallback
findings.detail: If the publication check rejects a comment, the effect is permanently marked done instead of creating and delivering a fixed safe message. The same suppression happens during the delivery-time recheck. This loses the lifecycle notification permanently.
findings.suggestion: Construct and check a fixed safe fallback and retain a pending effect until it is delivered.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured private string matches the generated run link or run ID; the start comment is marked done and no comment is ever posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:63–67 checks the comment against private strings; lines 98–100 handle rejection with `save(effect, "done")` and logging, without a fallback. test/issue-queue.test.ts:1562–1567 configures run.id as private and asserts that no comment POST occurs and comment:started is done.
verification.trigger: A configured private string matches the generated run ID or UI link. The comment is permanently suppressed instead of posting fixed fallback text. This unusual configuration causes a real missing notification.

findings.title: Lifecycle transitions between polls are lost
findings.detail: The poller derives events solely from the current run status and records no transition at the point the status changes. A needs-human or failure state that is resolved before the next poll is never observed, so neither its comment nor its corresponding label is applied. A single effect key per event also prevents a second needs-human episode from producing a comment.
findings.suggestion: Persist lifecycle events with the state transition and reconcile those durable records on subsequent polls.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and the owner resolves it before the next queue poll; the issue never receives the needs-you update or reason.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:203 invokes reconciliation during polling, and line 307 schedules the next poll using `q.pollSeconds`. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:82 creates needs_human effects only when `run.status === "needs_human"`. src/db/store.ts:2113–2115 changes the current status to resolved; lifecycle observation reads current runs at src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:105–110 rather than replaying status events.
verification.trigger: A linked run reaches needs_human and the owner resolves it through the API before the next poll (the default interval is 180 seconds, src/config.ts:427). Reconciliation sees resolved and never records or delivers the needs-you label transition or comment.

duplicates.title: Transient lifecycle states are lost between polls
duplicates.detail: The reconciler creates effects only from the current run snapshot. It does not durably record a needs-human transition when it happens, so a transition that is resolved or resumed before the next poll produces neither the required comment nor its label change. This also affects transitions while the daemon is stopped.
duplicates.suggestion: Persist lifecycle events at the corresponding state transitions, then let polling deliver their checkpointed effects.
duplicates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and an owner resumes it before the next queue poll; the issue never receives the needs-you update.

findings.title: A failed issue can be picked before the failure label is applied
findings.detail: When the failed label is absent, eligibility falls back to accepting any trusted priority event after the run finished. If the lifecycle label write fails, that approval can occur before the failure label exists, yet the next queue poll can select the issue. This violates the required ordering after the failure label was applied.
findings.suggestion: Keep failed runs ineligible until the failure label application is observed and a trusted priority event follows it.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails, adding `limitless:failed` fails, and a trusted user reapplies priority before the next poll. The issue has no failed label, so the timestamp fallback admits it without a priority event after the failure label.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:117-123 checks `context.latest.status === "failed" && failed`; when the failed label is absent it instead accepts `trusts(e.actor?.login) && Date.parse(e.createdAt) > (context.latest?.finishedAt ?? findings.title: Failure and needs-you comments omit the reason
findings.detail: Both terminal comments always use a fixed UI reference and never include the run's reason. The request requires a comment with the reason, using a fixed message when the private-strings check blocks that text. The added tests explicitly assert that the reason is absent.

findings.title: Publication errors permanently discard comments
findings.detail: Any exception while preparing or checking a comment marks the effect done. This includes transient inspection errors as well as a private-string match, so no later poll retries it and the required fixed fallback is never posted. The same permanent suppression occurs when rechecking a pending body at line 248.

findings.failure_scenario: A private string matches the generated UI link, or the private-strings file is temporarily unreadable; the lifecycle event is recorded as done without any issue comment and remains absent after the condition is corrected.

At :98-100, an exception executes `save(effect, "done")`; :87 skips existing effects with `if (effects.has(effect)) continue`. The delivery-time check likewise marks failures done at :248-251.

findings.title: A failed label write permits re-pick based on an earlier approval

findings.suggestion: Keep a failed run ineligible until the failure label has been observed and a trusted priority application is observed after that label.
findings.failure_scenario: A run fails, the owner reapplies a priority label, and posting `limitless:failed` fails. The same or a later poll sees the post-finish priority event and selects the issue despite there being no post-failure-label approval.

findings.title: Lifecycle events between polls are never recorded

findings.title: Blocked publication permanently drops the comment

findings.title: Canonicalized names no longer resolve existing mixed-case repository registrations
findings.detail: The queue passes the lowercased repository name into run creation. Repository resolution uses a case-sensitive getRepoBySlug lookup, so an existing mixed-case registration is missed. Resolution then calls GitHub and creates a second repository record with default settings. This can lose the existing registration's merge policy and default branch, and queue admission can fail when the extra GitHub lookup fails.
findings.suggestion: Use canonical keys for comparisons and snapshots while preserving or resolving the registered repository's spelling for run creation.

An existing registration such as Owner/Repo is therefore not found when the queue creates a run for owner/repo. resolveRepo instead performs a GitHub lookup and creates a second registration with default settings, losing the existing registration's repository-specific settings. If that lookup fails, queue admission fails altogether.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate using lowercase comparison keys while preserving a configured spelling for repository resolution, or make repository resolution reuse existing registrations case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for Owner/Repo has an existing Owner/Repo registration with a custom merge policy. After upgrade, an approved issue is admitted as owner/repo and resolves to a newly created registration using the default merge policy.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:440 lowercases queue repositories: `repos: [...new Set(repos.map((repo) => repo.toLowerCase()))]`. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:434-445 passes that `repo` through `issueRunRequest` to `factory.createRun`. src/app.ts:398 calls `resolveRepo(this.store, req.repo, this.cfg.githubMerge)`. src/db/store.ts:1222 uses `SELECT * FROM repos WHERE slug = ?`; src/db/migrations.ts:10 defines `slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` without NOCASE. src/git/repos.ts:199-215 retains the input slug and inserts it with `mergePolicy: merge` when lookup misses.
verification.trigger: An existing Owner/Repo registration has a custom merge policy differing from githubMerge, and the queue is configured for Owner/Repo. After upgrade, an approved issue requests owner/repo; successful GitHub resolution creates a separate registration using githubMerge, bypassing the custom policy.

findings.title: Changes before the repository snapshot still invalidate it
findings.detail: The listener records changes from the start of the poll, and the snapshot no longer clears invalidations. A change completed before `latestIssueRuns` is read is therefore treated as if it made that fresh snapshot stale. Repeated changes during lifecycle reconciliation or the repository lookup can defer an otherwise eligible issue on every poll.
findings.suggestion: Track whether each issue already has a snapshot when its linked run changes, while preserving invalidations for earlier candidates when a case-variant repository is read.
findings.failure_scenario: A linked run finishes during each poll's GitHub lookup, before the queue reads the latest run snapshot. The snapshot includes the finished state, but admission still refuses the issue indefinitely.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:251-259 subscribes before `await reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)`; :256-257 adds changed issue keys to `invalidated`. The later snapshot is read at :318-322 using `factory.store.latestIssueRuns(...)` and `snapshots.set(repo, latest)`, without clearing earlier invalidations. At :401-404, `changedDuringPoll(repo, issue.number)` causes admission to skip the candidate despite that fresh snapshot.
verification.trigger: A decision-relevant linked-run change occurs during lifecycle reconciliation or the repository lookup, before the snapshot. An otherwise eligible issue is unnecessarily deferred. Repeated changes in that window can repeatedly defer it; indefinite starvation requires recurring changes rather than a single completion.

findings.title: No test covers a relevant publication before the snapshot
findings.detail: The new decision-field tests publish during the second repository lookup, after the first repository's snapshot. They do not verify that a change observed before an issue's own snapshot is incorporated into that snapshot and does not defer admission. This gap hides the new indefinite deferral defect.
findings.suggestion: Publish a status or finish-time change during the issue's own lookup on consecutive polls, then assert that the fresh snapshot permits an eligible issue to start.
findings.failure_scenario: A linked run changes before `latestIssueRuns` executes, but the queue rejects the fresh snapshot as invalidated; the added tests still pass because they only change it after the snapshot.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:251–259 subscribes before asynchronous lifecycle reconciliation; its listener executes `if (previous?.state !== current.state) ... invalidated.add(key)`. Repository queries also await before src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:318–322 reads `factory.store.latestIssueRuns(...)` and executes `snapshots.set(repo, latest)`, without clearing earlier invalidation. At :401–404, `changedDuringPoll(repo, issue.number)` causes `continue` even for this fresh snapshot. The added regression at test/issue-queue.test.ts:1258 configures `["owner/a", "owner/b"]`, but :1267 changes the linked owner/a run only during `name:"b"`, after owner/a's snapshot.
verification.trigger: While an enabled queue poll awaits lifecycle reconciliation or the linked repository's GitHub query, a linked run publishes a decision-relevant change that leaves the issue eligible. The subsequent snapshot includes that change, yet admission still defers the issue until the next poll. The added tests cover changes after the affected snapshot and miss this ordering.

findings.title: Lowercasing configured slugs bypasses existing mixed-case registrations
findings.detail: Configuration now rewrites every queue repository to lowercase, but `resolveRepo` and `getRepoBySlug` still look up registered slugs case-sensitively. An existing registration such as `Owner/Repo` is missed when the queue creates a run for `owner/repo`, causing a remote lookup and potentially a second repository registration with different settings. The queue tests use a fake factory and do not exercise this resolution path.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate using a canonical comparison key while preserving a usable registered slug, or make repository resolution consistently case-insensitive and cover an existing mixed-case registration.
findings.failure_scenario: A deployment already has `Owner/Repo` registered and configured in the queue. After the change, queue admission requests `owner/repo`, misses the registered row, and resolves or creates a separate repository instead.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:440: `repos: [...new Set(repos.map((repo) => repo.toLowerCase()))]`. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:434-445 sends the normalized repository to `factory.createRun`; src/app.ts:398 calls `resolveRepo`. src/db/store.ts:1222 performs `SELECT * FROM repos WHERE slug = ?`, against `slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` (src/db/migrations.ts:10). src/git/repos.ts:199-210 constructs `slug` from the input and calls `store.upsertRepo({ slug, ... })` after both exact lookups miss.
verification.trigger: A deployment has Owner/Repo registered and configured in the queue. Admission now requests owner/repo, misses the case-sensitive registration, and creates a second repository row after GitHub lookup succeeds.

findings.title: Avoid resolving every historical run individually on each poll
findings.detail: Every poll loads every run and calls `linkedIssues` for each one; that function performs a recursive ownership query even for ordinary root runs. This introduces a synchronous query per historical run, including runs unrelated to configured queue repositories, and parses every stored prompt. The work grows with the entire database and can again block the daemon on each poll, undermining the stall reduction this follow-up is meant to preserve.
findings.suggestion: Seed observations with a bounded or batched query that resolves ownership and filters to relevant runs without issuing one query per run.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived installation with many historical runs starts a queue poll: the event loop synchronously executes an ownership query for every run before it can handle other daemon work.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:250 executes `factory.store.issueRunObservations().map((run) => [run.id, decision(run)])` synchronously inside every tick. src/db/store.ts:1460-1463 selects observations from all `runs JOIN repos`, with no repository or status filter. `decision` invokes `linkedIssues(run, factory.store)` (src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:245), which unconditionally calls `store.issueLinkOwner(run.id)` for identified runs (src/db/store.ts:374). That method executes a `WITH RECURSIVE owners(id)` query and `.get(id)` (src/db/store.ts:1447-1453).
verification.trigger: An enabled issue queue polls on an installation with substantial run history. Every historical run, including unrelated repositories, causes a synchronous ownership query before the first await, delaying other daemon work and reintroducing history-dependent polling stalls.

findings.title: Preserve the registered repository when canonicalizing queue keys
findings.detail: Lowercasing configured repository names changes the repository string passed to run creation. `resolveRepo` and `getRepoBySlug` look up slugs case-sensitively, so an existing registration such as `Owner/Repo` is not found when the queue now requests `owner/repo`. The factory creates a second registration with default settings instead of using the existing repository's settings and identity.
findings.suggestion: Deduplicate and key queue state case-insensitively while preserving the configured spelling for repository resolution, or make repository resolution reuse existing GitHub registrations case-insensitively.
findings.failure_scenario: A queue configured for `Owner/Repo` already has that exact registered repository with a custom merge policy. After this change, an admitted issue resolves `owner/repo`, misses the registration, and creates a separate repository record with the default policy.

verification.evidence: src/config.ts:440 lowercases configured slugs. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:434-445 passes `repo` into the run request; src/app.ts:398 resolves it with `this.cfg.githubMerge`. src/db/store.ts:1222 looks up `WHERE slug = ?`, with no case-insensitive collation on the column (src/db/migrations.ts:10). src/git/repos.ts:199-215 preserves the lowercase input slug and creates a registration with `mergePolicy: merge`.

findings.title: Avoid one ownership query per historical run on every poll
findings.detail: The observation seed loads every run in the database and calls `linkedIssues` for each one. Each call executes the recursive `issueLinkOwner` query, including for runs unrelated to configured queue repositories. This restores an unbounded number of synchronous database queries on the daemon's event loop, undermining the request's goal of retaining the batched lookup that removed 7–34 second stalls.
findings.suggestion: Seed the comparison with a batched query that resolves relevant linkage without issuing a separate ownership query for every historical run.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived installation with many historical runs executes one recursive SQLite query per run at the start of every issue-queue poll, delaying other daemon work even when only one repository is configured.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:250 seeds observations for every poll using `.map((run) => [run.id, decision(run)])`. src/db/store.ts:1460-1463 loads all historical runs without filtering to configured repositories. findings.title: Do not retain invalidations that precede the snapshot
findings.detail: The listener records changes from the start of the poll, but the snapshot no longer clears changes that it already incorporates. A linked run that changes during lifecycle reconciliation or a repository's GitHub lookup is therefore deferred even though `latestIssueRuns` subsequently reads its new state. Repeated changes before each snapshot can indefinitely defer an otherwise eligible issue, contrary to the guard's purpose of deferring a run that changed after its snapshot.
findings.suggestion: Track snapshot generations or clear only the relevant issue's pre-snapshot invalidations when taking its authoritative snapshot, without allowing a later case-variant read to clear an earlier candidate's invalidation.
findings.failure_scenario: On each poll a linked completed run changes status or finish time while lifecycle reconciliation is awaiting GitHub, before the issue's repository snapshot is read. The snapshot sees the updated run, but admission still defers the issue every time.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:256-259 records invalidations before awaiting lifecycle reconciliation. verification.trigger: A linked completed run changes status or finish time while lifecycle reconciliation awaits GitHub, and the resulting snapshot would permit the approved issue. findings.failure_scenario: A repository previously registered as `Owner/Repo` is configured in the queue with that spelling. After this change, the queue creates a run for `owner/repo`; `resolveRepo` misses the existing registration and creates a second repository record.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding a release intent
findings.detail: Every `moved` result from a replay marks the confirmed lease lost and clears the intent without examining the returned tip. The claim client can return `moved` for a malformed record or a valid record that does not meet the supersession conditions. The recovery rules require malformed content to remain pending, and only a higher generation or the same generation under another holder or run establishes supersession. Clearing the journal also makes the row forgettable, losing confirmed ownership history and the final release record.
findings.suggestion: Classify `result.tip` using the same recovery rules as the initial read; retain the intent for malformed or otherwise unclassifiable tips, and mark it lost only when the tip establishes supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed held tip and starts replaying a release. Before the compare-and-swap, another writer moves the ref to a malformed commit. The client returns `moved` with that malformed tip, and recovery returns `superseded`, marks the confirmed lease lost, and deletes the pending release instead of returning `pending`.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/lease-store.ts:155-156: recovery calls `reconcileLeaseIntent(deps, row.repo, row.ref)`. Lines 121-123 replay a release when `intent.before === confirmed?.tip`. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:227-229 excludes malformed records from equality confirmation, then returns `{ kind: "moved", tip: confirmed.tip }`. lease-store.ts:132-134 handles every moved result with `store.markLeaseLost(repo, ref); return "superseded";`. Lines 80-82 set confirmed state to lost and clear the intent.
verification.trigger: During release reconciliation, the ref moves from the confirmed tip to a malformed claim before CAS. The failed write returns moved; reconciliation incorrectly marks ownership lost and deletes the journal. This requires an unusual malformed-write race; the recovery API currently has no production callers.

findings.detail: The replay race exercises a higher-generation successor, but does not exercise a CAS failure whose newly observed tip is malformed or otherwise does not prove supersession. Consequently the unconditional `moved` handling clears the journal in those cases without a test failing.
findings.suggestion: Add replay races that move the ref to a malformed record and to a same-generation record from the same holder and run with different fields; assert pending and preservation of confirmed ownership and intent.
findings.failure_scenario: A malformed commit appears between the initial recovery read and the replay CAS. The existing race test remains green even though recovery incorrectly drops the pending release and marks ownership lost.

verification.evidence: test/lease-store.test.ts:420–421 injects only a valid successor: `if (r.step === "update") successors.push(f.gh.seed(successor));`. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:227–229 excludes malformed records from equality confirmation but then returns `return { kind: "moved", tip: confirmed.tip };`. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:132–134 handles every moved result with `store.markLeaseLost(repo, ref); return "superseded";`, without inspecting its record. At lines 83–85, markLeaseLost sets confirmed state to lost and clears the intent. The malformed guard at line 113 covers only the initial read. recoverLeases invokes reconciliation at lines 155–156; no production caller is wired yet.
verification.trigger: A confirmed held lease has a pending release. Recovery reads its confirmed tip, then a malformed commit replaces that tip before the replay CAS. The CAS fails and the client returns moved with the malformed tip; reconciliation incorrectly marks ownership lost and clears the pending release instead of retaining it for retry. The existing valid-successor race test misses this case.

findings.title: Preserve the intent when a replay races with a malformed tip
findings.detail: Every `moved` result is classified as superseded, even though the claim client can return `moved` with a malformed record. That clears the journal and marks confirmed ownership lost without establishing that a successor acquired the claim. The recovery table requires malformed records to leave the intent intact for a later retry.
findings.suggestion: Classify the moved tip using the same record validation and supersession rules as the initial read; retain the intent when the tip is malformed or does not establish supersession.
findings.failure_scenario: Recovery reads the confirmed tip and starts replaying a release. Before the compare-and-swap, the ref moves to a commit with a malformed claim record. The write returns `moved`, and recovery clears the final release intent instead of returning `pending`.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/lease-store.ts:122–126 sends the journaled release through `client.write(...)`. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:222–229 can return `"moved"` with a malformed tip after CAS failure. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:132–134 immediately invokes `markLeaseLost` rather than examining `result.tip.record`; lines 80–82 clear the intent and persist lost state.
verdicts.trigger: The ref becomes malformed after recovery reads the confirmed tip but before updateRefs. The failed replay returns moved, causing irreversible journal clearing and an unsupported lost classification. This unusual race affects the currently standalone recovery API.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:227–229 checks equality only when `confirmed.tip.record !== "malformed"`, otherwise returning `{ kind: "moved", tip: confirmed.tip }`. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:132–134 treats that result as superseded unconditionally. verdicts.trigger: A malformed claim message reaches the ref during a release replay's CAS window. Recovery discards the release journal despite the requirement to keep malformed observations pending. The trigger requires an unusual competing write, and no production recovery caller exists yet.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:225–229 returns moved for any changed tip whose record differs from the requested release, including malformed records and different checkpoints. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:132–134 unconditionally marks such replay results lost. Lines 80–82 show marking lost clears the intent.

verdicts.evidence: test/lease-store.test.ts:420-421 races replay only against a valid successor: `if (r.step === "update") successors.push(f.gh.seed(successor));`. The malformed-tip test at test/lease-store.test.ts:375 seeds corruption before reconciliation, not during replay. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:227-229 returns `return { kind: "moved", tip: confirmed.tip };` even when the new tip's record is malformed. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:132-134 then unconditionally executes `store.markLeaseLost(repo, ref); return "superseded";`, clearing the intent instead of retaining it.

findings.title: Release-intent replay bypasses lease-time validation
findings.detail: Reconciliation delegates a pending release to `reconcileLeaseIntent`, which can replay the release with `client.write` without a GitHub-time sample or `beforeSend` predicate. Both startup recovery and ordinary operations use that path, so an expired generation can mutate the claim after its lease window has closed.
findings.suggestion: Ensure release replay uses the same fresh time decision and send-time revalidation as other same-generation writes.
findings.failure_scenario: A release intent is journaled, the process stops before sending it, and recovery runs more than ten minutes later while the old tip remains current. Recovery writes the expired generation's release without checking whether it is renewable.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/leases.ts:65 calls `recoverLeases({ client, store })`; line 89 calls `reconcileLeaseIntent({ client, store, signal }, repo, ref)`. src/integrations/lease-store.ts:113-121 replays a release when the original confirmed tip remains current: `client.write(repo, ref, read.tip, intent.record, { signal, onCommit: ... })`, without time validation. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:206-208 only blocks when `opts.beforeSend?.()` returns false; the replay supplies no hook.

findings.title: A second moved result marks ownership lost without checking for supersession
findings.detail: After two moved outcomes that are not classified as same-holder writes, the code marks any confirmed row lost regardless of the moved tip's generation or identity. The invariant permits loss only when a moved record supersedes confirmed ownership. A malformed tip or an older-generation tip does not establish that the confirmed generation was superseded.
findings.suggestion: Classify the second moved tip against the confirmed generation and identity before marking the row lost; preserve ownership when supersession is not established.
findings.failure_scenario: A confirmed generation 2 write encounters two moved responses whose tips are malformed or generation 1. The manager marks generation 2 lost and calls `onLost` despite having no superseding record.

It does not require the second tip to supersede confirmed ownership. src/integrations/claim-ref.ts:229 can return `moved` for any differing tip. The manager currently has no production construction path; test/leases.test.ts:465 asserts its only source reference is its definition.
verification.trigger: A confirmed generation encounters two nonmatching moved responses, with an intervening fresh read permitting another write. findings.suggestion: Observe and report tick failures and isolate per-ref work so one failed operation does not prevent other leases from being processed.

findings.title: Treat browser availability as a positive setup outcome
findings.detail: The engine labels the browser available whenever a preview exists and no `browser_unavailable` event was recorded. That event only covers failures while constructing the MCP configuration; it does not establish that the MCP server or Chromium subsequently started successfully. A verifier that reports a genuine browser startup failure as blocked will therefore have its result converted to unclear and sent into an implementation feedback round.
findings.suggestion: Persist and use a positive, same-invocation browser setup outcome, and retain environment-block handling when successful setup cannot be established.
findings.failure_scenario: The preview starts and browserMcp produces a configuration, but the MCP server or Chromium fails to launch. No `browser_unavailable` warning is emitted, so a marked browser check reported blocked becomes unclear even though the browser was unavailable.

findings.title: A superseded unsent question set can never be published later
findings.detail: An unsent question effect is permanently marked done when its run temporarily stops waiting. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered question IDs, observe() sees the existing effect and never creates another publication. The same problem occurs after recovery establishes that a stale POST was not accepted. The run can therefore remain waiting indefinitely without its questions appearing on the issue.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a superseded effect with no confirmed publication from a completed publication, and allow a fresh eligible waiting episode to publish the set after any uncertain prior POST has been recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters waiting_input with question 42, but its pending comment has not been posted. The run temporarily changes to running, so reconciliation marks the effect done. It returns to waiting_input with question 42 still unanswered; subsequent polls and restarts never post the question.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366 polls `reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)`. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:355–358 sets `stale = pending.state === "recovering" || !eligible()` and then `if (stale && !pending.page) { save(effect, "done"); continue; }`. At :129, creation requires `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)`, including done effects. A normal restart requeues waiting runs (src/scheduler.ts:50–64); resumed execution sets `status: "running"` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:255) before returning to `waiting_input` (:964).
verification.trigger: In a managed repository, polling observes an unsent question checkpoint while its run is requeued or resuming after a deploy. It permanently closes the checkpoint; returning to waiting_input with the same unanswered IDs never publishes them, even after restart.

findings.title: Retired unsent question sets cannot be published if they become eligible again
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent question effect marks it done, and observe() will never create that effect again because it already exists. A temporary linkage or status change can therefore permanently suppress a question set that was never posted.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish superseded unsent effects from completed publications and allow the same set to be scheduled again when it becomes eligible.
findings.failure_scenario: A waiting run has a pending question publication, loses its issue link before the POST, and later regains the same link while the question remains open. The effect is done without a comment, so subsequent polls never publish that question set.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:169 includes prior pending question effects in work. Eligibility at :206–209 requires a matching current issue link. At :355–358, an ineligible effect without a POST recovery page is saved as `"done"`. At :129, `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)` prevents recreating that effect when the same link returns.
verification.trigger: A managed waiting run loses its issue link while its question publication is unsent, and reconciliation retires it. Restoring the same link and open-question set leaves the question permanently unpublished. Link removal and restoration is an unusual trigger.

findings.title: Privacy reinspection can close an uncertain POST without recovery
findings.detail: The pending body is reinspected before marker recovery, and any inspection failure immediately marks the effect done. For a checkpoint with page set, GitHub may already have accepted the POST; closing it without checking the marker violates the required recovery behavior and loses the recorded outcome.
findings.suggestion: Recover an uncertain POST using its independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing the effect, even when the stored body can no longer pass publication inspection. Keep any new POST suppressed if inspection fails.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a question comment but the response is lost. Before the next poll, private-string configuration becomes unreadable or changes to match the stored body. Reinspection fails, the checkpoint is marked done, and the accepted comment is never recovered.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:426–427 checkpoints `page: 1` immediately before POST. On the next reconciliation, :365 calls `checkBody(run, pending.body, ...)`; its catch at :366–369 saves `"done"` and continues. Marker recovery starts only afterwards at :371. `checkBody` loads current private strings through `inspection` (:76–85).
verification.trigger: GitHub accepts a POST whose response is lost, then private-string configuration becomes unreadable or newly matches the stored body. The next poll closes the uncertain checkpoint before looking for the accepted comment, permanently losing its recovery acknowledgement.

findings.title: Publication failures log exception output instead of a fixed code
findings.detail: The delivery catch passes the exception to logFailure, which logs its text. The subprocess error can include the full command and stderr, and credential redaction does not remove configured private strings. This violates the requirement that publication diagnostics contain fixed codes and never exception output. The new privacy tests inject fixed errors and do not exercise an exception containing withheld content.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed delivery-failure code without the exception text, and add a fake gh failure whose error contains protected question or reason text.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed GitHub POST or recovery request returns an error containing a configured private string or withheld field; that string is written to lifecycle diagnostics.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:442 passes the caught POST/recovery exception to `logFailure`. At :64 it logs `redactCredentials(`Issue lifecycle ...: ${String(error)}`)`, without private-string inspection or replacement by a fixed code. The production runner uses `githubSh` (src/integrations/github.ts:19–21), which delegates to `sh` (src/integrations/github-identity.ts:174). `sh` includes command arguments and stderr/stdout in its error (src/util/proc.ts:1210–1213).
verification.trigger: A failed GitHub POST or recovery read produces an exception containing a configured private string, including private content returned in an error response. Lifecycle diagnostics retain that content because credential redaction does not redact configured private strings.

findings.title: Store label-selection test passes without the changed SQL branch
findings.detail: The test asserts that waiting and running runs are selected, but issueLifecycleRuns already selects both statuses unconditionally. Reverting the waiting_input label comparison in the SQL therefore leaves those assertions passing, so the test does not independently verify the requested store label-selection change.
findings.suggestion: Add a focused assertion that fails when the store's desired-label comparison treats waiting_input as in-progress, or refactor the shared selection so its behavior can be tested directly.

verification.trigger: Revert only the SQL CASE to classify waiting_input as in-progress: both statuses remain unconditionally selected, and lifecycle reconciliation still applies the expected labels, so this test passes without detecting the regression.

findings.title: Upgrade fixture does not represent the immediately previous release
findings.detail: The upgrade test removes the lifecycle migration itself, then relies on migration seeding. The release being upgraded already has lifecycle checkpoints, so this does not exercise a waiting run with an existing observed checkpoint, completed started comment, and in-progress label.
findings.suggestion: Seed a database using the previous release's lifecycle schema and checkpoint state, reopen it with the current code, and assert that the outstanding question is published once.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression affecting only previously observed waiting runs with existing lifecycle effects is missed by the pre-lifecycle migration fixture.

verification.evidence: test/issue-queue.test.ts:1783 copies migrations with `filter: beforeLifecycle`; :40–41 defines that filter as excluding both `-issue-lifecycle.sql` and `-issue-lifecycle-history.sql`. The excluded migration creates `issue_lifecycle_effects` (src/db/migrations/20261024T224811-issue-lifecycle.sql:1). verification.trigger: Upgrade a waiting run already observed by the immediately previous release, with existing lifecycle checkpoints. A regression specific to those checkpoints would be missed because this upgrade fixture starts before the lifecycle table existed and only creates its checkpoints during migration.

findings.title: Superseded unsent sets can never be published if they become current again
findings.detail: The request requires publishing each unanswered question set and superseding unsent publications when waiting status or linkage changes. No comment was published, but the durable checkpoint treats the set as completed.

findings.failure_scenario: A question set is checkpointed but has not been posted; the run leaves `waiting_input` during identity lookup, then returns to `waiting_input` with the same unanswered question. The effect is `done`, so subsequent polls never publish it.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:405–408 awaits `postingLogin(repo, eligible)` and saves the effect as `"done"` if eligibility changed. Eligibility requires `current.status === "waiting_input"` (:209). Subsequent observation cannot recreate the same question effect because :129 requires `!effects.has(...)`. Normal resumed execution transitions through `status: "running"` (src/pipeline/engine.ts:255) before waiting again (:964).
verification.trigger: During identity lookup for an unsent question publication, a deploy or resume takes the run out of waiting_input. The checkpoint becomes done; returning to waiting_input with the same unanswered IDs never publishes the set. This is the same permanent-retirement defect as C1.

findings.title: Publication failures still log arbitrary exception output
findings.detail: The request says, "Diagnostics contain fixed codes, never withheld content or exception output." The new question publication and recovery path passes caught errors to `logFailure`, which logs `String(error)` with only credential redaction. Errors from GitHub calls or parsing can contain untrusted comment content or configured private strings, neither of which is guaranteed to be removed by credential redaction.
findings.suggestion: Log a fixed diagnostic code for publication and recovery failures without interpolating exception text.
findings.failure_scenario: A recovery response contains malformed JSON whose parser error includes a fragment containing a configured private string; the exception text is written to lifecycle diagnostics.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366 invokes `reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)` during polling. Recovery parses returned comment data at src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:383: `.parse(JSON.parse(String(await call(repo, [...])))`. Its outer catch passes the exception through at line 442: `logFailure(run, repo, number, error)`. Lines 62–64 log `redactCredentials(... ${String(error)})` without private-string inspection or a fixed diagnostic code. A Bun probe confirmed that malformed JSON errors include the offending identifier.
verification.trigger: A managed issue has an uncertain comment POST awaiting recovery. The recovery response is malformed JSON containing a configured private string in the parser's error excerpt. If that string is not a registered credential, the lifecycle logger emits it unchanged.

findings.title: Inspection failure closes an uncertain POST before marker recovery

This can happen after private-string configuration changes or a temporary inspection failure, leaving an accepted POST unrecorded as such.
findings.suggestion: Recover uncertain effects using the independently generated marker and checkpointed author before deciding whether a new publication body can be sent.

candidates.title: A failed body inspection closes an uncertain POST without recovery
candidates.detail: The request requires: “Recover an uncertain prior POST by its marker before closing its checkpoint.” An effect with a recovery page is instead marked done if reinspection of its stored body fails, before GitHub is searched. This loses the distinction between an accepted POST and one that never reached GitHub.
candidates.suggestion: Recover an issued POST using its independently generated marker and checkpointed identity before closing the checkpoint; apply publication checks before any subsequent POST.
candidates.failure_scenario: A question POST has an uncertain result, then the private-string configuration becomes unreadable before restart. Reconciliation marks the effect done without checking whether the comment exists, so an unaccepted question is never published.

candidates.title: Lifecycle delivery errors include exception output in diagnostics
candidates.detail: The request says “Diagnostics contain fixed codes, never withheld content or exception output.” The delivery and recovery catch passes the exception to `logFailure`, which logs its string after credential redaction only. GitHub or parsing errors can contain private strings or untrusted response text, and configured private strings are not redacted there.
candidates.suggestion: Log a fixed delivery or recovery failure code without including the exception text.
candidates.failure_scenario: A GitHub recovery response fails JSON parsing and its error message includes response text containing a configured private string; that text is written to the lifecycle log.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:426–427 checkpoints `page: 1` immediately before POST. On retry, lines 365–369 execute `body = checkBody(...)` and, on failure, `save(effect, "done"); ... continue;` before recovery begins at line 371: `if (pending.page)`. Lines 79–81 reload registered credentials and private strings during inspection.
verdicts.trigger: After GitHub accepts a POST whose response is lost, changed private strings or unavailable inspection causes the next poll to close the checkpoint without fetching comments or recording the accepted comment ID. The visible comment remains, but recovery bookkeeping is lost.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:209 requires `current.status === "waiting_input" && questionSet(current) === task.slice(10)`. Lines 355–358 retire an ineligible unsent effect with `if (stale && !pending.page) { save(effect, "done"); continue; }`. Lines 129–130 create a question publication only when `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)`, so restoring eligibility cannot recreate it.
verdicts.trigger: An unsent question set becomes ineligible while the run resumes or loses its issue link. If the same unanswered set later becomes eligible again, its done checkpoint permanently prevents publication. Returning to that exact prior state is an unusual trigger.

verdicts.evidence: Polling calls reconciliation at src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366. Publication errors reach `logFailure(run, repo, number, error)` at src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:442. Its implementation at lines 62–64 logs `${String(error)}` through only `redactCredentials`, without private-string inspection. src/util/proc.ts:1210–1213 constructs command errors containing `${cmd.join(" ")}\n${res.stderr.trim() || res.stdout.trim()}`.
verdicts.trigger: A failed GitHub publication or recovery command returns error output containing a configured private string that is not a registered credential. The lifecycle logger emits that private text instead of a fixed diagnostic code.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:206–208 makes eligibility depend on the current issue link. Lines 355–358 mark an unsent effect done when that link disappears. Restoring the link does not help: lines 129–130 require `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)`, while src/db/store.ts:1492 persists the existing effect through its conflict update.
verdicts.trigger: Remove an issue link while question A's publication is pending but unsent, poll to retire it, then restore the same link with A unanswered. The retained done effect prevents publication. This duplicates C2's linkage case and requires an unusual link reversal.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:85 defaults inspection through `checks = inspection(run)`, which calls `loadPrivateStrings` at line 81. Lines 363–369 catch inspection failure and immediately `save(effect, "done")`. The uncertain-POST recovery branch appears only afterward at line 371. src/gates/private.ts:138 throws `PrivateError("Cannot read private-strings.txt; publication blocked")` when loading fails.
verdicts.trigger: After an accepted question POST remains unacknowledged across restart, failure to load private strings closes its pending checkpoint before marker recovery. The accepted comment remains visible, but its ID is never recovered. This is C1's inspection-failure case.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366 calls `reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)`. Recovery parses the response with `.parse(JSON.parse(String(await call(...))))` (src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:383); its catch calls `logFailure(..., error)` (:442). That logger emits `redactCredentials(... ${String(error)})` (:64), without configured-private-string inspection. A Bun probe with an unquoted private identifier reproduced an exception containing that identifier.
verdicts.trigger: A pending comment enters recovery in a managed repository. Malformed response JSON contains a configured private string as an unexpected identifier; JSON.parse includes it in the exception, and lifecycle diagnostics expose it. Credential redaction does not cover private strings that are not registered credentials.

verdicts.evidence: Before POST, src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:426-428 checkpoints `page: 1`. On reconciliation, `body = checkBody(run, pending.body, ...)` (:365) executes before `if (pending.page)` recovery (:371). Inspection failure instead executes `save(effect, "done")` and `continue` (:367-369). Inspection reloads configured private strings (:81).
verdicts.trigger: GitHub accepts a POST whose response is lost, leaving an uncertain checkpoint. Before reconciliation, private configuration changes to reject the stored body or becomes unreadable. The checkpoint closes without recovering the accepted comment or recording its ID.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:383 parses recovery response JSON; exceptions reach `logFailure(run, repo, number, error)` (:442). The logger interpolates `${String(error)}` and applies only `redactCredentials` (:62-64). Bun's JSON.parse includes unexpected identifier text in its exception, as verified with a synthetic response.
verdicts.trigger: A malformed recovery response includes an unquoted identifier matching a configured private string. The parser exception carries that content into lifecycle logs without private-string filtering or replacement by a fixed diagnostic code.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:365 checks the stored body before recovery. Its failure handler does `save(effect, "done")` (:367) and `continue` (:369), bypassing the recovery block beginning at :371. `checkBody` defaults to `inspection(run)` (:85), which calls `loadPrivateStrings(...)` (:81).
verdicts.trigger: An accepted POST has a lost response and remains checkpointed for recovery. Private-string inspection subsequently becomes unavailable. Reconciliation permanently closes the uncertain effect without querying GitHub or recording the accepted comment.

verdicts.evidence: An ineligible unsent effect is permanently closed by `if (stale && !pending.page) { save(effect, "done"); continue; }` (src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:356-358). Question observation requires `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)` (:129), so a done effect prevents recreation; work selection includes only pending/recovering question effects (src/db/store.ts:1468). Pipeline resume writes `status: "running"` before awaiting recovery (src/pipeline/engine.ts:255-264), while `waitForAnswers` later restores `waiting_input` for unanswered questions (:962-964).
verdicts.trigger: An unsent question publication is checkpointed, then reconciliation sees the run temporarily outside waiting_input, such as during restart/resumption, and retires it. When the same unanswered set becomes current again, its existing done checkpoint prevents publication permanently.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366 invokes `reconcileIssueLifecycle(...)` during polling. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:426–427 checkpoints an issued POST with `save(effect, "pending", { body, login, page: 1 })`. On restart, lines 364–369 execute `body = checkBody(...)` and, on failure, `save(effect, "done")` followed by `continue`, before marker recovery at line 371. `checkBody` loads private strings through `inspection` (lines 76–85); src/gates/private.ts:138 throws `PrivateError("Cannot read private-strings.txt; publication blocked")` on inspection failure. Existing effects are skipped by `if (effects.has(effect)) continue` (lifecycle line 138).
verdicts.trigger: An issue-linked question POST fails ambiguously, leaving page=1, and private-string inspection becomes unavailable before reconciliation resumes. The checkpoint is permanently closed without marker recovery. Restoring inspection does not retry recovery or publish an unaccepted question set.

verdicts.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:366 calls lifecycle reconciliation during polling. Recovery parses GitHub response text using `.parse(JSON.parse(String(await call(...))))` at src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:383. Parsing exceptions reach `logFailure(run, repo, number, error)` at line 442. That helper logs `redactCredentials(`Issue lifecycle ${repo}#${number} run ${run.id}: ${String(error)}`)` at lines 62–64, without configured-private-string inspection. A read-only Bun probe confirmed that parsing `privatehost` produces `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "privatehost"`.
verdicts.trigger: A recovery response contains malformed JSON whose unexpected token includes a configured private string that is not a registered credential. Bun includes the token in its parsing exception, and lifecycle logging exposes it instead of emitting a fixed diagnostic code.

verdicts.evidence: test/issue-queue.test.ts:1844–1849 tests lost-response recovery with `await f.poll(); ... f.reopen(); ... await f.poll();` but never changes privacy configuration. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:81 loads `loadPrivateStrings(...)`; line 85 invokes inspection by default in `checkBody`. Lines 365–369 call `checkBody` and on failure execute `save(effect, "done"); ... continue;` before the recovery GET at line 383. src/gates/private.ts:138 throws `new PrivateError("Cannot read private-strings.txt; publication blocked")` on inspection failure.
verdicts.trigger: A managed, issue-linked waiting run has a question POST accepted, but its response is lost, leaving page:1 pending recovery. Before reopening, private-strings.txt becomes unreadable. The next reconciliation marks the effect done without querying GitHub or recording the accepted comment ID. Existing tests cover recovery and privacy changes separately, leaving this interaction undetected.
